Preface

Modern statistical learning and artificial intelligence increasingly rely on a common mechanism being reused across many local problems. Amortized inference replaces repeated optimization by one inference network; multitask systems share representations or parameters; sequential decision systems compress growing histories into finite states; scientific learning pipelines seek common labels or comparable representations across samples, batches, or conditions. Reuse creates efficiency, but it also creates a structural question that is distinct from ordinary finite-sample error and numerical optimization.

Suppose each input xx has a locally optimal object ax⋆a_{x}^{\star}. Pointwise solvability asks only

∀x​∃ax⋆.\forall x\;\exists a_{x}^{\star}.

Deployment asks for one admissible rule

∃A∈𝔄​∀x,A⁡(x)≈ax⋆,\exists A\in\mathfrak{A}\;\forall x,\qquad A(x)\approx a_{x}^{\star},

where 𝔄\mathfrak{A} may enforce shared parameters, continuity, finite memory, a fixed output type, communication limits, or a computation budget. The first statement does not imply the second. When the implication fails, more data, longer training, or greater width inside the same deployment contract need not remove the resulting loss; the required intervention may instead be a different representation, sharing pattern, memory state, output semantics, or resource allocation.

The phenomenon is not new. Approximation theory, amortized inference, multitask learning, representation learning, control, and topology all study nearby failures. The book therefore makes a narrower claim. Once a local statistical or optimization problem has fixed its oracle objects, can the loss caused specifically by a shared deployment contract be separated from local model approximation, finite-sample generalization, and implementation error? Can that loss be expressed in the scale generated by the original objective rather than in a convenient post hoc distance?

Three levels must be kept distinct. Local solvability asks whether the pointwise oracle is well defined and what it costs to deviate from it. Global realizability asks whether one rule satisfying the declared deployment contract can realize the collection of local optima simultaneously. Finite-sample certifiability asks whether the available data are sufficient to distinguish realizability, nonrealizability, and an unresolved case with stated error control. None of these levels subsumes the others: a population obstruction need not be identifiable from finite data, and statistical unresolvedness does not imply that the population structure is absent.

The technical starting point is elimination. If an auxiliary object aa is optimized out of a local objective,

J⁡(x)=infaHx​(a),J(x)=\inf_{a}H_{x}(a),

then

𝖣x​(a)=Hx​(a)−J⁡(x)≥0\mathsf{D}_{x}(a)=H_{x}(a)-J(x)\geq 0

is the native defect: the exact excess objective incurred by deploying aa rather than a local optimum. This quantity is inherited from the likelihood, divergence, proper score, Bellman objective, free energy, or other declared criterion; it is not an arbitrary distance chosen after the fact. For a deployment class 𝔄\mathfrak{A} and population law PP,

infA∈𝔄𝔼P​DX​{A⁡(X)}\inf_{A\in\mathfrak{A}}\mathbb{E}_{P}D_{X}\{A(X)\}

is the architecture obstruction: the smallest native population risk left by the deployment contract after the local oracle has been fixed.

The book assembles an audit workflow rather than a new universal approximation or representation theory. Its mathematical ingredients come from several established traditions, including convex duality, approximation and representation theory, information theory, control, topology, partial identification, and statistical learning. The proposed contribution is to type their assumptions and conclusions on a common native-loss interface and to expose the additional assumptions needed when moving from one interface to the next. The ordering is methodological, not a theorem saying that a native defect implies an architecture obstruction, or that an obstruction implies a successful repair.

The resulting workflow is deliberately falsifiable. It derives a native loss, audits a declared deployment contract, constructs an appropriate population or statistical certificate, and proposes a mechanism-matched intervention. A stronger architecture-choice claim additionally requires evidence of saturation within the fixed contract, independent validation, and parameter-, compute-, and selection-matched negative controls. The empirical studies in this edition illustrate only parts of that workflow; none completes a general certificate-saturation-repair validation chain.

This Version closes one architecture-specific mathematical chain for full-column-rank nonnegative sparse inference: strict active-set neighborhoods yield a computable one-pass native-loss floor, and the declared proximal repair has an explicit sufficient crossing depth. The sealed diabetes case also closes a separate two-step, patient-average, equal-information and equal-compute decision. These two advances are deliberately not conflated: the theorem-alignment calculation is post-confirmation, its priority remains independently unresolved, and no general architecture-choice theory or external replication is claimed.

This scope imposes important limits. Architecture obstruction is not a new name for generic approximation error. A positive worst-case topological cost does not automatically imply a positive average risk. A deterministic population obstruction is not automatically identifiable from finite data. A native defect need not be visible to the final scientific endpoint. And a structural repair does not by itself guarantee held-out improvement. Each transition requires its own theorem or empirical validation.

The recurring examples—variational inference and EM, graph-indexed distribution learning, shared policies and finite memory, roots and eigenvectors, resource-limited representations, and multi-sample population alignment—serve one purpose: to test whether the same sequence of questions can be answered across different mathematical objects. What is locally optimal? What must be reused globally? Which deployment constraint creates the obstruction? What is the minimal structural change that removes it? Can finite data support that diagnosis?

The intended contribution is therefore a typed, native-loss, audit-oriented synthesis complementary to existing learning theory. It organizes results about when local optima exist, when a declared shared contract can realize them, how particular lower bounds are expressed in objective units, and what additional statistical and experimental evidence would be needed before an architecture intervention is justified. It does not claim that these questions constitute a wholly new approximation or representation theory.

Notation and Standing Conventions

Orientation of asymmetric divergences

Throughout the book,

DΦ(a∥b)=Φ(a)−Φ(b)−⟨∇Φ(b),a−b⟩,D_{\Phi}(a\|b)=\Phi(a)-\Phi(b)-\langle\nabla\Phi(b),a-b\rangle,

so the first argument is the evaluation point and the second is the tangent or reference point. Likewise,

KL(Q∥P)=∫log(d​Qd​P)dQ\operatorname{KL}(Q\|P)=\int\log\!\left(\frac{\,\mathrm{d}Q}{\,\mathrm{d}P}\right)\,\mathrm{d}Q

when Q≪PQ\ll P, and KL(Q∥P)=+∞\operatorname{KL}(Q\|P)=+\infty otherwise. The first argument is the integration law and the second the reference; conditioning and pushforward preserve this order. Native defects therefore place the trial or deployed object first and the oracle second.

Standing distinctions

The following distinctions are maintained throughout.

  • •

    A zero infimum does not imply that an exact minimizer or global section is attained.

  • •

    Uniform, average, and task-weighted risks are different contracts and are never interchanged without an explicit theorem.

  • •

    Local oracle error, architecture obstruction, generalization error, and implementation error are recorded separately unless an exact identity combines them.

  • •

    Point-valued, set-valued, quotient-valued, projector-valued, and distribution-valued outputs are different semantic contracts.

  • •

    Deterministic obstruction, statistical impossibility, posterior credibility, and computational intractability are different claims.

  • •

    The independent statistical unit is the declared sampling unit, not automatically an individual cell, token, edge, or repeated measurement.

Infima and measurability

Unless stated otherwise, all infima are over nonempty declared classes. Measurability, lower semicontinuity, compactness, coercivity, or closure assumptions needed for attainment are stated locally rather than imposed globally. When only approximation is required, the book works with infima and ε\varepsilon-optimal selections.

Part I The Structural Realizability Problem
Modern learning systems reuse representations, parameterizations, memories, and output interfaces across many local problems. The first question is therefore not only whether local optima exist, but whether one declared deployment system can realize them simultaneously.

Chapter 1 Structural Realizability under Shared Deployment

1.1 Reuse changes the learning problem

Many modern learning systems solve a family of local problems and then reuse a single mechanism across them. Let

ax⋆∈arg​mina∈𝖠x⁡Hx​(a)a_{x}^{\star}\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{a\in\mathsf{A}_{x}}H_{x}(a)

denote a local posterior, conditional policy, spectral object, population identity, or inner optimization state. A pointwise procedure asks only that each local problem be solvable. Deployment asks for one field

A:𝖷⟶⨆x∈𝖷𝖠x,A⁡(x)∈𝖠x,A:\mathsf{X}\longrightarrow\bigsqcup_{x\in\mathsf{X}}\mathsf{A}_{x},\qquad A(x)\in\mathsf{A}_{x},

subject to a contract such as continuity, Lipschitz regularity, finite memory, shared parameters, a fixed output type, bounded communication, or a prescribed computation graph.

The quantifiers are different:

∀x​∃ax⋆⇏∃A∈𝔄​∀x,A⁡(x)=ax⋆.\forall x\;\exists a_{x}^{\star}\qquad\not\Rightarrow\qquad\exists A\in\mathfrak{A}\;\forall x,\ A(x)=a_{x}^{\star}.

The right-hand statement is a global realizability problem. Its failure is structural when it persists after the local oracles have been fixed and after optimization within the declared deployment class has been completed.

A two-point example isolates the issue. Let X∈{0,1}X\in\{0,1\} be equiprobable and let the native loss be 𝖣x​(a)=(a−x)2\mathsf{D}_{x}(a)=(a-x)^{2}. Each local optimum is exact: a⋆​(x)=xa^{\star}(x)=x. If deployment is restricted to constant rules A⁡(x)≡cA(x)\equiv c, then

infc𝔼​(c−X)2=infc12​{c2+(c−1)2}=14.\inf_{c}\mathbb{E}(c-X)^{2}=\inf_{c}\frac{1}{2}\{c^{2}+(c-1)^{2}\}=\frac{1}{4}.

No reparameterization of the same constant-output contract removes this 1/41/4. The obstruction disappears only when the deployment rule is allowed to depend on xx.

The same pattern appears in less trivial forms. Amortized inference asks one encoder to reproduce many instancewise variational optima. Sequential decision systems reuse parameters or a compressed memory state across many histories. Spectral procedures may need one continuous representative of an eigenspace whose oriented eigenvector changes sign around a loop. The mechanisms differ, but the quantifier mismatch is the same: local solvability does not determine global realizability under reuse.

1.2 Three levels: solvability, realizability, and certifiability

The book separates three questions that are often mixed together.

  1. 1.

    Local solvability. For each input, is the local oracle well defined, and what excess objective is paid by deviating from it?

  2. 2.

    Global realizability. Does one rule satisfying the declared representation, sharing, memory, regularity, and resource constraints realize the local oracle family simultaneously?

  3. 3.

    Finite-sample certifiability. When the local oracles and population structure must themselves be estimated, do the available data support a statistically valid conclusion of realizability, nonrealizability, or unresolvedness?

These levels do not substitute for one another. A genuine population obstruction need not be identifiable at a realistic sample size. Conversely, an unresolved statistical certificate does not imply that the obstruction is absent. If the local model itself is misspecified, then a perfectly realizable deployment can still be scientifically inadequate.

This separation determines the intervention. Model misspecification calls for a richer local model; finite-sample ambiguity calls for more informative data or a different experiment; implementation error calls for a better solver. Structural nonrealizability calls instead for a change in the deployment contract—for example a quotient representation, an atlas, additional memory, a different sharing pattern, or a larger resource budget.

Position relative to neighboring theory.

The book does not claim priority for the observation that sharing can create suboptimality. The amortization gap has been separated from variational-family approximation since early work on VAEs (Cremer et al., 2018), and recent results characterize when amortized variational inference can attain its instancewise optimum (Margossian and Blei, 2024). Multitask representation learning studies benefits and limits of shared features (Li et al., 2025), while finite-memory RL quantifies errors caused by compressed histories (Eberhard et al., 2025). Elimination geometry makes a more specific claim: once the local oracle and its native excess objective are fixed, it seeks objective-denominated lower bounds, finite-data certificates, and mechanism-specific repairs for the remaining deployment constraint.

The architecture-specific candidate in Chapter 19 is correspondingly narrower. O’Neill et al. (2025) already establish a global amortisation gap for a one-layer linear–nonlinear sparse autoencoder and study inference-time optimization. This book does not reclaim that conclusion. It asks whether two strict KKT neighborhoods in one fitted nonnegative sparse problem expose incompatible oracle Jacobian rows, converts that conflict into a quantitative native-loss floor for the declared one-pass class, and computes a sufficient proximal repair depth. Its exact priority remains unresolved and is recorded as such in Appendix G.

1.3 Native risk and architecture obstruction

A structural lower bound is useful only if it is measured in a loss scale connected to the original problem. If an auxiliary object aa is eliminated from

J⁡(x)=infa∈𝖠xHx​(a),J(x)=\inf_{a\in\mathsf{A}_{x}}H_{x}(a),

then the native defect is

𝖣x​(a)=Hx​(a)−J⁡(x)≥0.\mathsf{D}_{x}(a)=H_{x}(a)-J(x)\geq 0.

It is an exact excess objective, not a post hoc parameter distance. The population risk of a deployment AA is

ℒP​(A)=𝔼P​𝖣X​{A⁡(X)},\mathcal{L}_{P}(A)=\mathbb{E}_{P}\mathsf{D}_{X}\{A(X)\},

and the architecture obstruction is

𝔒P​(𝔄)=infA∈𝔄ℒP​(A).\mathfrak{O}_{P}(\mathfrak{A})=\inf_{A\in\mathfrak{A}}\mathcal{L}_{P}(A).

When 𝔒P​(𝔄)>0\mathfrak{O}_{P}(\mathfrak{A})>0, the declared deployment class has a strictly positive population floor relative to the already fixed local oracle family.

This is the book’s organizing interface with generic expressivity and approximation theory. In settings with a unique oracle and a norm-equivalent defect, the resulting obstruction may reduce to an ordinary approximation error. The useful additional discipline is then not a new mathematical mechanism, but the requirement that the local target, loss scale, deployment contract, and population quantifier remain explicit.

1.4 Mission and falsifiable consequences

The purpose of this book is to provide a common audit language for identifying, quantifying, and testing claims of structural nonrealizability under shared deployment. The chapters that follow ask five questions in a recommended workflow order:

  1. 1.

    Which native loss scale is generated by the original elimination?

  2. 2.

    Are the local defect descriptions and lifted representations structurally valid?

  3. 3.

    What regular, coordination, singular, or resource obstruction is forced by the deployment contract?

  4. 4.

    Can finite data certify the relevant structural conclusion, and can the declared downstream task observe it?

  5. 5.

    Which minimal structural intervention is predicted to remove the obstruction, and does that intervention improve independent held-out risk?

A structural explanation should be falsifiable. A performance plateau alone is not evidence of architecture obstruction: misspecification, optimization failure, data scarcity, regularization, and metric ceilings can produce the same curve. A stronger empirical signature has several parts. First, a structural certificate predicts a nonzero floor under a fixed deployment contract. Second, capacity or compute increases that preserve that contract do not remove the diagnosed gap. Third, a mechanism-matched change of representation, sharing, memory, or output semantics reduces the native defect. Finally, the gain survives independent validation and matched controls. Failure of any step weakens the structural interpretation.

The book therefore does not propose a replacement for approximation, generalization, optimization, information theory, or representation learning. It develops a complementary structural question: once local optima are defined, what can a shared learning system coherently realize, what native risk is unavoidable when it cannot, and what evidence justifies changing the deployment contract?

Chapter 2 Certified Elimination Systems

2.1 The primitive interface

The theory begins with a family of inner optimization problems. Let 𝖷\mathsf{X} be an instance space. Let π:ℰ→𝖷\pi:\mathcal{E}\to\mathsf{X} be a fibered auxiliary space with fiber 𝖠x=π−1​(x)\mathsf{A}_{x}=\pi^{-1}(x). A lifted objective is a function

H:ℰ→ℝ∪{+∞},Hx​(a)=H⁡(x,a).H:\mathcal{E}\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\},\qquad H_{x}(a)=H(x,a).
Definition 2.1 (Certified elimination).

A certified elimination is a triple (H,J,𝖣)(H,J,\mathsf{D}) satisfying

J⁡(x)=infa∈𝖠xHx​(a)∈ℝ,𝖣x​(a)=Hx​(a)−J⁡(x)∈[0,+∞].J(x)=\inf_{a\in\mathsf{A}_{x}}H_{x}(a)\in\mathbb{R},\qquad\mathsf{D}_{x}(a)=H_{x}(a)-J(x)\in[0,+\infty].

Thus every auxiliary fiber is nonempty and its lifted objective is proper and bounded below by a finite value; attainment is not required. These conditions make the residual well defined even when a trial state has infinite lifted cost. The oracle fiber is

𝒪⁡(x)={a∈𝖠x:𝖣x​(a)=0}.\mathcal{O}(x)=\{a\in\mathsf{A}_{x}:\mathsf{D}_{x}(a)=0\}.

The adjective certified refers to the exact objective identity. A distance from aa to a chosen optimizer may still be useful, but it is not a certificate until a proved exchange inequality links that distance to Hx​(a)−J​(x)H_{x}(a)-J(x).

Example 2.2 (Quadratic profiling).

Let Hx​(a)=12​‖a−m⁡(x)‖2+c⁡(x)H_{x}(a)=\frac{1}{2}\|a-m(x)\|^{2}+c(x). Then J⁡(x)=c⁡(x)J(x)=c(x), 𝒪⁡(x)={m⁡(x)}\mathcal{O}(x)=\{m(x)\}, and

𝖣x​(a)=12​‖a−m⁡(x)‖2.\mathsf{D}_{x}(a)=\frac{1}{2}\|a-m(x)\|^{2}.

Here Euclidean distance and native defect coincide up to scale.

Example 2.3 (Nonidentifiable mixture).

Suppose Hx​(a)H_{x}(a) is invariant under a permutation group GG. The oracle fiber is an orbit rather than a point. Parameter distance between two representatives may be positive while the native defect is zero. The correct geometry lives on a quotient or an unordered output space.

2.2 A complete learning contract

A learning system is not determined by HH alone. We use the following package.

Definition 2.4 (Certified learning system).

A certified learning system is

𝔈=(𝖷,P,ℰ,H,J,𝖣,𝔄,ℛ,𝔗,𝒫),\mathfrak{E}=(\mathsf{X},P,\mathcal{E},H,J,\mathsf{D},\mathfrak{A},\mathcal{R},\mathfrak{T},\mathcal{P}),

where:

  • •

    (𝖷,P)(\mathsf{X},P) is the population probability space;

  • •

    ℰ→𝖷\mathcal{E}\to\mathsf{X} is the auxiliary fibration;

  • •

    (H,J,𝖣)(H,J,\mathsf{D}) is a certified elimination;

  • •

    𝔄\mathfrak{A} is a class of PP-measurable sections AA of ℰ→𝖷\mathcal{E}\to\mathsf{X} for which x↦𝖣x​{A⁡(x)}x\mapsto\mathsf{D}_{x}\{A(x)\} is measurable;

  • •

    ℛ\mathcal{R} is the representation and resource grammar;

  • •

    𝔗\mathfrak{T} is the legal downstream task/context contract;

  • •

    𝒫\mathcal{P} is the statistical experiment generating observed data.

The components play different roles: the objective determines the defect; deployment determines the architecture class; the task contract determines operational visibility; and the statistical experiment determines what can be certified.

2.3 Pointwise, population, and uniform risk functionals

For a deployed field A∈𝔄A\in\mathfrak{A}, define pointwise and population defects

𝖣A​(x)=𝖣x​{A⁡(x)},ℒP​(A)=𝔼P​𝖣A​(X).\mathsf{D}_{A}(x)=\mathsf{D}_{x}\{A(x)\},\qquad\mathcal{L}_{P}(A)=\mathbb{E}_{P}\mathsf{D}_{A}(X).

The expectation is allowed to be extended-valued. For the finite population decomposition below, assume that 𝔄\mathfrak{A} is nonempty and contains at least one field of finite population defect, and take AA itself to have finite population defect. Then the architecture obstruction is finite:

𝔒P​(𝔄)=infA∈𝔄ℒP​(A).\mathfrak{O}_{P}(\mathfrak{A})=\inf_{A\in\mathfrak{A}}\mathcal{L}_{P}(A).

Every deployed field satisfies the exact architecture decomposition

ℒP​(A)=𝔒P​(𝔄)+ΔPimpl​(A,𝔄),\mathcal{L}_{P}(A)=\mathfrak{O}_{P}(\mathfrak{A})+\Delta^{\mathrm{impl}}_{P}(A;\mathfrak{A}),

where

ΔPimpl​(A,𝔄)=ℒP​(A)−𝔒P​(𝔄)≥0.\Delta^{\mathrm{impl}}_{P}(A;\mathfrak{A})=\mathcal{L}_{P}(A)-\mathfrak{O}_{P}(\mathfrak{A})\geq 0.

The identity is simple, but conceptually decisive. It separates an irreducible class-level floor from failure to reach the class optimum.

Uniform deployment uses

ℒ∞​(A)=supx∈𝖷𝖣A​(x),𝔒∞​(𝔄)=infA∈𝔄ℒ∞​(A).\mathcal{L}_{\infty}(A)=\sup_{x\in\mathsf{X}}\mathsf{D}_{A}(x),\qquad\mathfrak{O}_{\infty}(\mathfrak{A})=\inf_{A\in\mathfrak{A}}\mathcal{L}_{\infty}(A).

Uniform and average risks can differ sharply. A continuous field may be forced to incur a fixed worst-case tax at a topological seam while concentrating that seam on a set of arbitrarily small PP-mass.

2.4 Regular and singular oracle geometry

The oracle incidence set

𝒪={(x,a):a∈𝒪⁡(x)}⊆ℰ\mathcal{O}=\{(x,a):a\in\mathcal{O}(x)\}\subseteq\mathcal{E}

can have several geometries.

Unique regular oracle.

Each fiber contains one oracle a⋆​(x)a^{\star}(x) and the map x↦a⋆​(x)x\mapsto a^{\star}(x) is regular. Obstruction then comes from limited variation, resources, or decoder capacity.

Separated finite cover.

Each fiber contains finitely many separated branches. Local branches form a covering space; a global labeled section may fail because of monodromy.

Singular oracle family.

Branches collide, disappear, or change multiplicity. The incidence map is stratified rather than a covering. Strong convexity and uniform branch separation fail, and the defect itself must price the singularity.

Set- or distribution-valued oracle.

The natural oracle object may be an orbit, a projector, an unordered set, or a law. A point-valued representation can introduce an artificial obstruction.

2.5 Defect fibrations and fine-to-coarse maps

Suppose ρ:ℰ→ℬ\rho:\mathcal{E}\to\mathcal{B} maps a fine auxiliary object to a coarse one. A useful elimination hierarchy has an exact decomposition

𝖣xℰ​(e)=𝖣xℬ​{ρ⁡(e)}+δx​(e),δx​(e)≥0.\mathsf{D}_{x}^{\mathcal{E}}(e)=\mathsf{D}_{x}^{\mathcal{B}}\{\rho(e)\}+\delta_{x}(e),\qquad\delta_{x}(e)\geq 0.

The coarse defect measures the price of choosing the wrong coarse state; the vertical term measures the price of realizing that coarse state in the fine fiber.

For a restricted fine architecture 𝔄ℰ\mathfrak{A}_{\mathcal{E}}, define the fiber realization tax

Ψx(b)=inf{δx(e):e∈𝔄ℰ(x),ρ(e)=b}.\Psi_{x}(b)=\inf\{\delta_{x}(e):e\in\mathfrak{A}_{\mathcal{E}}(x),\ \rho(e)=b\}.

Then the fine obstruction takes the infimal form

𝔒ℰ=infb{𝖣ℬ​(b)+Ψ⁡(b)}.\mathfrak{O}^{\mathcal{E}}=\inf_{b}\bigl\{\mathsf{D}^{\mathcal{B}}(b)+\Psi(b)\bigr\}.

This is the basic obstruction tower. It is a Bellman or min-plus recursion over representation levels.

2.6 Common loss scales, attainment, and approximation

A central discipline of elimination geometry is that different nonnegative quantities are not added merely because they appear in the same problem.

For example, KL defect, topological degree, parameter distance, runtime, and task regret have different units and semantics. A theorem may exchange one for another under strong convexity, data processing, an exposure gate, or a complexity model. Without that theorem, the quantities should be reported separately.

Attainment and approximation.

A zero architecture obstruction has several interpretations.

  • •

    If the infimum is attained and equals zero, the architecture contains an exact oracle section.

  • •

    If the infimum is zero but unattained, the architecture approximates the oracle arbitrarily well in the declared risk.

  • •

    If the average obstruction is zero but the uniform obstruction is positive, the architecture can squeeze failure into a vanishing seam but cannot remove it everywhere.

Compactness, lower semicontinuity, coercivity, or finite-dimensional closure are needed for attainment. The notation min\min must not replace inf\inf without such a theorem.

Exercise 2.5.

For a finite instance space and finite auxiliary fibers, prove that the population architecture obstruction is attained for every nonempty architecture class.

Chapter 3 A Four-Component Decomposition of Population Risk

The same excess risk can have different causes, and those causes call for different interventions. The local statistical model may be inadequate; a shared deployment contract may fail to realize the local oracle family; finite data may not identify a good deployment; or the numerical procedure may not have reached the best member of the declared class. The decomposition below separates these mechanisms by their reference objects before any probability bound is applied.

3.1 Reference risks and the four components

Let R⋆R^{\star} be the scientifically relevant population optimum. Let RoracleR_{\rm oracle} be the population risk attained by the local oracle family generated by the declared local model or variational approximation. Let 𝔄\mathfrak{A} be the deployment class, and let A^\widehat{A} be the learned deployment. Define

Δmodel=Roracle−R⋆,Δarch=infA∈𝔄R⁡(A)−Roracle,\Delta^{\mathrm{model}}=R_{\rm oracle}-R^{\star},\qquad\Delta^{\mathrm{arch}}=\inf_{A\in\mathfrak{A}}R(A)-R_{\rm oracle},

and

Δnopt=R^n​(A^)−infA∈𝔄R^n​(A).\Delta^{\mathrm{opt}}_{n}=\widehat{R}_{n}(\widehat{A})-\inf_{A\in\mathfrak{A}}\widehat{R}_{n}(A).

For a reference deployment A†∈𝔄A^{\dagger}\in\mathfrak{A}, define

ρ^n​(A†)=R^n​(A†)−infA∈𝔄R^n​(A)\widehat{\rho}_{n}(A^{\dagger})=\widehat{R}_{n}(A^{\dagger})-\inf_{A\in\mathfrak{A}}\widehat{R}_{n}(A)

and

ρ⁡(A†)=R⁡(A†)−infA∈𝔄R⁡(A).\rho(A^{\dagger})=R(A^{\dagger})-\inf_{A\in\mathfrak{A}}R(A).

The four principal components have different meanings.

  • •

    Δmodel\Delta^{\mathrm{model}} is the model approximation component: it compares the best local oracle family with the scientific target.

  • •

    Δarch\Delta^{\mathrm{arch}} is the architecture obstruction component: after the local oracle has been fixed, it measures the smallest population loss forced by the deployment contract.

  • •

    The population–empirical deviations at A^\widehat{A} and a comparator form the generalization component.

  • •

    Δnopt\Delta^{\mathrm{opt}}_{n} is the implementation component: it measures empirical suboptimality within the declared deployment class.

All components that are added quantitatively must refer to a common risk scale, or be connected by an explicit exchange theorem. A KL defect, a parameter distance, a topological degree, a runtime, and a scientific utility difference are not automatically commensurable.

Proposition 3.1 (Exact four-component risk identity).

For any reference A†∈𝔄A^{\dagger}\in\mathfrak{A},

R⁡(A^)−R⋆=\displaystyle R(\widehat{A})-R^{\star}={} Δmodel+Δarch\displaystyle\Delta^{\mathrm{model}}+\Delta^{\mathrm{arch}}
+[R⁡(A^)−R^n​(A^)+R^n​(A†)−R⁡(A†)]\displaystyle+\Bigl[R(\widehat{A})-\widehat{R}_{n}(\widehat{A})+\widehat{R}_{n}(A^{\dagger})-R(A^{\dagger})\Bigr]
+Δnopt+ρ⁡(A†)−ρ^n​(A†).\displaystyle+\Delta^{\mathrm{opt}}_{n}+\rho(A^{\dagger})-\widehat{\rho}_{n}(A^{\dagger}).

If A†A^{\dagger} is a population minimizer, then ρ⁡(A†)=0\rho(A^{\dagger})=0; if it is an empirical minimizer, then ρ^n​(A†)=0\widehat{\rho}_{n}(A^{\dagger})=0.

When the population risk has the native form

R⁡(A)=Roracle+𝔼​𝖣X​{A⁡(X)},R(A)=R_{\rm oracle}+\mathbb{E}\mathsf{D}_{X}\{A(X)\},

the second component becomes exactly

Δarch=infA∈𝔄𝔼​𝖣X​{A⁡(X)}=𝔒P​(𝔄).\Delta^{\mathrm{arch}}=\inf_{A\in\mathfrak{A}}\mathbb{E}\mathsf{D}_{X}\{A(X)\}=\mathfrak{O}_{P}(\mathfrak{A}).

This is the principal interface between elimination geometry and statistical learning: generic approximation relative to R⋆R^{\star} is refined into local model inadequacy and structural nonrealizability under shared deployment.

In amortized variational inference, the distinction is especially simple. Fix the decoder and local variational family and take Hx=−ELBOxH_{x}=-\operatorname{ELBO}_{x}. Then 𝖣x\mathsf{D}_{x} is the per-datum amortization gap of Cremer et al. (2018), while Δarch\Delta^{\mathrm{arch}} is the smallest population-averaged amortization gap attainable by the declared encoder class—not the gap of a particular fitted encoder. For a deployed encoder AA, the population-averaged amortization gap is therefore the sum of this class-level floor and a within-class residual, Δarch+ΔPimpl​(A,𝔄)\Delta^{\mathrm{arch}}+\Delta^{\mathrm{impl}}_{P}(A;\mathfrak{A}). Margossian and Blei (2024) characterize when the first term can vanish under the sharing rule they study: one deterministic inference function must produce all local variational parameters.

3.2 A high-probability learning bound

Assume that, with probability at least 1−δ1-\delta,

supA∈𝔄|R⁡(A)−R^n​(A)|≤εn​(δ),\sup_{A\in\mathfrak{A}}|R(A)-\widehat{R}_{n}(A)|\leq\varepsilon_{n}(\delta),

and that the training algorithm satisfies

R^n​(A^)≤infA∈𝔄R^n​(A)+ηn.\widehat{R}_{n}(\widehat{A})\leq\inf_{A\in\mathfrak{A}}\widehat{R}_{n}(A)+\eta_{n}.
Theorem 3.2 (Four-component certified learning bound).

On the uniform generalization event,

Δmodel+Δarch≤R⁡(A^)−R⋆≤Δmodel+Δarch+2​εn​(δ)+ηn.\Delta^{\mathrm{model}}+\Delta^{\mathrm{arch}}\leq R(\widehat{A})-R^{\star}\leq\Delta^{\mathrm{model}}+\Delta^{\mathrm{arch}}+2\varepsilon_{n}(\delta)+\eta_{n}.

3.3 Structural meaning and mechanism coupling

The decomposition is exact, but its mechanisms are not independent. Enlarging a local variational family can reduce Δmodel\Delta^{\mathrm{model}} while producing a multibranch oracle family that increases Δarch\Delta^{\mathrm{arch}}. A data-driven atlas makes the deployment class itself random. Test-time computation can reduce implementation error while also enlarging the effective deployment class. A nonconvex optimizer may reach only a subset of a nominal architecture class.

The correct use of the decomposition is therefore diagnostic, not merely algebraic. The order of analysis is:

local oracle⟶architecture floor⟶finite-sample control⟶implementation residual.\text{local oracle}\longrightarrow\text{architecture floor}\longrightarrow\text{finite-sample control}\longrightarrow\text{implementation residual}.

The intervention then follows the dominant mechanism.

Component Typical cause First intervention to examine
Model approximation local family omits relevant structure change the local model or scientific target
Architecture obstruction representation, sharing, memory, regularity, or resource restriction change the deployment contract
Generalization limited independent data or data-dependent selection collect information or control statistical complexity
Implementation incomplete training or numerical solution improve the solver or computation budget

A positive architecture obstruction can itself admit more refined exact or infimal decompositions. Carrier information loss and decoder nonsaturation are separated in Chapter 16; rectangularization and coordination are separated in Chapter 13; fine-to-coarse representations generate fiber realization costs in Chapter 2. These decompositions are used only under their declared assumptions. They are not combined into a universal multi-term formula without an exact identity or a proved exchange bound.

3.4 What an empirical study should separate

A convincing structural study should report evidence for the four components rather than infer mechanism from one performance gap.

A performance plateau is therefore only a symptom. It supports a structural interpretation only after local model inadequacy, finite-sample uncertainty, and implementation error have been separately controlled. The prospectively frozen MNIST audit in Laboratory 24.2.1 applies this separation to a finite one-pass inference grammar: it holds the local variational contract fixed, uses held-out selection and evaluation, audits the imagewise reference, and tests data, width, and training-effort alternatives before changing the deployment computation.

Appendix to Chapter 3: complete proofs

Proof of the exact four-component risk identity

Dependencies. Only the definitions of the four components and finiteness of every displayed population/empirical evaluation and class infimum are used. No stochastic assumption and no attainment of the architecture infimum are needed.

Proof.

Write

R⁡(A^)−R⋆={Roracle−R⋆}+{infA∈𝔄R⁡(A)−Roracle}+{R⁡(A^)−infA∈𝔄R⁡(A)}.R(\widehat{A})-R^{\star}=\{R_{\rm oracle}-R^{\star}\}+\{\inf_{A\in\mathfrak{A}}R(A)-R_{\rm oracle}\}+\{R(\widehat{A})-\inf_{A\in\mathfrak{A}}R(A)\}.

For an arbitrary reference A†∈𝔄A^{\dagger}\in\mathfrak{A}, decompose the last bracket by adding and subtracting R⁡(A†)R(A^{\dagger}), R^n​(A†)\widehat{R}_{n}(A^{\dagger}), the empirical class infimum, and R^n​(A^)\widehat{R}_{n}(\widehat{A}):

R⁡(A^)−infA∈𝔄R⁡(A)=\displaystyle R(\widehat{A})-\inf_{A\in\mathfrak{A}}R(A)={} R​(A^)−R^n​(A^)\displaystyle R(\widehat{A})-\widehat{R}_{n}(\widehat{A})
+{R^n​(A^)−infA∈𝔄R^n​(A)}\displaystyle+\left\{\widehat{R}_{n}(\widehat{A})-\inf_{A\in\mathfrak{A}}\widehat{R}_{n}(A)\right\}
−{R^n​(A†)−infA∈𝔄R^n​(A)}\displaystyle-\left\{\widehat{R}_{n}(A^{\dagger})-\inf_{A\in\mathfrak{A}}\widehat{R}_{n}(A)\right\}
+R^n​(A†)−R⁡(A†)\displaystyle+\widehat{R}_{n}(A^{\dagger})-R(A^{\dagger})
+R⁡(A†)−infA∈𝔄R⁡(A).\displaystyle+R(A^{\dagger})-\inf_{A\in\mathfrak{A}}R(A).

The first two population brackets are respectively Δmodel\Delta^{\mathrm{model}} and Δarch\Delta^{\mathrm{arch}}; the two empirical-infimum brackets are Δnopt\Delta^{\mathrm{opt}}_{n} and ρ^n​(A†)\widehat{\rho}_{n}(A^{\dagger}); and the final population term is ρ⁡(A†)\rho(A^{\dagger}). Substitution proves the identity. The two residuals vanish under population and empirical attainment, respectively. ∎

Proof of the four-component certified learning bound

Dependencies. The lower bound uses only membership A^∈𝔄\widehat{A}\in\mathfrak{A}. The upper bound uses the uniform generalization event and the empirical optimization residual. Population attainment is not required.

Proof.

Since A^∈𝔄\widehat{A}\in\mathfrak{A},

R⁡(A^)≥infA∈𝔄R⁡(A)=R⋆+Δmodel+Δarch,R(\widehat{A})\geq\inf_{A\in\mathfrak{A}}R(A)=R^{\star}+\Delta^{\mathrm{model}}+\Delta^{\mathrm{arch}},

which proves the lower bound.

For the upper bound, let (Ak)k≥1⊆𝔄(A_{k})_{k\geq 1}\subseteq\mathfrak{A} be a minimizing sequence such that

R⁡(Ak)↓infA∈𝔄R⁡(A).R(A_{k})\downarrow\inf_{A\in\mathfrak{A}}R(A).

On the event supA∈𝔄|R⁡(A)−R^n​(A)|≤εn​(δ)\sup_{A\in\mathfrak{A}}|R(A)-\widehat{R}_{n}(A)|\leq\varepsilon_{n}(\delta), we have, for every kk,

R⁡(A^)\displaystyle R(\widehat{A}) ≤R^n​(A^)+εn​(δ)\displaystyle\leq\widehat{R}_{n}(\widehat{A})+\varepsilon_{n}(\delta)
≤infA∈𝔄R^n​(A)+ηn+εn​(δ)\displaystyle\leq\inf_{A\in\mathfrak{A}}\widehat{R}_{n}(A)+\eta_{n}+\varepsilon_{n}(\delta)
≤R^n​(Ak)+ηn+εn​(δ)\displaystyle\leq\widehat{R}_{n}(A_{k})+\eta_{n}+\varepsilon_{n}(\delta)
≤R⁡(Ak)+2​εn​(δ)+ηn.\displaystyle\leq R(A_{k})+2\varepsilon_{n}(\delta)+\eta_{n}.

Letting k→∞k\to\infty gives

R⁡(A^)≤infA∈𝔄R⁡(A)+2​εn​(δ)+ηn.R(\widehat{A})\leq\inf_{A\in\mathfrak{A}}R(A)+2\varepsilon_{n}(\delta)+\eta_{n}.

Chapter 4 Four Running Laboratories

4.1 Four recurring structural problems

Four recurring laboratories keep the abstract machinery tied to concrete failure modes. Each isolates one obstruction and its matched repair; Chapter 24 later recombines them inside more complex scientific interfaces.

  1. 1.

    Oracle-preserving coarse-graining illustrates carrier information loss, safe quotienting, back-mapping, and representation refinement.

  2. 2.

    Graph-indexed distribution learning illustrates signed high-order smoothing, probability validity, nonlinear projection, and sharp statistical rates.

  3. 3.

    Sequential conditional decision making illustrates rectangularity, shared-parameter coordination, memory compression, and operational context.

  4. 4.

    One-pass prediction illustrates architecture obstruction, local refinement, and an exact computation–defect frontier indexed by deployment budget.

The same terminology will mean the same thing in all four settings.

4.2 Laboratory I: oracle-preserving coarse-graining

What may a representation safely forget? Let a fine state X~\widetilde{X} have oracle output aX~⋆a_{\widetilde{X}}^{\star}, and let Z=q⁡(X~)Z=q(\widetilde{X}) be the carrier exposed to a decoder. Under squared native loss, the best unrestricted decoder returns 𝔼⁡(aX~⋆∣Z)\mathbb{E}(a_{\widetilde{X}}^{\star}\mid Z) and pays the carrier-information component

𝒞⁡(Z)=12​𝔼​‖aX~⋆−𝔼⁡(aX~⋆∣Z)‖2.\mathcal{C}(Z)=\frac{1}{2}\mathbb{E}\left\|a_{\widetilde{X}}^{\star}-\mathbb{E}(a_{\widetilde{X}}^{\star}\mid Z)\right\|^{2}.

If W=h⁡(Z)W=h(Z) is a further coarsening, the tower property gives the exact tax

𝒞⁡(W)−𝒞⁡(Z)=12​𝔼​‖𝔼⁡(aX~⋆∣Z)−𝔼⁡(aX~⋆∣W)‖2.\mathcal{C}(W)-\mathcal{C}(Z)=\frac{1}{2}\mathbb{E}\left\|\mathbb{E}(a_{\widetilde{X}}^{\star}\mid Z)-\mathbb{E}(a_{\widetilde{X}}^{\star}\mid W)\right\|^{2}.

Thus forgetting is free exactly when WW preserves the conditional oracle signature; raw state count and hidden dimension are not the relevant capacity.

Molecular coarse-graining supplies a concrete fiber model. A reaction coordinate z=q⁡(x~)z=q(\widetilde{x}) descends a fine potential UU to the potential of mean force

𝖶β​(z)=−1β​log⁡[v⁡(z)​∫q−1​(z)e−β​U​(x~)​νz​(𝑑x~)].\mathsf{W}_{\beta}(z)=-\frac{1}{\beta}\log\left[v(z)\int_{q^{-1}(z)}e^{-\beta U(\widetilde{x})}\,\nu_{z}(d\widetilde{x})\right].

Here v⁡(z)​νzv(z)\nu_{z} records the declared disintegration of the fine reference measure.

If Π~β\widetilde{\Pi}_{\beta} is the fine Gibbs law, Πβ𝖶\Pi_{\beta}^{\mathsf{W}} its coarse marginal, and ηβ,z\eta_{\beta,z} its oracle fiber kernel, then any trial fine law QQ, with coarse marginal PP and conditional back-mapping QzQ_{z}, obeys the exact conditional-KL decomposition

1βKL(Q∥Π~β)=1βKL(P∥Πβ𝖶)+1β𝔼PKL(Qz∥ηβ,z).\frac{1}{\beta}\operatorname{KL}(Q\|\widetilde{\Pi}_{\beta})=\frac{1}{\beta}\operatorname{KL}(P\|\Pi_{\beta}^{\mathsf{W}})+\frac{1}{\beta}\mathbb{E}_{P}\operatorname{KL}(Q_{z}\|\eta_{\beta,z}).

When PP is induced by a learned coarse potential, enriching that potential can reduce only the first component. The second is controlled by the conditional back-map; if the scientific oracle requires distinctions not measurable from zz, no coarse predictor can restore them. The matched repair is to refine the reaction coordinate or retain a faithful conditional back-mapping, according to which component is dominant.

Not every quotient is destructive. Replacing a subspace frame UU by the projector U​U⊤UU^{\top} removes only the U∼U​QU\sim UQ basis gauge and preserves the subspace oracle. The criterion is always oracle survival, not whether the representation became smaller.

Structural prediction.

Scaling a predictor behind a fixed coarse carrier saturates at 𝒞⁡(Z)\mathcal{C}(Z) when distinct conditional oracle means have been merged. Witness-directed carrier refinement can reduce that floor. For fine-law reconstruction, a faithful stochastic back-mapping instead removes the separate conditional-fiber term; dummy states and irrelevant gauge coordinates reduce neither.

4.3 Laboratory II: graph-indexed distribution learning

Let t=1,…,Tt=1,\ldots,T index vertices of a graph with Laplacian LL. At vertex tt, observations Yt​1,…,Yt​ntY_{t1},\ldots,Y_{tn_{t}} define an empirical CDF F^t\widehat{F}_{t}. A graph filter SS produces a raw field

F~=S​F^.\widetilde{F}=S\widehat{F}.

For higher-order qualification, the filter may have signed off-diagonal weights. Then F~t\widetilde{F}_{t} need not be a CDF.

Fix a compact outcome interval I=[a,b]I=[a,b] and work in the product space L2​(I)TL^{2}(I)^{T}. The valid set

𝒞={F:Ft​ is a CDF for every ​t}\mathcal{C}=\{F:F_{t}\text{ is a CDF for every }t\}

is closed and convex in that space. Projection

F=Π𝒞​(F~)F=\Pi_{\mathcal{C}}(\widetilde{F})

restores validity. Because the truth F⋆F^{\star} belongs to 𝒞\mathcal{C},

‖F−F⋆‖2≤‖F~−F⋆‖2.\|F-F^{\star}\|^{2}\leq\|\widetilde{F}-F^{\star}\|^{2}.

The projection can also contract graph roughness under the declared product geometry. On an unbounded outcome line, CDFs themselves need not lie in L2L^{2}; the corresponding statement must instead be formulated for an affine difference class (for example, functions whose difference from a fixed reference CDF is square integrable).

The laboratory separates three objects that are often conflated:

  1. 1.

    the raw ambient variational solution;

  2. 2.

    the nonlinear validity-repaired field;

  3. 3.

    the constrained variational optimizer over the CDF set.

The first and second are not generally the same as the third.

Structural prediction.

For smoothness beyond the graph-universal Markov range, linear high-order validity fails. Nonlinear repair can retain the statistical rate while restoring the semantic contract.

4.4 Laboratory III: shared conditional decisions

Consider a finite history tree. At history hh, a local oracle kernel is qh⋆(⋅∣h)q_{h}^{\star}(\cdot\mid h). The formal rectangular-hull construction is given in Chapter 13; here we use only its motivating contrast. A fully rectangular architecture can choose every conditional kernel independently, whereas a shared architecture may require

qh(⋅∣h)=qθ(⋅∣ϕ(h))q_{h}(\cdot\mid h)=q_{\theta}(\cdot\mid\phi(h))

for one parameter θ\theta and perhaps one compressed memory state ϕ⁡(h)\phi(h).

The rectangular hull Rect⁡(𝔄)\operatorname{Rect}(\mathfrak{A}), defined formally in Chapter 13, frees the locally available kernels and allows independent pasting. The rectangular value obeys an exact Bellman recursion. The gap

𝖳coord​(𝔄)=𝔒⁡(𝔄)−𝔒⁡{Rect⁡(𝔄)}\mathsf{T}^{\mathrm{coord}}(\mathfrak{A})=\mathfrak{O}(\mathfrak{A})-\mathfrak{O}\{\operatorname{Rect}(\mathfrak{A})\}

prices the cross-history coupling induced by sharing.

A coarse memory representation can be objective-faithful for one task while failing to realize the canonical fine conditional fibers. The resulting fiber tax depends on occupancy and on the declared oracle law.

Structural prediction.

Increasing network width without refining memory may not remove the coordination tax. Rectangularization, memory refinement, or a task-specific quotient can.

4.5 Laboratory IV: one-pass prediction and local refinement

When does test-time computation change the deployed class rather than merely improve training? At instance xx, consider the scalar local problem

Hx​(a)=12​{a−m⁡(x)}2,J⁡(x)=infaHx​(a)=0,𝖣x​(a)=Hx​(a)−J⁡(x).H_{x}(a)=\frac{1}{2}\{a-m(x)\}^{2},\qquad J(x)=\inf_{a}H_{x}(a)=0,\qquad\mathsf{D}_{x}(a)=H_{x}(a)-J(x).

The local oracle is ax⋆=m⁡(x)a_{x}^{\star}=m(x). Let PP be the deployment law and let 𝔄0\mathfrak{A}_{0} be a declared class of one-pass predictors. Its architecture obstruction is

𝔒P​(𝔄0)=infA∈𝔄0𝔼P​𝖣X​{A⁡(X)}.\mathfrak{O}_{P}(\mathfrak{A}_{0})=\inf_{A\in\mathfrak{A}_{0}}\mathbb{E}_{P}\mathsf{D}_{X}\{A(X)\}.

This infimum is architecture-relative by definition. A measured positive residual estimates it only after reachability error inside 𝔄0\mathfrak{A}_{0} has been controlled.

Starting from a0=A⁡(x)a_{0}=A(x), now permit exact local-gradient steps with a fixed 0<η<10<\eta<1:

aj+1=aj−η⁡{aj−m⁡(x)}.a_{j+1}=a_{j}-\eta\{a_{j}-m(x)\}.

The recursion is explicit,

aj=m⁡(x)+(1−η)j​{A⁡(x)−m⁡(x)},𝖣x​(aj)=(1−η)2​j​𝖣x​{A⁡(x)}.a_{j}=m(x)+(1-\eta)^{j}\{A(x)-m(x)\},\qquad\mathsf{D}_{x}(a_{j})=(1-\eta)^{2j}\mathsf{D}_{x}\{A(x)\}.

Write Rj​AR_{j}A for the resulting predictor and define the budgeted deployment class by

𝔄≤k={RjA:A∈𝔄0, 0≤j≤k},\mathfrak{A}_{\leq k}=\{R_{j}A:A\in\mathfrak{A}_{0},\ 0\leq j\leq k\},

where jj is integer. These classes are nested, and the pointwise identity gives the exact class-level resource–defect frontier

𝔒P​(𝔄≤k)=(1−η)2​k​𝔒P​(𝔄0).\boxed{\mathfrak{O}_{P}(\mathfrak{A}_{\leq k})=(1-\eta)^{2k}\mathfrak{O}_{P}(\mathfrak{A}_{0}).} (4.1)
An exact three-point ledger.

Let PP be uniform on {−1,0,1}\{-1,0,1\}, set m⁡(x)=x2m(x)=x^{2}, and take the one-pass grammar

𝔄0=𝔄aff={x↦α+βx:α,β∈ℝ}.\mathfrak{A}_{0}=\mathfrak{A}_{\mathrm{aff}}=\{x\mapsto\alpha+\beta x:\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}\}.

Its exact population risk is

𝔼P​𝖣X​{α+β​X}=16​[(α−β−1)2+α2+(α+β−1)2].\mathbb{E}_{P}\mathsf{D}_{X}\{\alpha+\beta X\}=\frac{1}{6}\left[(\alpha-\beta-1)^{2}+\alpha^{2}+(\alpha+\beta-1)^{2}\right].

The unique minimizer is (α⋆,β⋆)=(2/3,0)(\alpha^{\star},\beta^{\star})=(2/3,0), so

𝔒P​(𝔄aff)=19≈0.111111.\mathfrak{O}_{P}(\mathfrak{A}_{\mathrm{aff}})=\frac{1}{9}\approx 0.111111.

With η=1/2\eta=1/2, the class-level identity gives the complete numerical ledger in Table 4.1. These are exact population values under the declared three-point law, not Monte Carlo estimates.

The last row enlarges the one-pass grammar to {α+β​x+γ​x2}\{\alpha+\beta x+\gamma x^{2}\} and realizes the oracle with (α,β,γ)=(0,0,1)(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)=(0,0,1). It therefore removes the same baseline obstruction through a representation change rather than test-time compute. Operationally the refined system runs a local optimizer; structurally it has moved from 𝔄0\mathfrak{A}_{0} to the computation-indexed contract 𝔄≤k\mathfrak{A}_{\leq k}, not merely trained the same class more accurately.

Interface accounting.

Changing predictor width or features changes 𝔄0\mathfrak{A}_{0}; adding training data changes estimation; improving the one-pass optimizer changes reachability inside 𝔄0\mathfrak{A}_{0}; and increasing kk changes the deployment computation budget. Calling all four changes “more model capacity” loses the intervention map.

Structural prediction and boundary.

If a well-optimized one-pass class has 𝔒P​(𝔄0)>0\mathfrak{O}_{P}(\mathfrak{A}_{0})>0, local refinement traces the monotone frontier in (4.1). The quadratic calculation transfers an existing baseline floor; it does not prove that the floor is positive. For fixed-variance Gaussian variational inference, the negative-ELBO defect is this same laboratory up to a constant scale factor. Nonquadratic problems replace the equality by a curvature-controlled bound or an empirical audit; Chapter 24 later applies that audit logic to learned one-pass inference on MNIST.

4.6 A common table

The four laboratories can now be compared row by row. The table aligns their oracle, native defect, deployment contract, obstruction, repair, and statistical evidence before the final cross-laboratory lesson.

Why one example is not enough.

A theory based only on coarse-graining could be dismissed as information compression. A theory based only on graph CDFs could be dismissed as shape-constrained smoothing. A theory based only on sequential kernels could be dismissed as robust control or memory approximation. A theory based only on one-pass refinement could be dismissed as amortized inference or local optimization. The common lesson is deliberately limited: the same decomposition discipline applies in all four laboratories, while the obstruction mechanism and the repair remain model specific.

Part I Historical and Conceptual Notes

Where the four accounts sit in learning theory

Classical statistical learning separates approximation and estimation, and computational analyses add optimization error (Bartlett and Mendelson, 2002; Bousquet and Elisseeff, 2002; Bottou and Bousquet, 2008). Amortized inference then makes a further distinction between the best member of a local variational family and the output delivered by a shared inference mechanism (Cremer et al., 2018; Amos, 2023; Margossian and Blei, 2024). Part I does not claim priority for these decompositions or for the telescoping identity in Proposition 3.1.

The narrower book contribution is to insert a contract-relative reference between local approximation and learned deployment:

R⋆⟶Roracle⟶infA∈𝔄R⁡(A)⟶R⁡(A^).R^{\star}\longrightarrow R_{\rm oracle}\longrightarrow\inf_{A\in\mathfrak{A}}R(A)\longrightarrow R(\widehat{A}).

The first arrow measures whether the declared local family is scientifically adequate. The second asks whether one declared global architecture can realize the already-fixed local oracle family. The last arrow is governed by data and implementation. This split can coincide with an amortization gap in a variational-inference example, but it is not defined by amortization: it also applies to shared policies, finite memories, continuous selectors, compressed carriers, and other deployment contracts.

Account Historical neighbor Part I distinction
Local model gap approximation or variational-family gap compares the local oracle with the scientific target before global sharing is imposed
Architecture gap amortization, approximation under a restricted function class fixes one deployment contract and prices failure to realize the whole oracle field in population-risk units
Generalization estimation and uniform convergence controls population versus empirical behavior for the declared, possibly selected, class
Implementation optimization or reachability error compares the fitted rule with the empirical class optimum and is not folded into structural nonrealizability
Ownership of the Part I results

The exact identity is a book-level accounting synthesis. The certified bound is the standard two-deviation empirical-risk argument specialized to that accounting chain. Their value is diagnostic separation: changing the local family, the shared architecture, the data, or the optimizer changes a different reference comparison. The detailed row-by-row provenance is in Appendix G.1.

Part II Native Defects and Elimination Calculus
Elimination does more than simplify an objective. It generates an objective-native notion of excess loss and determines which transformations preserve the statistical target.

Chapter 5 Conjugate Lifts and Native Loss Scales

Suppose an inner state is introduced because it makes an objective easier to optimize. After elimination, a trial inner state should be evaluated in the same units as the objective. A Euclidean penalty may be algorithmically convenient, but it is not automatically the insertion price.

The canonical residual is

𝖣x​(a)=Hx​(a)−infbHx​(b).\mathsf{D}_{x}(a)=H_{x}(a)-\inf_{b}H_{x}(b).

In conjugate-complete lifts this residual is a directed Bregman divergence. This observation fixes the orientation of KL and other asymmetric divergences.

5.1 Legendre conjugacy

Let Φ:𝒜→ℝ∪{+∞}\Phi:\mathcal{A}\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\} be a proper, closed, strictly convex Legendre function. Its conjugate is

Φ⋆​(u)=supa{⟨u,a⟩−Φ⁡(a)}.\Phi^{\star}(u)=\sup_{a}\{\langle u,a\rangle-\Phi(a)\}.

For uu in the interior of the dual domain,

a⋆​(u)=∇Φ⋆​(u)a^{\star}(u)=\nabla\Phi^{\star}(u)

solves

infa{Φ⁡(a)−⟨u,a⟩}=−Φ⋆​(u).\inf_{a}\{\Phi(a)-\langle u,a\rangle\}=-\Phi^{\star}(u).

The Bregman divergence generated by Φ\Phi is (Bregman, 1967)

DΦ(a∥b)=Φ(a)−Φ(b)−⟨∇Φ(b),a−b⟩.D_{\Phi}(a\|b)=\Phi(a)-\Phi(b)-\langle\nabla\Phi(b),a-b\rangle.
Theorem 5.1 (Conjugate defect identity).

Let

Hu​(a)=Φ⁡(a)−⟨u,a⟩+c⁡(u).H_{u}(a)=\Phi(a)-\langle u,a\rangle+c(u).

Then the eliminated objective is

J⁡(u)=c⁡(u)−Φ⋆​(u),J(u)=c(u)-\Phi^{\star}(u),

and

Hu(a)−J(u)=DΦ{a∥a⋆(u)}.H_{u}(a)-J(u)=D_{\Phi}\{a\|a^{\star}(u)\}.

The order of the arguments is not cosmetic. The trial state appears in the first argument and the oracle in the second. Reversing the divergence generally changes both geometry and performance guarantees.

5.2 Examples of native Bregman defects

5.2.1 Relative entropy

For probability vectors qq and pp on the same finite set, take

Φ⁡(q)=∑zqz​log⁡qz.\Phi(q)=\sum_{z}q_{z}\log q_{z}.

Then

DΦ(q∥p)=KL(q∥p).D_{\Phi}(q\|p)=\operatorname{KL}(q\|p).

Classical II-divergence geometry supplies the projection background for this probability-simplex example (Csiszár, 1975). A variational lift based on entropy nevertheless generates one particular KL direction. The reverse direction is not certified unless it arises from a different elimination.

5.2.2 LogDet divergence

For positive-definite matrices X,Y∈𝕊+⁣+mX,Y\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^{m}, take

Φ(X)=−logdetX.\Phi(X)=-\log\det X.

The corresponding Bregman divergence is

DΦ(X∥Y)=tr(Y−1X)−logdet(Y−1X)−m.D_{\Phi}(X\|Y)=\operatorname{tr}(Y^{-1}X)-\log\det(Y^{-1}X)-m.

This is the Burg or LogDet divergence (Kulis et al., 2009). Its natural centroid and consensus endpoint differ from Euclidean matrix averaging.

5.2.3 Quantum relative entropy

On the faithful density-matrix domain, the entropy functional

Φ⁡(ρ)=tr⁡(ρ​log⁡ρ)\Phi(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho\log\rho)

induces Umegaki relative entropy (Umegaki, 1962)

D(ρ∥σ)=trρ(logρ−logσ).D(\rho\|\sigma)=\operatorname{tr}\rho(\log\rho-\log\sigma).

For general density matrices, this formula is understood through its lower-semicontinuous extension: D(ρ∥σ)<∞D(\rho\|\sigma)<\infty only when supp⁡(ρ)⊆supp⁡(σ)\operatorname{supp}(\rho)\subseteq\operatorname{supp}(\sigma), and it is +∞+\infty otherwise. On the faithful domain both logarithms and the Bregman gradient are ordinary finite-dimensional operators. The noncommutative case preserves the defect orientation but changes the validity of base change—the fine-to-coarse passage formalized in Chapter 18—and measurement.

5.3 Further certified eliminations and boundaries

EM as a certified elimination.

Let pθ​(x,z)p_{\theta}(x,z) be a latent-variable model. For a trial conditional law q⁡(z)q(z) define

Hx​(θ,q)=−𝔼q​log⁡pθ​(x,Z)−𝖧⁡(q),H_{x}(\theta,q)=-\mathbb{E}_{q}\log p_{\theta}(x,Z)-\mathsf{H}(q),

where 𝖧⁡(q)=−𝔼q​log⁡q⁡(Z)\mathsf{H}(q)=-\mathbb{E}_{q}\log q(Z). The Gibbs variational identity gives

−log⁡pθ​(x)=infqHx​(θ,q).-\log p_{\theta}(x)=\inf_{q}H_{x}(\theta,q).

Moreover,

Hx(θ,q)+logpθ(x)=KL{q∥pθ(⋅∣x)}.H_{x}(\theta,q)+\log p_{\theta}(x)=\operatorname{KL}\{q\|p_{\theta}(\cdot\mid x)\}.

Thus inserting a shared or approximated posterior pays the forward variational KL from the trial law to the exact posterior. This is the variational identity underlying classical EM and its free-energy interpretation (Dempster et al., 1977; Neal and Hinton, 1998).

Left and right Bregman pooling.

For interior points a1,…,aTa_{1},\ldots,a_{T} with weights wt≥0w_{t}\geq 0 satisfying ∑twt=1\sum_{t}w_{t}=1, two pooling problems differ:

mina∑twtDΦ(at∥a),mina∑twtDΦ(a∥at).\min_{a}\sum_{t}w_{t}D_{\Phi}(a_{t}\|a),\qquad\min_{a}\sum_{t}w_{t}D_{\Phi}(a\|a_{t}).

When the displayed means remain in the relevant Legendre domain, the first produces the primal arithmetic average

a=∑twt​at,a=\sum_{t}w_{t}a_{t},

whereas the second produces the dual-coordinate average

∇Φ(a)=∑twt∇Φ(at).\nabla\Phi(a)=\sum_{t}w_{t}\nabla\Phi(a_{t}).

For KL on probability vectors, these are respectively arithmetic mixture pooling and normalized geometric pooling; the distinction is standard in Bregman centroid geometry (Banerjee et al., 2005b).

This distinction matters when a shared auxiliary field is designed by averaging. The correct pooling direction depends on the certified defect orientation.

Saddle elimination.

Certified residuals also arise from convex–concave elimination. Suppose

J⁡(x)=infasupbLx​(a,b)J(x)=\inf_{a}\sup_{b}L_{x}(a,b)

under strong duality. Let (ax⋆,bx⋆)(a_{x}^{\star},b_{x}^{\star}) be a saddle point. A trial pair can be audited by primal and dual insertion gaps,

Lx​(a,bx⋆)−J⁡(x)≥0,J⁡(x)−Lx​(ax⋆,b)≥0.L_{x}(a,b_{x}^{\star})-J(x)\geq 0,\qquad J(x)-L_{x}(a_{x}^{\star},b)\geq 0.

Their sum is a primal–dual certificate. The same orientation discipline applies: the two signs are fixed by the min–max order.

Exchange inequalities.

The native defect can be exchanged for a more geometric error when the objective has curvature. If

𝖣x​(a)≥μ2​d2​{a,𝒪⁡(x)},\mathsf{D}_{x}(a)\geq\frac{\mu}{2}d^{2}\{a,\mathcal{O}(x)\},

then

d​{a,𝒪⁡(x)}≤2​𝖣x​(a)/μ.d\{a,\mathcal{O}(x)\}\leq\sqrt{2\mathsf{D}_{x}(a)/\mu}.

Conversely, work in Euclidean or Hilbert geometry, with d⁡(a,b)=∥a−b∥d(a,b)=\lVert a-b\rVert. Suppose a nearest oracle

b∈arg​minc∈𝒪⁡(x)⁡∥a−c∥b\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{c\in\mathcal{O}(x)}\lVert a-c\rVert

exists, 𝖣x\mathsf{D}_{x} is differentiable on a neighborhood containing the whole segment [b,a][b,a], ∇𝖣x​(b)=0\nabla\mathsf{D}_{x}(b)=0, and ∇𝖣x\nabla\mathsf{D}_{x} is LL-Lipschitz on that neighborhood. The descent lemma and 𝖣x​(b)=0\mathsf{D}_{x}(b)=0 then give

𝖣x​(a)≤𝖣x​(b)+⟨∇𝖣x​(b),a−b⟩+L2​∥a−b∥2=L2​d2​{a,𝒪⁡(x)}.\mathsf{D}_{x}(a)\leq\mathsf{D}_{x}(b)+\langle\nabla\mathsf{D}_{x}(b),a-b\rangle+\frac{L}{2}\lVert a-b\rVert^{2}=\frac{L}{2}d^{2}\{a,\mathcal{O}(x)\}.

These exchanges are local analytic theorems, not definitions of the defect.

When the defect is set-valued.

If 𝒪⁡(x)\mathcal{O}(x) has multiple elements, the residual still satisfies

𝖣x​(a)=0⇔a∈𝒪⁡(x).\mathsf{D}_{x}(a)=0\iff a\in\mathcal{O}(x).

A distance-to-oracle bound may use

d⁡{a,𝒪⁡(x)}=infb∈𝒪⁡(x)d⁡(a,b),d\{a,\mathcal{O}(x)\}=\inf_{b\in\mathcal{O}(x)}d(a,b),

but a particular labeled representative should not be selected unless the output contract requires it. This is the first place where representation semantics enters.

Appendix to Chapter 5: complete proofs

Proof of the conjugate defect identity

Dependencies. Fenchel conjugacy and the Legendre identity ∇Φ​(a⋆​(u))=u\nabla\Phi(a^{\star}(u))=u are the only ingredients. Strict convexity is used for uniqueness of the oracle, not for the algebraic equality itself.

Proof.

By definition of the convex conjugate,

Φ⋆​(u)=⟨u,a⋆​(u)⟩−Φ⁡{a⋆​(u)},\Phi^{\star}(u)=\langle u,a^{\star}(u)\rangle-\Phi\{a^{\star}(u)\},

where a⋆​(u)=∇Φ⋆​(u)a^{\star}(u)=\nabla\Phi^{\star}(u) and u=∇Φ​{a⋆​(u)}u=\nabla\Phi\{a^{\star}(u)\}. Therefore

J⁡(u)\displaystyle J(u) =infa{Φ⁡(a)−⟨u,a⟩+c⁡(u)}\displaystyle=\inf_{a}\{\Phi(a)-\langle u,a\rangle+c(u)\}
=c​(u)−Φ⋆​(u).\displaystyle=c(u)-\Phi^{\star}(u).

For an arbitrary trial state aa,

Hu​(a)−J​(u)\displaystyle H_{u}(a)-J(u) =Φ⁡(a)−⟨u,a⟩+Φ⋆​(u)\displaystyle=\Phi(a)-\langle u,a\rangle+\Phi^{\star}(u)
=Φ⁡(a)−Φ⁡(a⋆)−⟨u,a−a⋆⟩\displaystyle=\Phi(a)-\Phi(a^{\star})-\langle u,a-a^{\star}\rangle
=Φ⁡(a)−Φ⁡(a⋆)−⟨∇Φ​(a⋆),a−a⋆⟩\displaystyle=\Phi(a)-\Phi(a^{\star})-\left\langle\nabla\Phi(a^{\star}),a-a^{\star}\right\rangle
=DΦ(a∥a⋆).\displaystyle=D_{\Phi}(a\|a^{\star}).

Nonnegativity and equality only at a=a⋆a=a^{\star} follow from strict convexity of Φ\Phi. ∎

Chapter 6 Elimination Towers and the P/G/X/V/C Calculus

The P/G/X/V/C calculus and an elimination tower describe orthogonal directions. The five letters classify what happens within one elimination level after its local oracle has been exposed, whereas a tower records how states and defects pass between levels. The mode says what was changed; the tower says where its cost propagates.

6.1 Five distinct operations on an elimination system

The calculus begins from one noncommutation:

Eliminate∘Couple≠Couple∘Eliminate.\operatorname{Eliminate}\circ\operatorname{Couple}\neq\operatorname{Couple}\circ\operatorname{Eliminate}.

The decisive question is not which numerical smoother is used, but where the coupling enters the declared contract.

Suppose J⁡(Θ)=infAH0​(Θ,A)J(\Theta)=\inf_{A}H_{0}(\Theta,A) and A⋆​(Θ)A^{\star}(\Theta) is the pointwise oracle. Across an index set 𝒯\mathcal{T} of locations, tasks, or replicas, the oracles form a field A⋆=(At⋆)t∈𝒯A^{\star}=(A_{t}^{\star})_{t\in\mathcal{T}}. A practitioner may wish to smooth, pool, share, or couple that field.

The common contract fixes the original lift H0H_{0}, its eliminated target JJ, and the oracle field A⋆A^{\star}. It may also declare an external field operator SS, a coherence penalty RR, or marginal laws (μt)(\mu_{t}) whose couplings form Γ(μt:t∈𝒯)\Gamma(\mu_{t}:t\in\mathcal{T}). A P/G/X/V/C label records which of these objects is acted on and what remains invariant. It does not name a numerical algorithm: the same smoother can implement different operations under different contracts.

6.1.1 P: pointwise elimination

The baseline is

At=At⋆​(Θ).A_{t}=A_{t}^{\star}(\Theta).

No cross-index coherence is imposed. The target remains exactly JJ and every local defect is zero. P is the reference contract against which the other four operations are measured.

6.1.2 G: plug-in globalization

An external operator SS transforms the oracle field:

A~=S​A⋆.\widetilde{A}=SA^{\star}.

The field is inserted back into the original lift. The target value becomes

H0​(Θ,A~)=J⁡(Θ)+𝖣Θ​(A~).H_{0}(\Theta,\widetilde{A})=J(\Theta)+\mathsf{D}_{\Theta}(\widetilde{A}).

The insertion defect is exact. G does not optimize a new joint objective; it deploys an externally constructed field. Thus G changes the deployed field while holding H0H_{0} and JJ fixed.

6.1.3 X: exactification

If a frozen G step at anchor Θ¯\bar{\Theta} gives QG​(Θ)=J⁡(Θ)+d⁡(Θ)Q_{G}(\Theta)=J(\Theta)+d(\Theta), X forms

QX(k)​(Θ∣Θ¯)=QG​(Θ)−Tk​d​(Θ,Θ¯),jΘ¯k​QX(k)=jΘ¯k​J.Q_{X}^{(k)}(\Theta\mid\bar{\Theta})=Q_{G}(\Theta)-T_{k}d(\Theta;\bar{\Theta}),\qquad j_{\bar{\Theta}}^{k}Q_{X}^{(k)}=j_{\bar{\Theta}}^{k}J.

X changes the frozen surrogate, not the field or the joint law. Chapter 7 develops the construction and its converse.

6.1.4 V: variational coupling

V places the field and a coherence penalty inside a new objective:

Jλ​(Θ)=infA{H0​(Θ,A)+λ​R​(A)}.J_{\lambda}(\Theta)=\inf_{A}\{H_{0}(\Theta,A)+\lambda R(A)\}.

The statistical or optimization target changes. Block monotonicity can be exact, but the estimator need not target the original JJ. The returned estimand is JλJ_{\lambda}, not merely JJ evaluated at an external field.

6.1.5 C: fixed-marginal coupling

C keeps every coordinate procedure and marginal law fixed, choosing only

γ∈Γ(μt:t∈𝒯).\gamma\in\Gamma(\mu_{t}:t\in\mathcal{T}).

It is relevant to common random numbers, antithetic couplings, ensemble dependence, and variance reduction. Additive coordinate expectations cannot improve under a fixed-marginal coupling; only genuinely joint functionals can.

6.2 A compact classification test

Classify a procedure from the provenance of its returned object, not from the last numerical array it produces.

  1. 1.

    If it stops after independent pointwise elimination, label it P.

  2. 2.

    If it transforms the oracle field outside the original objective and then evaluates that field in H0H_{0}, label it G.

  3. 3.

    If it subtracts a defect jet to restore target contact at an anchor, label that correction X.

  4. 4.

    If it moves coherence inside an objective and reoptimizes jointly, label it V.

  5. 5.

    If it fixes all marginals and changes only their joint coupling, label it C.

A workflow may answer more than one question affirmatively. Record the sequence—for example, G→X\mathrm{G}\to\mathrm{X}—because the last step does not erase the contract of the earlier one.

6.3 Horizontal operations and multistage towers

If a stage uses one or more horizontal modes, its certified defect contribution enters the vertical decomposition; the stage costs then compose by infimal convolution.

A multistage elimination tower.

Let a fine state ee map to an intermediate state bb and then to a coarse state cc:

ℰ→𝜋ℬ→𝜎𝒞.\mathcal{E}\xrightarrow{\pi}\mathcal{B}\xrightarrow{\sigma}\mathcal{C}.

Suppose the defect splits at each stage,

𝖣ℰ​(e)=𝖣ℬ​(π​e)+δπ​(e),\mathsf{D}^{\mathcal{E}}(e)=\mathsf{D}^{\mathcal{B}}(\pi e)+\delta_{\pi}(e),
𝖣ℬ​(b)=𝖣𝒞​(σ​b)+δσ​(b).\mathsf{D}^{\mathcal{B}}(b)=\mathsf{D}^{\mathcal{C}}(\sigma b)+\delta_{\sigma}(b).

Then

𝖣ℰ​(e)=𝖣𝒞​(σ​π​e)+δσ​(π​e)+δπ​(e).\mathsf{D}^{\mathcal{E}}(e)=\mathsf{D}^{\mathcal{C}}(\sigma\pi e)+\delta_{\sigma}(\pi e)+\delta_{\pi}(e).

After minimizing over architecture-constrained fibers, the realization costs compose by infimal convolution:

Ψσ​π(c)=infb:σ​b=c{δσ(b)+Ψπ(b)}.\Psi_{\sigma\pi}(c)=\inf_{b:\sigma b=c}\{\delta_{\sigma}(b)+\Psi_{\pi}(b)\}.

This is the usual Bellman/min-plus composition law (Bellman, 1957; Baccelli et al., 1992).

Proposition 6.1 (Tower associativity).

For compatible consecutive state spaces, define the typed stage-cost composition by

(c1□c2)​(x2,x0):=infx1​compatible{c1​(x1,x0)+c2​(x2,x1)}.(c_{1}\mathbin{\square}c_{2})(x_{2},x_{0}):=\inf_{x_{1}\ {\rm compatible}}\{c_{1}(x_{1},x_{0})+c_{2}(x_{2},x_{1})\}.

Whenever the relevant feasible sets are nonempty, the following identity holds pointwise for every compatible endpoint pair (x3,x0)(x_{3},x_{0}):

{(c1□c2)□c3}​(x3,x0)={c1□(c2□c3)}​(x3,x0).\{(c_{1}\mathbin{\square}c_{2})\mathbin{\square}c_{3}\}(x_{3},x_{0})=\{c_{1}\mathbin{\square}(c_{2}\mathbin{\square}c_{3})\}(x_{3},x_{0}).
Why the tower matters.

The tower converts a vague statement such as “the representation loses information” into a decomposition with identifiable stages.

  • •

    A coarse representation can choose the wrong coarse object.

  • •

    Even the correct coarse object may be expensive to realize in the fine architecture.

  • •

    A deployed algorithm may then incur additional implementation error inside the chosen fine class.

The same structure appears in COT under conditional-law base change, in resource-constrained architectures under carrier–decoder decomposition, and in certificate statistics under evidence compression.

6.4 Worked decompositions and coupling boundaries

Bregman Pythagorean identities.

Suppose 𝒞⊆𝒜\mathcal{C}\subseteq\mathcal{A} is convex and the Bregman projection in the first argument exists:

a𝒞∈arg​minc∈𝒞DΦ(c∥a⋆).a_{\mathcal{C}}\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{c\in\mathcal{C}}D_{\Phi}(c\|a^{\star}).

Thus the projected point varies in the first argument while a⋆a^{\star} remains the second argument. Under the standard differentiability and convex projection conditions (Bauschke and Borwein, 1997), every comparison point a∈𝒞a\in\mathcal{C} satisfies

DΦ(a∥a⋆)≥DΦ(a∥a𝒞)+DΦ(a𝒞∥a⋆).D_{\Phi}(a\|a^{\star})\geq D_{\Phi}(a\|a_{\mathcal{C}})+D_{\Phi}(a_{\mathcal{C}}\|a^{\star}).

This gives a three-level interpretation:

  1. 1.

    irreducible constraint defect;

  2. 2.

    within-constraint implementation defect;

  3. 3.

    possible nonorthogonality remainder if exact Pythagoras fails.

A worked Gaussian field.

Let at⋆a_{t}^{\star} be local Gaussian means and let

Ht​(at)=12​(at−at⋆)2.H_{t}(a_{t})=\frac{1}{2}(a_{t}-a_{t}^{\star})^{2}.

On a graph with Laplacian LL, V solves

mina⁡12​‖a−a⋆‖2+λ2​a⊤​L​a.\min_{a}\frac{1}{2}\|a-a^{\star}\|^{2}+\frac{\lambda}{2}a^{\top}La.

The solution is

aV=(I+λ​L)−1​a⋆.a^{\rm V}=(I+\lambda L)^{-1}a^{\star}.

If G uses the same filter externally, the deployed field coincides numerically with aVa^{\rm V} in this quadratic unconstrained example. Nevertheless the interpretation differs: G evaluates the original lift at an external field; V defines the field as the optimizer of a changed objective. Under constraints or nonlinear repair, the numerical equality generally disappears.

C coupling and its boundary.

Let Y1,…,YTY_{1},\ldots,Y_{T} have fixed marginals. Whenever every ℓt​(Yt)\ell_{t}(Y_{t}) is integrable, any additive target satisfies

𝔼​∑tℓt​(Yt)=∑t𝔼​ℓt​(Yt),\mathbb{E}\sum_{t}\ell_{t}(Y_{t})=\sum_{t}\mathbb{E}\ell_{t}(Y_{t}),

changing the joint coupling cannot change the expectation. A benefit requires a joint functional, such as variance of an average, maximum loss, simultaneous coverage, or a path-dependent objective.

Appendix to Chapter 6: complete proofs

Proof of tower associativity

Dependencies. Only the compatibility of intermediate states and the convention that the infimum of an empty feasible set is +∞+\infty are used.

Proof.

Let x0,x1,x2,x3x_{0},x_{1},x_{2},x_{3} denote compatible states at four consecutive levels, and let the three stage costs be c1​(x1,x0)c_{1}(x_{1},x_{0}), c2​(x2,x1)c_{2}(x_{2},x_{1}), and c3​(x3,x2)c_{3}(x_{3},x_{2}). For fixed endpoints (x3,x0)(x_{3},x_{0}),

{(c1□c2)□c3}​(x3,x0)\displaystyle\{(c_{1}\mathbin{\square}c_{2})\mathbin{\square}c_{3}\}(x_{3},x_{0}) =infx2[infx1{c1​(x1,x0)+c2​(x2,x1)}+c3​(x3,x2)]\displaystyle=\inf_{x_{2}}\left[\inf_{x_{1}}\{c_{1}(x_{1},x_{0})+c_{2}(x_{2},x_{1})\}+c_{3}(x_{3},x_{2})\right]
=infx1,x2{c1​(x1,x0)+c2​(x2,x1)+c3​(x3,x2)}.\displaystyle=\inf_{x_{1},x_{2}}\{c_{1}(x_{1},x_{0})+c_{2}(x_{2},x_{1})+c_{3}(x_{3},x_{2})\}.

Similarly,

{c1□(c2□c3)}​(x3,x0)\displaystyle\{c_{1}\mathbin{\square}(c_{2}\mathbin{\square}c_{3})\}(x_{3},x_{0}) =infx1[c1​(x1,x0)+infx2{c2​(x2,x1)+c3​(x3,x2)}]\displaystyle=\inf_{x_{1}}\left[c_{1}(x_{1},x_{0})+\inf_{x_{2}}\{c_{2}(x_{2},x_{1})+c_{3}(x_{3},x_{2})\}\right]
=infx1,x2{c1​(x1,x0)+c2​(x2,x1)+c3​(x3,x2)}.\displaystyle=\inf_{x_{1},x_{2}}\{c_{1}(x_{1},x_{0})+c_{2}(x_{2},x_{1})+c_{3}(x_{3},x_{2})\}.

The two expressions are identical. The same argument applies to extended-valued realization costs and proves the stated tower law. ∎

Chapter 7 Exactification and Optimization Certificates

Fix an anchor Θ¯\bar{\Theta} and freeze a feasible, possibly nonlocal, auxiliary field A~\widetilde{A}. The field may have been constructed by a globalization step at the anchor, but it is held fixed as the outer parameter varies. Define

QG​(Θ)=H0​(Θ,A~)=J⁡(Θ)+d⁡(Θ),Q_{G}(\Theta)=H_{0}(\Theta,\widetilde{A})=J(\Theta)+d(\Theta),

where

d⁡(Θ)=𝖣Θ​(A~)=H0​(Θ,A~)−J⁡(Θ)≥0.d(\Theta)=\mathsf{D}_{\Theta}(\widetilde{A})=H_{0}(\Theta,\widetilde{A})-J(\Theta)\geq 0.

Even if the frozen lift is smooth in Θ\Theta, QGQ_{G} need not touch JJ at the current iterate. Minimizing QGQ_{G} can therefore optimize the defect rather than the target.

Exactification repairs this problem by subtracting the local defect jet. In the P/G/X/V/C calculus of Chapter 6, the frozen construction is G and the jet correction is X; no V objective or C coupling is introduced.

In this chapter, an optimization certificate combines target-jet contact with explicit inner-oracle, defect-score, and step-acceptance error budgets; exactification supplies the target-contact component.

7.1 Jet exactification

Let Tk​d​(Θ,Θ¯)T_{k}d(\Theta;\bar{\Theta}) be the order-kk Taylor polynomial of the frozen defect dd at Θ¯\bar{\Theta}. Define

QX(k)​(Θ∣Θ¯)=J⁡(Θ)+d⁡(Θ)−Tk​d​(Θ,Θ¯).Q_{X}^{(k)}(\Theta\mid\bar{\Theta})=J(\Theta)+d(\Theta)-T_{k}d(\Theta;\bar{\Theta}).

Then the kk-jet of QX(k)Q_{X}^{(k)} agrees with that of JJ at the anchor.

Theorem 7.1 (Jet exactification).

If both JJ and dd are CkC^{k} on a neighborhood of Θ¯\bar{\Theta}, then

jΘ¯k​QX(k)=jΘ¯k​J.j_{\bar{\Theta}}^{k}Q_{X}^{(k)}=j_{\bar{\Theta}}^{k}J.

In particular, for k=1k=1,

QX​(Θ¯∣Θ¯)=J⁡(Θ¯),∇QX​(Θ¯∣Θ¯)=∇J​(Θ¯).Q_{X}(\bar{\Theta}\mid\bar{\Theta})=J(\bar{\Theta}),\qquad\nabla Q_{X}(\bar{\Theta}\mid\bar{\Theta})=\nabla J(\bar{\Theta}).

The result is elementary once dd is known. The substantive point is that dd is the exact native insertion defect, not an arbitrary correction. The construction and converse below are the exactification normal form of the companion framework; their relation to first-order surrogate functions is discussed there as well (Huang and Wang, 2026f; Mairal, 2013).

Candidate-wise descent identity.

For first-order exactification,

QX​(Θ∣Θ¯)=J⁡(Θ)+d⁡(Θ)−d⁡(Θ¯)−⟨∇d​(Θ¯),Θ−Θ¯⟩.Q_{X}(\Theta\mid\bar{\Theta})=J(\Theta)+d(\Theta)-d(\bar{\Theta})-\langle\nabla d(\bar{\Theta}),\Theta-\bar{\Theta}\rangle.

If a candidate Θ+\Theta^{+} satisfies

QX​(Θ+∣Θ¯)≤QX​(Θ¯∣Θ¯)−γ​‖Θ+−Θ¯‖2,Q_{X}(\Theta^{+}\mid\bar{\Theta})\leq Q_{X}(\bar{\Theta}\mid\bar{\Theta})-\gamma\|\Theta^{+}-\bar{\Theta}\|^{2},

then

J⁡(Θ+)−J⁡(Θ¯)=\displaystyle J(\Theta^{+})-J(\bar{\Theta})={} QX​(Θ+∣Θ¯)−QX​(Θ¯∣Θ¯)\displaystyle Q_{X}(\Theta^{+}\mid\bar{\Theta})-Q_{X}(\bar{\Theta}\mid\bar{\Theta})
−[d⁡(Θ+)−d⁡(Θ¯)−⟨∇d​(Θ¯),Θ+−Θ¯⟩].\displaystyle-\Bigl[d(\Theta^{+})-d(\bar{\Theta})-\langle\nabla d(\bar{\Theta}),\Theta^{+}-\bar{\Theta}\rangle\Bigr].

If the defect gradient is locally LdL_{d}-Lipschitz, the bracket is bounded below by −Ld∥Θ+−Θ¯∥2/2-L_{d}\|\Theta^{+}-\bar{\Theta}\|^{2}/2. Hence

J⁡(Θ+)−J⁡(Θ¯)≤−(γ−Ld/2)​‖Θ+−Θ¯‖2.J(\Theta^{+})-J(\bar{\Theta})\leq-(\gamma-L_{d}/2)\|\Theta^{+}-\bar{\Theta}\|^{2}.

A trust region or backtracking line search enforces γ>Ld/2\gamma>L_{d}/2.

7.2 The converse normal form

The forward construction subtracts the Taylor jet of the frozen defect. The converse asks whether any scalar correction can preserve the target kk-jet without doing the same. The hypothesis box fixes the local comparison under which the theorem gives the answer.

Theorem 7.2 (Converse exactification normal form).

Suppose J,d,c,SJ,d,c,S are CkC^{k} on a neighborhood of Θ¯\bar{\Theta} and a surrogate can be written as

Q⁡(Θ)=J⁡(Θ)+d⁡(Θ)−c⁡(Θ)+S⁡(Θ).Q(\Theta)=J(\Theta)+d(\Theta)-c(\Theta)+S(\Theta).

Then

jΘ¯k​Q=jΘ¯k​Jj_{\bar{\Theta}}^{k}Q=j_{\bar{\Theta}}^{k}J

if and only if

jΘ¯k​{c−S}=jΘ¯k​d.j_{\bar{\Theta}}^{k}\{c-S\}=j_{\bar{\Theta}}^{k}d.

Thus any target-kk-jet-preserving correction subtracts the defect jet, modulo a kk-flat term. Equivalently, the canonical representative is

QX,can(k)​(Θ∣Θ¯)=H0​(Θ,A~)−Tk​d​(Θ,Θ¯),Q_{X,\mathrm{can}}^{(k)}(\Theta\mid\bar{\Theta})=H_{0}(\Theta,\widetilde{A})-T_{k}d(\Theta;\bar{\Theta}),

and every other target-kk-jet-preserving surrogate of the displayed form is QX,can(k)+RQ_{X,\mathrm{can}}^{(k)}+R, where RR is kk-flat at Θ¯\bar{\Theta}. Conversely, every such kk-flat perturbation preserves the target kk-jet.

The converse gives exactification a structural status: first-order target preservation forces a defect-score correction, not just any tangent surrogate.

7.3 Approximation, transmission, and certification error

Approximate inner oracles.

In practice, the auxiliary oracle and its defect gradient are computed approximately. Suppose H0​(Θ,⋅)H_{0}(\Theta,\cdot) is differentiable and μ\mu-strongly convex, its minimizer a⋆a^{\star} is interior and satisfies ∇aH0​(Θ,a⋆)=0\nabla_{a}H_{0}(\Theta,a^{\star})=0, and the outer score ∇ΘH0​(Θ,a)\nabla_{\Theta}H_{0}(\Theta,a) is LL-Lipschitz in aa. Then an inner gradient residual

‖∇aH0​(Θ,a~)‖≤ϵ\|\nabla_{a}H_{0}(\Theta,\widetilde{a})\|\leq\epsilon

implies

‖a~−a⋆‖≤ϵ/μ,\|\widetilde{a}-a^{\star}\|\leq\epsilon/\mu,
0≤H0​(Θ,a~)−J⁡(Θ)≤ϵ2/(2​μ),0\leq H_{0}(\Theta,\widetilde{a})-J(\Theta)\leq\epsilon^{2}/(2\mu),

and, under the usual envelope/Danskin regularity giving ∇J​(Θ)=∇ΘH0​(Θ,a⋆)\nabla J(\Theta)=\nabla_{\Theta}H_{0}(\Theta,a^{\star}),

‖∇ΘH0​(Θ,a~)−∇J​(Θ)‖≤L​ϵ/μ.\|\nabla_{\Theta}H_{0}(\Theta,\widetilde{a})-\nabla J(\Theta)\|\leq L\epsilon/\mu.

These bounds turn numerical stopping tolerances into objective and gradient certificates.

Summable certification error.

Let QkQ_{k} be an approximate exactified surrogate at anchor Θk\Theta^{k} and write rk=Qk−Jr_{k}=Q_{k}-J. Suppose an accepted candidate satisfies

Qk​(Θk+1)≤Qk​(Θk)−Δk,rk​(Θk+1)−rk​(Θk)≥−ηk​Δk−εk,Q_{k}(\Theta^{k+1})\leq Q_{k}(\Theta^{k})-\Delta_{k},\qquad r_{k}(\Theta^{k+1})-r_{k}(\Theta^{k})\geq-\eta_{k}\Delta_{k}-\varepsilon_{k},

where Δk≥0\Delta_{k}\geq 0, 0≤ηk<10\leq\eta_{k}<1, and εk≥0\varepsilon_{k}\geq 0. If JJ is bounded below, supkηk<1\sup_{k}\eta_{k}<1, ∑kεk<∞\sum_{k}\varepsilon_{k}<\infty, and

Δk≥c​‖Θk+1−Θk‖2for some ​c>0,\Delta_{k}\geq c\|\Theta^{k+1}-\Theta^{k}\|^{2}\quad\text{for some }c>0,

then ∑kΔk<∞\sum_{k}\Delta_{k}<\infty and

∑k‖Θk+1−Θk‖2<∞.\sum_{k}\|\Theta^{k+1}-\Theta^{k}\|^{2}<\infty.

For the stationary-point conclusion, additionally assume

‖∇rk​(Θk)‖≤δk→0,‖∇Qk​(Θk+1)‖≤ζk→0,\|\nabla r_{k}(\Theta^{k})\|\leq\delta_{k}\to 0,\qquad\|\nabla Q_{k}(\Theta^{k+1})\|\leq\zeta_{k}\to 0,

and that ∇Qk\nabla Q_{k} is KK-Lipschitz on the segment from Θk\Theta^{k} to Θk+1\Theta^{k+1}, uniformly in kk. Then

‖∇J​(Θk)‖≤K​‖Θk+1−Θk‖+ζk+δk⟶0.\|\nabla J(\Theta^{k})\|\leq K\|\Theta^{k+1}-\Theta^{k}\|+\zeta_{k}+\delta_{k}\longrightarrow 0.

If ∇J\nabla J is continuous, every cluster point is stationary for JJ. Compactness or level boundedness is needed only to guarantee that cluster points exist.

Conjugate transmission.

For the conjugate lift

H0​(Θ,A)=c⁡(Θ)+Φ⁡(A)−⟨A,η⁡(Θ)⟩,H_{0}(\Theta,A)=c(\Theta)+\Phi(A)-\langle A,\eta(\Theta)\rangle,

let QX,A(k)Q_{X,A}^{(k)} and QX,B(k)Q_{X,B}^{(k)} be the canonical exactifications obtained by freezing AA and BB. Direct cancellation gives the transmission identity

QX,A(k)−QX,B(k)=−⟨A−B,η−Tk​η⟩.Q_{X,A}^{(k)}-Q_{X,B}^{(k)}=-\langle A-B,\eta-T_{k}\eta\rangle.

Thus, for k=1k=1, their Hessians at the anchor differ by −⟨A−B,D2​η​(Θ¯)⟩-\langle A-B,D^{2}\eta(\bar{\Theta})\rangle. If the natural-parameter map η\eta is affine, the Taylor tail vanishes and no nonlinear curvature is transmitted. This is the conjugate-transmission calculation in the companion framework (Huang and Wang, 2026f).

7.4 Practical algorithm

The preceding error bounds become an implementable outer loop only when the acceptance test keeps the inner-oracle, defect-score, and outer-solver budgets separate. The algorithm records that interface.

The algorithm separates three tolerances: inner-oracle error, defect-score error, and outer minimization error. Collapsing them into one generic tolerance obscures the proof.
