Appendix to Chapter 7: complete proofs

Proof of jet exactification

Dependencies. The frozen defect dd and target JJ are CkC^{k} on a neighborhood of the anchor. The proof then uses only the defining derivative identities of the order-kk Taylor polynomial; no convexity, majorization, or optimization assumption is required.

Proof.

Let Rk​(Θ)=d⁡(Θ)−Tk​d​(Θ,Θ¯)R_{k}(\Theta)=d(\Theta)-T_{k}d(\Theta;\bar{\Theta}). By the defining property of the Taylor polynomial, for every multi-index α\alpha with |α|≤k|\alpha|\leq k,

∂αRk​(Θ¯)=0.\partial^{\alpha}R_{k}(\bar{\Theta})=0.

Since

QX(k)​(Θ∣Θ¯)=J⁡(Θ)+Rk​(Θ),Q_{X}^{(k)}(\Theta\mid\bar{\Theta})=J(\Theta)+R_{k}(\Theta),

all derivatives of QX(k)−JQ_{X}^{(k)}-J through order kk vanish at Θ¯\bar{\Theta}. Hence jΘ¯k​QX(k)=jΘ¯k​Jj_{\bar{\Theta}}^{k}Q_{X}^{(k)}=j_{\bar{\Theta}}^{k}J. For k=1k=1, the zeroth- and first-order identities are precisely

QX​(Θ¯∣Θ¯)=J⁡(Θ¯),∇QX​(Θ¯∣Θ¯)=∇J​(Θ¯).Q_{X}(\bar{\Theta}\mid\bar{\Theta})=J(\bar{\Theta}),\qquad\nabla Q_{X}(\bar{\Theta}\mid\bar{\Theta})=\nabla J(\bar{\Theta}).

∎

Proof of the converse exactification normal form

Dependencies. All functions are CkC^{k} on a neighborhood of the anchor. The conclusion is local: it identifies the correction jet and a canonical representative, uniquely only modulo a kk-flat remainder.

Proof.

From

Q−J=d−c+SQ-J=d-c+S

we obtain

jΘ¯kQ=jΘ¯kJ⟺jΘ¯k(d−c+S)=0.j_{\bar{\Theta}}^{k}Q=j_{\bar{\Theta}}^{k}J\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad j_{\bar{\Theta}}^{k}(d-c+S)=0.

Linearity of the jet operator gives

jΘ¯k(d−c+S)=0⟺jΘ¯k(c−S)=jΘ¯kd.j_{\bar{\Theta}}^{k}(d-c+S)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad j_{\bar{\Theta}}^{k}(c-S)=j_{\bar{\Theta}}^{k}d.

This proves both directions. Because Tk​dT_{k}d has the same kk-jet as dd, the difference

Q−{H0​(Θ,A~)−Tk​d​(Θ,Θ¯)}=−c+S+Tk​dQ-\{H_{0}(\Theta,\widetilde{A})-T_{k}d(\Theta;\bar{\Theta})\}=-c+S+T_{k}d

is kk-flat whenever the target-jet condition holds. Conversely, adding any kk-flat remainder to the canonical representative leaves the target kk-jet unchanged. This proves the claimed local uniqueness modulo kk-flat terms. ∎

Chapter 8 Probability Validity, Graph Smoothing, and CRPS

The native statistical loss is the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS), whose expected excess equals squared L2​(I)L^{2}(I) distance between the forecast and true CDFs in the compact-support setup declared below.

Let G=(V,E)G=(V,E) be a graph with T=|V|T=|V| and Laplacian LL. Vertex tt has distribution function Ft⋆F_{t}^{\star} and observations Yt​1,…,Yt​ntY_{t1},\ldots,Y_{tn_{t}}. Throughout this chapter’s projection and risk statements, outcomes are supported on a declared compact interval I=[a,b]I=[a,b]. Put

ℍ=L2​(I),𝒞cdf={F∈ℍ:0≤F≤1​ and F is nondecreasing a.e.}.\mathbb{H}=L^{2}(I),\qquad\mathcal{C}_{\rm cdf}=\{F\in\mathbb{H}:0\leq F\leq 1\text{ and $F$ is nondecreasing a.e.}\}.

Choose right-continuous representatives with F⁡(b)=1F(b)=1, extended by zero to the left of aa and by one to the right of bb. Then 𝒞cdf\mathcal{C}_{\rm cdf} is the nonempty closed convex set of CDF restrictions in ℍ\mathbb{H}. The empirical CDF restriction is

F^t(y)=1nt∑i=1nt𝟏{Yt​i≤y}.\widehat{F}_{t}(y)=\frac{1}{n_{t}}\sum_{i=1}^{n_{t}}\mathbf{1}\{Y_{ti}\leq y\}.

Stack the CDFs as a vector-valued function F^​(y)∈ℝT\widehat{F}(y)\in\mathbb{R}^{T}.

For a self-adjoint graph filter SS, define the raw estimator

F~​(y)=S​F^​(y).\widetilde{F}(y)=S\widehat{F}(y).

A higher-order Richardson filter can cancel low-order bias but may use signed weights. The raw coordinates may then fail monotonicity or leave [0,1][0,1].

8.1 The CDF set and projection repair

Let 𝒞=𝒞cdfT⊂ℍT\mathcal{C}=\mathcal{C}_{\rm cdf}^{T}\subset\mathbb{H}^{T}, and let 𝚷cdf\bm{\Pi}_{\rm cdf} be its coordinatewise metric projection. Define

F=𝚷cdf​(F~)=Π𝒞​(F~).F=\bm{\Pi}_{\rm cdf}(\widetilde{F})=\Pi_{\mathcal{C}}(\widetilde{F}).

On an unbounded outcome space, one must instead formulate the argument in an affine L2L^{2}-difference class under suitable moment conditions; no L2​(ℝ)L^{2}(\mathbb{R}) membership of each individual CDF is asserted here.

Proposition 8.1 (Validity repair).

For every true CDF field F⋆∈𝒞F^{\star}\in\mathcal{C},

‖F−F⋆‖2≤‖F~−F⋆‖2.\|F-F^{\star}\|^{2}\leq\|\widetilde{F}-F^{\star}\|^{2}.

For the coordinatewise product projection above, graph roughness also satisfies

⟨F,L​F⟩≤⟨F~,L​F~⟩.\langle F,LF\rangle\leq\langle\widetilde{F},L\widetilde{F}\rangle.

In the P/G/X/V/C calculus of Chapter 6, the repaired field is a G construction: an ambient proposal followed by a validity interface. It is not generally equal to the V solution obtained by minimizing a penalized objective directly over 𝒞\mathcal{C}.

8.2 CRPS risk and its observable decomposition

CRPS as squared-CDF risk.

For a forecast CDF FF and observation YY, the usual real-line CRPS integral reduces, under the support convention above, to

CRPS⁡(F,Y)=∫I{F⁡(y)−𝟏​(Y≤y)}2​𝑑y.\operatorname{CRPS}(F,Y)=\int_{I}\{F(y)-\mathbf{1}(Y\leq y)\}^{2}\,\mathrm{d}y.

Its expected excess risk is

𝔼​CRPS⁡(F,Y)−𝔼​CRPS⁡(F⋆,Y)=∫I{F⁡(y)−F⋆​(y)}2​𝑑y.\mathbb{E}\operatorname{CRPS}(F,Y)-\mathbb{E}\operatorname{CRPS}(F^{\star},Y)=\int_{I}\{F(y)-F^{\star}(y)\}^{2}\,\mathrm{d}y.

The continuous-distribution scoring-rule lineage and the strict-propriety framework are classical (Matheson and Winkler, 1976; Gneiting and Raftery, 2007). What is specific here is the probability-valid graph repair and its matching rate analysis. The displayed identity implies that the Hilbert projection repair cannot increase excess CRPS.

Exact bias–variance decomposition.

Assume that observations are i.i.d. within each vertex and that the samples are independent across vertices. Let B=(S−I)​F⋆B=(S-I)F^{\star} be the smoothing bias. Then

F~−F⋆=B+S⁡(F^−F⋆).\widetilde{F}-F^{\star}=B+S(\widehat{F}-F^{\star}).

The cross term vanishes after expectation, giving

𝔼​‖F~−F⋆‖2=‖B‖2+∑t=1T(S2)t​t​κtnt,\mathbb{E}\|\widetilde{F}-F^{\star}\|^{2}=\|B\|^{2}+\sum_{t=1}^{T}(S^{2})_{tt}\frac{\kappa_{t}}{n_{t}},

where

κt=∫IFt⋆​(y)​{1−Ft⋆​(y)}​𝑑y.\kappa_{t}=\int_{I}F_{t}^{\star}(y)\{1-F_{t}^{\star}(y)\}\,\mathrm{d}y.

The variance complexity is therefore controlled by

tr⁡(S2),\operatorname{tr}(S^{2}),

not merely by tr⁡(S)\operatorname{tr}(S).

An observable raw-risk estimate.

For a fixed data-independent filter, pairwise empirical-CDF identities yield an unbiased estimate of the raw risk after correcting the diagonal self-influence. The correction involves 2​St​t−12S_{tt}-1. The nonlinear projection then provides the pathwise Pythagorean bound

‖F−F⋆‖2+‖F~−F‖2≤‖F~−F⋆‖2.\|F-F^{\star}\|^{2}+\|\widetilde{F}-F\|^{2}\leq\|\widetilde{F}-F^{\star}\|^{2}.

Thus ‖F~−F‖2\|\widetilde{F}-F\|^{2} is an observable guaranteed deduction from the raw squared error. The raw estimator can therefore be tuned using an exact risk decomposition while the final projection restores validity.

8.3 The probability-validity barrier

Projection repairs a raw forecast after it has left the CDF set. A sharper question is when the ambient linear filter preserves probability validity without repair. The source box fixes the provenance and scope of that classification and of the path-rate result used in the next section.

Within that scope, suppose the ambient V filter is

S=(I+λ​ψ​(L))−1.S=(I+\lambda\psi(L))^{-1}.

Here ψ:[0,∞)→[0,∞)\psi:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty) and ψ⁡(0)=0\psi(0)=0; the latter condition is the spectral mass-preservation gate. A positive-semidefinite contraction need not be entrywise nonnegative or mass preserving. Graph-universal Markov validity requires the generator ψ⁡(L)\psi(L) to be a graph Laplacian for every weighted graph.

Every Bernstein function with ψ⁡(0)=0\psi(0)=0 satisfies this Laplacian gate, possibly producing a dense graph; this uses the classical link among Bernstein functions, matrix functions, and graph generators (Schilling et al., 2012; Micchelli and Willoughby, 1979; Gregorio and Mugnolo, 2020). If exact kernel preservation on every connected graph is also required, assume in addition that ψ⁡(x)>0\psi(x)>0 for x>0x>0. In particular,

(I+λ​Lν)−1(I+\lambda L^{\nu})^{-1}

is Markov for every finite weighted graph and every λ>0\lambda>0 exactly when

0<ν≤1.0<\nu\leq 1.

For ν>1\nu>1, a weighted three-node path produces a negative entry for a range of λ\lambda. Likewise, among real polynomials ψ\psi with ψ⁡(0)=0\psi(0)=0, the only graph-universally valid spectral penalties are nonnegative multiples of LL.

This barrier applies to linear probability-preserving mechanisms. It does not rule out nonlinear projection repair.

8.4 Sharp path rates

On a growing path, suppose the graph-source smoothness is s>0s>0 and a Richardson filter has integer qualification m≥sm\geq s. With calibrated bandwidth, the repaired forecast attains average excess CRPS

N−1+R2/(4​s+1)N−4s/(4s+1),N=nT,N^{-1}+R^{2/(4s+1)}N^{-4s/(4s+1)},\qquad N=nT,

in the stated regime. An embedded Bernoulli experiment gives a matching lower bound.

The rate has two pieces. The N−1N^{-1} term reflects the graph nullspace or global average. The nonparametric term balances spectral bias and effective dimension.

The broader design principle.

The example suggests a general workflow for constrained statistical objects:

high-order ambient proposal\displaystyle\text{high-order ambient proposal} ⟶diagnose semantic invalidity\displaystyle\longrightarrow\text{diagnose semantic invalidity}
⟶nonlinear validity repair\displaystyle\longrightarrow\text{nonlinear validity repair}
⟶risk and rate certificate.\displaystyle\longrightarrow\text{risk and rate certificate}.

The workflow is relevant to covariance matrices, densities, quantiles, stochastic matrices, projectors, and other shape-constrained outputs, but each case requires its own projection and loss geometry.

Proof of validity repair

Dependencies. The first assertion uses the Hilbert-space projection theorem. The graph-roughness assertion additionally uses coordinatewise nonexpansiveness of the projection and the edge representation of the graph Dirichlet form.

Proof.

Let P=Π𝒞P=\Pi_{\mathcal{C}} be metric projection onto the nonempty closed convex set 𝒞\mathcal{C}. The projection variational inequality states that

⟨u−P​u,v−P​u⟩≤0(v∈𝒞).\langle u-Pu,v-Pu\rangle\leq 0\qquad(v\in\mathcal{C}).

Taking u=F~u=\widetilde{F} and v=F⋆v=F^{\star} and expanding the square gives

‖F~−F⋆‖2\displaystyle\|\widetilde{F}-F^{\star}\|^{2} =‖F~−F‖2+‖F−F⋆‖2+2​⟨F~−F,F−F⋆⟩\displaystyle=\|\widetilde{F}-F\|^{2}+\|F-F^{\star}\|^{2}+2\langle\widetilde{F}-F,F-F^{\star}\rangle
≥‖F−F⋆‖2,\displaystyle\geq\|F-F^{\star}\|^{2},

For the graph claim, write the weighted Dirichlet form as

⟨G,L​G⟩=12​∑u,vwu​v​‖Gu−Gv‖ℍ2.\langle G,LG\rangle=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{u,v}w_{uv}\|G_{u}-G_{v}\|_{\mathbb{H}}^{2}.

‖P0​(F~u)−P0​(F~v)‖ℍ≤‖F~u−F~v‖ℍ.\|P_{0}(\widetilde{F}_{u})-P_{0}(\widetilde{F}_{v})\|_{\mathbb{H}}\leq\|\widetilde{F}_{u}-\widetilde{F}_{v}\|_{\mathbb{H}}.

Squaring, multiplying by wu​v/2w_{uv}/2, and summing over edges yields

⟨F,L​F⟩≤⟨F~,L​F~⟩.\langle F,LF\rangle\leq\langle\widetilde{F},L\widetilde{F}\rangle.

Part II Historical and Conceptual Notes

Classical engines

Part II uses four mature mathematical mechanisms. Fenchel–Young equality produces Bregman divergences (Bregman, 1967; Rockafellar, 1970); infimal composition is Bellman/min-plus algebra (Bellman, 1957; Baccelli et al., 1992); Taylor subtraction produces a touching jet and is adjacent to first-order surrogate methodology (Mairal, 2013); and metric projection onto a convex CDF set gives the validity-repair contraction. CRPS as squared-CDF risk and its propriety are likewise established (Matheson and Winkler, 1976; Gneiting and Raftery, 2007).

Book object Classical core Elimination-calculus use
Conjugate defect Fenchel–Bregman identity the eliminated objective fixes the loss units and the direction of an asymmetric divergence
Obstruction tower infimal convolution and dynamic programming intermediate states are typed and every stage cost is read as an objective-generated tax
Exactification Taylor touching and surrogate correction the subtracted jet is the actual frozen insertion defect; the converse is stated modulo a flat remainder within that class
CDF repair Hilbert projection and nonexpansiveness validity is restored without increasing squared-CDF/CRPS risk or the declared graph roughness
What is and is not claimed

The conjugate identity, tower associativity, jet-matching calculation, and projection inequalities are not claimed as new classical mathematics. The program-specific layer is the insistence that a defect be generated by the same elimination as the target, that transformations preserve its units and orientation, and that target-jet preservation be audited against that exact defect. The converse exactification normal form is recorded as a source- program claimed increment, not as an exhaustive priority assertion.

Part III Validity of Defects and Representations
An architecture obstruction is meaningful only when its local defect system is integrable and its carrier is intrinsic to the declared target.

Chapter 9 Integrability, Hodge Repair, and Global Defect Consistency

9.1 When local defect reports may be inconsistent

A complex learning pipeline may eliminate several coordinates in different orders. Local modules can report nonnegative, touching residuals while failing to arise from one global objective. The first structural audit is therefore integrability.

Consider a finite elimination complex whose vertices represent partial eliminations and whose edges represent eliminating one additional coordinate. Let ee assign a reported increment to every oriented edge.

If ee is the gradient of a potential VV,

e=d0​V,e=d_{0}V,

then every path sum between two vertices is the same. Conversely, on a simply connected complex, zero circulation around every elementary face implies path independence. This discrete potential/cycle condition is the same integrability mechanism that underlies exact potential games (Monderer and Shapley, 1996); here the edge quantities are elimination defects rather than unilateral payoffs.

9.2 Square curvature

For the elementary square shown below, e1,e4e_{1},e_{4} form the lower-then-right path and e2,e3e_{2},e_{3} form the left-then-upper path. Define

Ω=e1+e4−e2−e3.\Omega=e_{1}+e_{4}-e_{2}-e_{3}.

A nonzero Ω\Omega measures elimination-order dependence.

Theorem 9.1 (Flat elimination criterion).

On a product-of-stars elimination complex, let a real-valued local increment ej|S​(aS,aj)e_{j\mid S}(a_{S},a_{j}) be given for every S⊆[K]S\subseteq[K] and j∉Sj\notin S. There are potentials VSV_{S} satisfying

ej|S=VS∪{j}−VS,VS​(aS)=infajVS∪{j}​(aS,aj),e_{j\mid S}=V_{S\cup\{j\}}-V_{S},\qquad V_{S}(a_{S})=\inf_{a_{j}}V_{S\cup\{j\}}(a_{S},a_{j}),

if and only if, for every SS, jj, and fixed aSa_{S}, the edge reports are nonnegative with infajej|S​(aS,aj)=0\inf_{a_{j}}e_{j\mid S}(a_{S},a_{j})=0, and every elementary square has zero circulation.

The nonnegativity and fiberwise touching conditions make the potential a certified defect potential rather than an arbitrary scalar potential.

9.3 Approximate flatness and Hodge repair

Approximate flatness.

Two elimination orders differ by adjacent swaps. Every swap crosses one elementary square. Hence the discrepancy between path sums is bounded by the sum of absolute square curvatures along a swap sequence. A Kendall-distance bound follows when a uniform curvature bound is available.

This provides a quantitative diagnostic: small local curvature implies limited order ambiguity, but does not guarantee exact integrability.

Hodge decomposition.

Let C0,C1,C2C^{0},C^{1},C^{2} be weighted cochain spaces with coboundary maps

d0:C0→C1,d1:C1→C2.d_{0}:C^{0}\to C^{1},\qquad d_{1}:C^{1}\to C^{2}.

An observed edge-defect field e∈C1e\in C^{1} decomposes orthogonally as

e=d0​V+d1⋆​ψ+h,e=d_{0}V+d_{1}^{\star}\psi+h,

where

  • •

    d0​Vd_{0}V is exact;

  • •

    d1⋆​ψd_{1}^{\star}\psi carries local curvature;

  • •

    hh is harmonic and carries global periods.

Combinatorial Hodge decompositions have been used to separate gradient, cyclic, and harmonic components of graph data, notably in statistical ranking (Jiang et al., 2011). The present use is narrower and auditable: the cochain is an elimination defect field, and exactness is the condition for a global potential with the declared units and orientation.

The exact and flat projections must be distinguished. The nearest exact defect field is

eex=Pim⁡d0​e=d0​V,e^{\rm ex}=P_{\operatorname{im}d_{0}}e=d_{0}V,

whereas the nearest flat defect field is

efl=Pker⁡d1​e=d0​V+h.e^{\rm fl}=P_{\ker d_{1}}e=d_{0}V+h.

On a contractible elimination complex the harmonic component vanishes and the two projections coincide. On a general complex, local face tests cannot detect hh.

9.4 Repair, falsification, and audit boundaries

Nearest certified repair.

Let Ccert⊆im⁡d0C_{\rm cert}\subseteq\operatorname{im}d_{0} be a declared nonempty closed convex set of exact defect fields satisfying witness constraints. Starting from the exact projection eexe^{\rm ex}, the certified repair is

ecert=PCcert​eex.e_{\rm cert}=P_{C_{\rm cert}}e^{\rm ex}.

Orthogonality gives

‖e−ecert‖W2=‖d1⋆​ψ‖W2+‖h‖W2+‖eex−ecert‖W2.\|e-e_{\rm cert}\|_{W}^{2}=\|d_{1}^{\star}\psi\|_{W}^{2}+\|h\|_{W}^{2}+\|e^{\rm ex}-e_{\rm cert}\|_{W}^{2}.

The three terms are curvature, period, and certification taxes.

Local falsification.

If a square has circulation Ω\Omega, then at least one of its four edge reports must be wrong by at least |Ω|/4|\Omega|/4 under the sup norm. This turns local curvature into a falsification certificate for the collection of local claims.

When integrability must be audited.

Architecture obstruction assumes that the local defect field belongs to one declared objective. This contract is automatic when the defect is derived directly as Hx​(a)−J​(x)H_{x}(a)-J(x) from a single global objective. It is not automatic when local modules report increments that are later assembled into a defect field. In the latter case, optimizing before validation can produce a precise answer to an incoherent question.

This chapter closes the integrability gate before the architecture obstruction results of Part IV are invoked. The logical validation order is

global derivation\displaystyle\text{global derivation} ⟹interpret obstruction,\displaystyle\Longrightarrow\text{interpret obstruction},
assembled defect field\displaystyle\text{assembled defect field} ⟹audit/repair⟹interpret obstruction.\displaystyle\Longrightarrow\text{audit/repair}\Longrightarrow\text{interpret obstruction}.

A reader may postpone the full Hodge repair construction, but any theorem that combines separately reported local increments must either invoke this audit or derive its defect directly from one global objective.

9.4.1 Local generative vector fields under density and transport contracts

Score-based generation supplies a useful contract-sensitive example. If a reported field s:𝒳→ℝds:\mathcal{X}\to\mathbb{R}^{d} is declared to be the score of one positive density,

s​(x)=∇log⁡p​(x),s(x)=\nabla\log p(x),

then, on a simply connected smooth domain, a continuously differentiable field must have symmetric Jacobian:

∂isj=∂jsi.\partial_{i}s_{j}=\partial_{j}s_{i}.

On a domain with holes, vanishing local curl must additionally be supplemented by zero periods around noncontractible loops. An antisymmetric Jacobian entry or a nonzero loop integral is therefore a finite falsification certificate for the declared global density or energy interpretation. Projecting the field onto an exact component, or parameterizing it directly as a scalar-energy gradient, repairs the gradient-consistency part of that contract; the removed coexact and harmonic components are the corresponding integrability taxes. A density claim still requires the exponential potential to be integrable and normalized. This viewpoint is consistent with empirical audits of conservativeness in learned score fields (Chao et al., 2023).

The conclusion changes when the output contract changes. A vector field used only to define a transport ODE or sampler need not be conservative. Nonzero curl alone then does not certify poor samples, invalid transport, or excess native generative loss. The audit must instead use the declared terminal law or transport objective. Thus the same numerical field can fail a global-score contract while remaining admissible under a sampling contract; integrability is a typed obligation, not a model-name diagnosis.

Operational ordering curvature.

Algebraic elimination curvature asks whether two orders produce the same internal defect field. Operational curvature, developed in Chapter 17, asks whether a legal task and context can observe the difference. An internal discrepancy may be operationally invisible; conversely, a context can expose a difference hidden at the base input.

Chapter 10 Lift Admissibility, Slack Factorization, and Complexity

In this chapter, lift admissibility means target-faithfulness of a nonnative lifted representation after slack, minimal-face, quotient, and gauge reduction. This is a representation-level gate. A lift used to support a deployment claim must also pass a second interface: quotient-faithful extraction into a state whose oracle-relevant distinctions are measured in the native defect. The audit therefore proceeds from target slack, through minimal-face and gauge reduction, to deployment extraction; finite auxiliary dimension alone certifies none of these steps.

10.1 Why exact lifts can be vacuous

Given any target objective J⁡(x)J(x) and any chosen field g⁡(x)g(x),

Hg​(x,a)=J⁡(x)+12​‖a−g⁡(x)‖2H_{g}(x,a)=J(x)+\frac{1}{2}\|a-g(x)\|^{2}

is an exact lift. Its oracle is a⋆​(x)=g​(x)a^{\star}(x)=g(x). By choosing gg we can manufacture arbitrary coherence, local metrics, or apparent geometric structure that was not present in the target.

This first observation is analytical: it does not assert that an arbitrary gg has a finite representation in a declared lift grammar. The finite-size statement below therefore restricts gg to an affine field, or more generally to a field whose graph and penalty composition are explicitly representable by that grammar.

A constant gg makes the oracle globally coherent. An affine g⁡(x)=M​x+bg(x)=Mx+b manufactures frozen-oracle metric M⊤​MM^{\top}M. With suitable primitives, arbitrary positive-semidefinite Hessians can be appended at fixed dimension-dependent overhead.

Theorem 10.1 (Finite-complexity target-calling no-go).

Under the preceding conditions, LL has an exact augmentation

HL⁡[g,ψ](x,z,a,s)=HL(x,z)+s+ι{s≥ψ(a−g(x))}H_{L[g,\psi]}(x,z,a,s)=H_{L}(x,z)+s+\iota_{\{s\geq\psi(a-g(x))\}}

of size at most m+cψ​(q)m+c_{\psi}(q), whose appended exact oracle is a⋆​(x)=g​(x)a^{\star}(x)=g(x). The overhead is independent of the coefficients M,bM,b. Consequently a constant gg appends a dummy coherent coordinate; a polyhedral ℓ1\ell_{1} primitive appends any affine field at fixed dimension-dependent overhead; and a quadratic primitive produces frozen-oracle Hessian M⊤​MM^{\top}M, hence any prescribed positive-semidefinite local metric.

10.2 Epigraph geometry and intrinsic lift structure

Thus finite auxiliary dimension or extension size alone does not define lift admissibility. The target-calling no-go and the quotient-faithful lift interface in this chapter come from the Lift Complexity companion (Huang and Wang, 2026i). For a convex objective on a compact domain, consider a truncated epigraph body

KJ={(x,t):x∈X,J(x)≤t≤M}.K_{J}=\{(x,t):x\in X,\ J(x)\leq t\leq M\}.

A proper conic lift of the objective corresponds to an extended formulation of KJK_{J}. The intrinsic target object is the slack operator

SJ​(u,v)=1−⟨u,v⟩S_{J}(u,v)=1-\langle u,v\rangle

after the appropriate normalization of extreme points and supporting functionals.

Classical extension-complexity theory relates lift size to factorization of the slack operator: nonnegative rank governs polyhedral lifts, and cone factorizations extend the principle to semidefinite and other convex lifts (Yannakakis, 1991; Gouveia et al., 2013; Fawzi et al., 2015). Semidefinite hierarchies and extension-complexity lower bounds provide complementary parts of this literature (Lasserre, 2001; Parrilo, 2003; Fiorini et al., 2015; Fiorini et al., 2012).

Theorem 10.2 (Conic lift–factorization gate).

Every proper 𝒦\mathcal{K}-lift of the truncated epigraph induces a 𝒦\mathcal{K}-factorization of its slack operator, and every 𝒦\mathcal{K}-factorization induces a 𝒦\mathcal{K}-lift. A nonproper lift is handled after restriction to the minimal face containing its affine slice. Polyhedral and semidefinite lifts correspond to nonnegative and positive-semidefinite factorizations.

This is the lift–factorization theorem of Gouveia et al. (2013), extending the polyhedral theorem of Yannakakis (1991).

The theorem does not by itself define a useful auxiliary coherence field. It supplies the gate through which lift design must pass.

10.3 Gauge reduction and the fidelity–coherence–complexity frontier

Factorizations are nonunique. Cone automorphisms, duplicated factors, and slack-invisible directions can change raw coordinates without changing the represented objective. A reduced slack carrier removes directions not seen by the target slack operator. A coherence rule is admissible only if it is invariant under cone gauge and faithful under quotient refinement.

Example 10.3 (Factor splitting artifact).

Duplicate each nonnegative factor kk times and divide its weight among copies. A naive Euclidean factor-coherence penalty can decrease by a factor 1/k1/k while the represented convex set is unchanged. On the quotient-reduced carrier the apparent improvement disappears.

Fidelity–coherence–complexity frontier.

For cone family 𝒦\mathcal{K}, size budget mm, coherence budget rr, and one-sided objective-fidelity error δ\delta, define

𝔉J,𝒦​(m,r,δ)\mathfrak{F}_{J,\mathcal{K}}(m,r,\delta)

as the least true objective defect achievable by a quotient-reduced 𝒦\mathcal{K}-lift satisfying the budgets.

The exact-lift frontier is the slice δ=0\delta=0. Approximate lifts introduce a model or formulation bias that must be separated from coupling obstruction.

A deployed lift admits the decomposition

total defect=\displaystyle\text{total defect}={} complexity-limited obstruction\displaystyle\text{complexity-limited obstruction}
+formulation-selection tax\displaystyle+\text{formulation-selection tax}
+within-formulation implementation tax,\displaystyle+\text{within-formulation implementation tax},

under the declared decomposition convention.

10.4 Target-visible reduction and extraction

Slack reduction answers which lift directions belong to the target. It does not yet answer which distinctions in a retained deployment state matter to native defect. In the common-fiber Legendre–Bregman regime there is a second, canonical reduction. Let a⋆a^{\star} be the unique oracle, put

S=∇Φ​(a⋆),SU=𝔼⁡(S∣U),aU†=∇Φ⋆​(SU)S=\nabla\Phi(a^{\star}),\qquad S_{U}=\mathbb{E}(S\mid U),\qquad a_{U}^{\dagger}=\nabla\Phi^{\star}(S_{U})

for a standard-Borel deployment statistic UU, and define

𝒞Φ(U)=𝔼DΦ(aU†∥a⋆)=𝔼DΦ⋆(S∥SU).\mathcal{C}_{\Phi}(U)=\mathbb{E}D_{\Phi}(a_{U}^{\dagger}\|a^{\star})=\mathbb{E}D_{\Phi^{\star}}(S\|S_{U}).

For every factorized deployment a^=q⁡(U)\widehat{a}=q(U), conditional Bregman projection gives the exact defect field

𝔼DΦ(a^∥a⋆)=𝒞Φ(U)+𝔼DΦ(a^∥aU†).\mathbb{E}D_{\Phi}(\widehat{a}\|a^{\star})=\mathcal{C}_{\Phi}(U)+\mathbb{E}D_{\Phi}(\widehat{a}\|a_{U}^{\dagger}). (10.1)

Thus 𝒞Φ​(U)\mathcal{C}_{\Phi}(U) is the native obstruction caused by the carrier, while the second term is a decoder tax. The identity is the classical conditional Bregman predictor decomposition (Banerjee et al., 2005a; Pfau, 2025; Adlam et al., 2022); its use as a canonical quotient of an admissible lift is the additional step here.

Count only distinct conditional dual signatures:

vcΦ⁡(U)=|essran⁡SU|,𝒞Φ​(k)=infvcΦ⁡(U)≤k𝒞Φ​(U).\operatorname{vc}_{\Phi}(U)=\bigl|\operatorname{essran}S_{U}\bigr|,\qquad\mathcal{C}_{\Phi}(k)=\inf_{\operatorname{vc}_{\Phi}(U)\leq k}\mathcal{C}_{\Phi}(U).

Raw labels inducing the same SUS_{U} therefore consume one visible state, not several. For finitely many separated oracle types, this is the ordinary Bregman quantization frontier and is positive below the number of distinct types.

Theorem 10.4 (Visible quotient and lift-to-carrier transfer).

Let RU=SUR_{U}=S_{U}. Then RUR_{U} is a quotient of UU,

𝔼⁡(S∣RU)=RU,𝒞Φ​(RU)=𝒞Φ​(U).\mathbb{E}(S\mid R_{U})=R_{U},\qquad\mathcal{C}_{\Phi}(R_{U})=\mathcal{C}_{\Phi}(U).

If VV is a coarsening of UU and both 𝒞Φ​(U),𝒞Φ​(V)<∞\mathcal{C}_{\Phi}(U),\mathcal{C}_{\Phi}(V)<\infty, then

𝒞Φ​(V)−𝒞Φ​(U)\displaystyle\mathcal{C}_{\Phi}(V)-\mathcal{C}_{\Phi}(U) =𝔼DΦ⋆(SU∥SV)\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}D_{\Phi^{\star}}(S_{U}\|S_{V}) (10.2)
=𝔼DΦ(aV†∥aU†)≥0,\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}D_{\Phi}(a_{V}^{\dagger}\|a_{U}^{\dagger})\geq 0,

with equality exactly when SU=SVS_{U}=S_{V} almost surely. Hence σ⁡(RU)\sigma(R_{U}) is, modulo null sets, the coarsest quotient of UU preserving optimal native defect.

Suppose, in addition, that every quotient-reduced exact lift of size at most mm and every deployment of coherence at most rr admits the declared extraction and satisfies

true defect≥c𝔼DΦ(a^L,z∥a⋆),vcΦ(UL,z)≤κ𝒦(m,r).\text{true defect}\geq c\,\mathbb{E}D_{\Phi}(\widehat{a}_{L,z}\|a^{\star}),\qquad\operatorname{vc}_{\Phi}(U_{L,z})\leq\kappa_{\mathcal{K}}(m,r).

Then the exact lift frontier obeys

𝔉J,𝒦​(m,r,0)≥c​𝒞Φ​(κ𝒦​(m,r)).\mathfrak{F}_{J,\mathcal{K}}(m,r,0)\geq c\,\mathcal{C}_{\Phi}\!\left(\kappa_{\mathcal{K}}(m,r)\right). (10.3)

The upgraded lift chain can therefore be read as

(m,r)→quotient-faithful extractionκ𝒦​(m,r)→visible Bregman frontierc​𝒞Φ​(κ𝒦​(m,r)).(m,r)\xrightarrow{\text{quotient-faithful extraction}}\kappa_{\mathcal{K}}(m,r)\xrightarrow{\text{visible Bregman frontier}}c\,\mathcal{C}_{\Phi}\!\left(\kappa_{\mathcal{K}}(m,r)\right).

Chapter 16 starts after such a deployment carrier has been declared or extracted and separates its information loss from decoder nonsaturation.

10.5 From lift size to native defect

Scaling obstruction.

Positive rescaling of the objective preserves extension size while rescaling the native defect. Therefore extension size cannot be a universal defect scale. Complexity and objective loss live in different units until an exchange theorem is supplied.

Barrier-to-defect exchange.

For a fixed encoded, well-conditioned conic lift with a self-concordant barrier, a primal–dual gap provides an objective defect certificate. Iteration complexity depends on:

  • •

    barrier parameter;

  • •

    coefficient encoding length;

  • •

    conditioning;

  • •

    cone-oracle cost;

  • •

    per-iteration linear algebra;

  • •

    requested numerical accuracy.

Relationship to architecture obstruction.

When an obstruction argument uses a nonnative lift, lift complexity answers a logically earlier question than EOT or COT: do the auxiliary states arise from an intrinsic factorization of the target rather than an arbitrary appended coordinate? Native auxiliary states require no separate lift audit, and a lift whose target-faithfulness follows by construction has already discharged the gate.

This chapter closes the target-faithfulness gate before nonnative lifts are used in the architecture-obstruction results of Part IV. The logical order is

target epigraph and slack\displaystyle\text{target epigraph and slack} ⟶reduced admissible carrier\displaystyle\longrightarrow\text{reduced admissible carrier}
⟶coherence grammar\displaystyle\longrightarrow\text{coherence grammar}
⟶architecture obstruction.\displaystyle\longrightarrow\text{architecture obstruction}.

Proof of the finite-complexity target-calling no-go

Dependencies. The cone dictionary must represent the epigraph of the declared penalty primitive with fixed overhead and must be stable under products. The oracle map is affine so that its graph can be imposed by affine formulation constraints. A nonaffine field is covered only if the declared grammar separately represents its graph and the composed epigraph with the claimed overhead.

Proof.

Let the original exact lift be represented by auxiliary variable zz and objective HL​(x,z)H_{L}(x,z), so that

infzHL​(x,z)=J⁡(x).\inf_{z}H_{L}(x,z)=J(x).

Append variables a∈ℝqa\in\mathbb{R}^{q} and s∈ℝs\in\mathbb{R}, together with the representable epigraph constraint

s≥ψ​{a−g⁡(x)}.s\geq\psi\{a-g(x)\}.

The enlarged lifted objective is

HL⁡[g,ψ](x,z,a,s)=HL(x,z)+s+ι{s≥ψ(a−g(x))}.H_{L[g,\psi]}(x,z,a,s)=H_{L}(x,z)+s+\iota_{\{s\geq\psi(a-g(x))\}}.

Because ψ≥0\psi\geq 0 and vanishes only at zero,

infa,s{s:s≥ψ⁡(a−g⁡(x))}=0,\inf_{a,s}\{s:s\geq\psi(a-g(x))\}=0,

and the infimum is attained uniquely at a=g⁡(x)a=g(x) and s=0s=0. Eliminating first (a,s)(a,s) and then zz therefore returns J⁡(x)J(x), so the enlarged formulation is exact. Product stability of the cone dictionary adds at most the fixed representation cost cψ​(q)c_{\psi}(q), proving the size bound.

If gg is constant, the appended exact oracle is constant. If ψ=∥⋅∥1\psi=\|\cdot\|_{1}, any affine field is appended with polyhedral overhead depending only on qq. If ψ⁡(v)=12​‖v‖22\psi(v)=\frac{1}{2}\|v\|_{2}^{2} and the auxiliary state is frozen at a=g⁡(x0)a=g(x_{0}), then

12​‖g⁡(x0)−g⁡(x)‖2=12​‖M⁡(x−x0)‖2=12​(x−x0)⊤​M⊤​M​(x−x0).\frac{1}{2}\|g(x_{0})-g(x)\|^{2}=\frac{1}{2}\|M(x-x_{0})\|^{2}=\frac{1}{2}(x-x_{0})^{\top}M^{\top}M(x-x_{0}).

Its Hessian is M⊤​MM^{\top}M. Every positive semidefinite matrix has such a factorization, establishing the final claim. ∎

Proof of the conic lift–factorization gate

Dependencies. The body is full dimensional, compact, and affinely normalized with the origin in its interior. Properness ensures conic dual certificates on the ambient cone; a nonproper lift is first restricted to its minimal face.

We give the standard lift–factorization construction. Suppose first that

C=π⁡(K∩L)C=\pi(K\cap L)

is a proper KK-lift, where LL is an affine subspace meeting int⁡K\operatorname{int}K. For every extreme point x∈Cx\in C, choose a lifted representative A⁡(x)∈K∩LA(x)\in K\cap L with π​A​(x)=x\pi A(x)=x. For every u∈ext⁡(C∘)u\in\operatorname{ext}(C^{\circ}), the inequality

⟨u,x⟩≤1\langle u,x\rangle\leq 1

is valid on the projection. Conic strong duality for the proper slice supplies a dual vector B⁡(u)∈K∗B(u)\in K^{\ast} whose pairing with any lifted feasible point equals the slack of that inequality. In particular,

1−⟨u,x⟩=⟨A⁡(x),B⁡(u)⟩.1-\langle u,x\rangle=\langle A(x),B(u)\rangle.

Thus the intrinsic slack operator has a KK-factorization.

Conversely, suppose maps

A:ext⁡(C)→K,B:ext⁡(C∘)→K∗A:\operatorname{ext}(C)\to K,\qquad B:\operatorname{ext}(C^{\circ})\to K^{\ast}

satisfy

1−⟨u,x⟩=⟨A⁡(x),B⁡(u)⟩.1-\langle u,x\rangle=\langle A(x),B(u)\rangle.

⟨z,B⁡(u)⟩=1−⟨u,x⟩for every ​u∈ext⁡(C∘),z∈K.\langle z,B(u)\rangle=1-\langle u,x\rangle\quad\text{for every }u\in\operatorname{ext}(C^{\circ}),\qquad z\in K.

Every extreme point xx of CC has feasible witness z=A⁡(x)z=A(x), and convexity supplies witnesses for all of CC. Conversely, if (x,z)(x,z) satisfies the displayed system, then

1−⟨u,x⟩=⟨z,B⁡(u)⟩≥01-\langle u,x\rangle=\langle z,B(u)\rangle\geq 0

for every extreme point of C∘C^{\circ}, hence for every u∈C∘u\in C^{\circ}. By the bipolar theorem, x∈Cx\in C. Therefore the projection of this affine slice of KK is exactly CC.

If the original lift is not proper, intersect KK with the minimal face containing the affine slice. The slice is proper relative to that face, and the same argument applies there. ∎

Proof of the visible quotient and lift-to-carrier transfer

Dependencies. The conditional Bregman decomposition uses the common-fiber Legendre assumptions stated in the chapter. Doob–Dynkin is applied to the standard-Borel statistic UU. The frontier conclusion additionally uses the declared quotient-faithful extraction, native exchange, and capacity bound; none is inferred from cone order.

Proof.

The random variable RU=SUR_{U}=S_{U} is a measurable function of UU. Since it is also RUR_{U}-measurable, the tower property gives

𝔼⁡(S∣RU)=𝔼⁡{𝔼⁡(S∣U)∣RU}=RU.\mathbb{E}(S\mid R_{U})=\mathbb{E}\{\mathbb{E}(S\mid U)\mid R_{U}\}=R_{U}.

Substitution in the dual expression for 𝒞Φ\mathcal{C}_{\Phi} shows that 𝒞Φ​(RU)=𝒞Φ​(U)\mathcal{C}_{\Phi}(R_{U})=\mathcal{C}_{\Phi}(U).

If σ⁡(V)⊆σ⁡(U)\sigma(V)\subseteq\sigma(U), then SV=𝔼⁡(SU∣V)S_{V}=\mathbb{E}(S_{U}\mid V). The conditional Bregman predictor identity, now in dual coordinates, yields

𝔼DΦ⋆(S∥SV)=𝔼DΦ⋆(S∥SU)+𝔼DΦ⋆(SU∥SV).\mathbb{E}D_{\Phi^{\star}}(S\|S_{V})=\mathbb{E}D_{\Phi^{\star}}(S\|S_{U})+\mathbb{E}D_{\Phi^{\star}}(S_{U}\|S_{V}).

Legendre duality converts the last term to 𝔼DΦ(aV†∥aU†)\mathbb{E}D_{\Phi}(a_{V}^{\dagger}\|a_{U}^{\dagger}). Strict convexity makes it zero exactly when SU=SVS_{U}=S_{V} almost surely. Any defect-preserving coarsening must therefore retain SUS_{U}, proving the coarsest-quotient claim modulo null sets.

Finally fix a deployment counted by 𝔉J,𝒦​(m,r,0)\mathfrak{F}_{J,\mathcal{K}}(m,r,0). Its factorized extraction and (10.1) imply

true defect≥c𝔼DΦ(a^L,z∥a⋆)≥c𝒞Φ(UL,z)≥c𝒞Φ(κ𝒦(m,r)).\text{true defect}\geq c\,\mathbb{E}D_{\Phi}(\widehat{a}_{L,z}\|a^{\star})\geq c\,\mathcal{C}_{\Phi}(U_{L,z})\geq c\,\mathcal{C}_{\Phi}\!\left(\kappa_{\mathcal{K}}(m,r)\right).

The last inequality is the definition of the visible-capacity frontier. Taking the infimum over all exact deployments proves (10.3). ∎

Part III Historical and Conceptual Notes

Two different validity questions

The Part separates an integrability question from a representation question. Cycle-flat edge data are gradients of a potential under familiar discrete integrability conditions, as in exact potential games and combinatorial Hodge theory (Monderer and Shapley, 1996; Jiang et al., 2011). Separately, a convex lift is intrinsic only when it factors the target slack operator: the polyhedral equivalence is due to Yannakakis (1991), and the general closed-cone equivalence to Gouveia et al. (2013).

These are not interchangeable audits. A perfectly integrable local defect field can be attached to a target-calling auxiliary coordinate; a valid slack factorization can still carry duplicated or gauge directions whose raw coherence has no target meaning.

Gate Established antecedent Part III increment or specialization
Flatness potential/cycle tests adds nonnegativity and fiberwise touching so the potential is a partial-minimum elimination tower
Lift admissibility slack-factorization/extension complexity imports the classical iff theorem as a gate and removes minimal-face and gauge artifacts
Target-calling no-go exact augmentation by representable penalties elementary diagnostic specialization showing why size alone is not admissibility
Visible quotient conditional Bregman prediction (Banerjee et al., 2005a) retains only conditional dual signatures and then requires an explicit resource-to-carrier extraction theorem

The conic lift–factorization theorem is therefore explicitly classical. The finite target-calling no-go and the quotient/extraction bridge are the Part’s program-specific claims, with the qualified priority statuses stated in Appendix G.1.

Part IV Structural Obstructions under Shared Deployment
A shared deployment contract turns local optimization into a global compatibility problem. Regularity, coordination, and singularity impose different structural limits and call for mechanism-matched repairs.

Chapter 11 Architecture Obstruction as a Second Elimination

11.1 From a local defect to a class-level floor

Once the native defect is fixed, architecture design becomes another optimization problem. Throughout Part IV, that defect is assumed either to be derived directly from one declared global objective or to come with an integrable local defect system. Any nonnative lifted carrier is assumed to satisfy the target-faithfulness gate. Chapters 9 and 10 audit these conditions retrospectively when they are not guaranteed by construction.

For a population law PP and architecture class 𝔄\mathfrak{A},

𝔒P​(𝔄)=infA∈𝔄𝔼P​𝖣X​{A⁡(X)}.\mathfrak{O}_{P}(\mathfrak{A})=\inf_{A\in\mathfrak{A}}\mathbb{E}_{P}\mathsf{D}_{X}\{A(X)\}.

This is a second elimination: the first eliminates the local auxiliary state at each xx; the second eliminates over globally deployable fields.

Every deployment A∈𝔄A\in\mathfrak{A} has the exact defect field

𝔼P​𝖣X​{A⁡(X)}=𝔒P​(𝔄)+ΔPimpl​(A,𝔄).\mathbb{E}_{P}\mathsf{D}_{X}\{A(X)\}=\mathfrak{O}_{P}(\mathfrak{A})+\Delta^{\mathrm{impl}}_{P}(A;\mathfrak{A}).

The architecture obstruction is a property of the triple

(𝖣,P,𝔄),(\mathsf{D},P,\mathfrak{A}),

not of the architecture alone. Changing the loss, population weighting, or output contract can change the tax.

11.2 Saturation

The first class-level question is whether the second elimination leaves any irreducible defect. The definition distinguishes a zero infimum from its attainment by an exact oracle section.

Definition 11.1 (Saturation).

An architecture class 𝔄\mathfrak{A} is saturated for an oracle family if its obstruction is zero under the declared contract. It is exactly saturated if it contains an exact oracle section.

Saturation is the correct zero-tax condition. Universal approximation in a generic norm is neither necessary nor sufficient without an exchange theorem connecting that norm to the native defect.

Example 11.2 (Quotient saturation).

A vector-valued architecture may be nonsaturated for an eigenline oracle because of sign ambiguity. A projector-valued architecture can be exactly saturated while using no more intrinsic information.

11.3 Architecture comparison and witnesses

If 𝔄1⊆𝔄2\mathfrak{A}_{1}\subseteq\mathfrak{A}_{2}, then

𝔒P​(𝔄2)≤𝔒P​(𝔄1).\mathfrak{O}_{P}(\mathfrak{A}_{2})\leq\mathfrak{O}_{P}(\mathfrak{A}_{1}).

But a larger class can have worse generalization or optimization behavior. The structural comparison isolates only the irreducible floor.

For a resource-indexed family {𝔄r:r≥0}\{\mathfrak{A}_{r}:r\geq 0\} with 𝔄r⊆𝔄r′\mathfrak{A}_{r}\subseteq\mathfrak{A}_{r^{\prime}} for r≤r′r\leq r^{\prime}, the frontier

r⟼𝔒P​(𝔄r)r\longmapsto\mathfrak{O}_{P}(\mathfrak{A}_{r})

is nonincreasing. Plateaus identify ranges in which additional resources do not change realizability.

Lower and upper architecture witnesses.

The same native defect supports both directions of the theory: a concrete deployment gives a constructive upper witness, while a flow, topological, resource, or information argument gives a converse lower certificate; together, the two should bracket the obstruction.

Lower witness.

A dual flow, topological argument, resource counting theorem, or information contraction gives

𝔒¯≤𝔒P​(𝔄).\underline{\mathfrak{O}}\leq\mathfrak{O}_{P}(\mathfrak{A}).
Upper witness.

An explicit deployment Awit∈𝔄A_{\rm wit}\in\mathfrak{A} gives

𝔒P​(𝔄)≤𝔼P​𝖣X​{Awit​(X)}.\mathfrak{O}_{P}(\mathfrak{A})\leq\mathbb{E}_{P}\mathsf{D}_{X}\{A_{\rm wit}(X)\}.

A sharp theory seeks matching witnesses. Even when they do not match, the gap is itself an auditable unresolved region.

11.4 Architecture obstruction versus approximation and optimization

Classical approximation theory studies

inff∈ℱ‖f−f⋆‖.\inf_{f\in\mathcal{F}}\|f-f^{\star}\|.

Architecture obstruction differs in four ways.

  1. 1.

    The target may be a fiber, orbit, or set rather than one function.

  2. 2.

    The error loss scale is generated by an eliminated objective.

  3. 3.

    The architecture contract may include sharing, memory, topology, and output semantics.

  4. 4.

    The obstruction may disappear under a quotient or atlas without enlarging ordinary function capacity.

The two theories are complementary. When the oracle is a unique function and the defect is equivalent to a norm, architecture obstruction reduces to a familiar approximation problem.

Architecture obstruction versus optimization.

Suppose a training algorithm returns A^\widehat{A}. A large achieved defect may arise because

ΔPimpl​(A^,𝔄)>0\Delta^{\mathrm{impl}}_{P}(\widehat{A};\mathfrak{A})>0

or because

𝔒P​(𝔄)>0.\mathfrak{O}_{P}(\mathfrak{A})>0.

Training loss alone does not separate the two. One needs a class-level lower certificate and an upper witness.

A particularly strong empirical design compares:

  1. 1.

    more optimization within the baseline class;

  2. 2.

    more parameters within the same contract;

  3. 3.

    a targeted contract change predicted by the obstruction;

  4. 4.

    random or capacity-matched repairs.

11.5 Output, risk, and theorem contracts

The same oracle incidence can have different taxes.

Output contract.

A point, unordered set, orbit, projector, probability law, or charted section are different outputs.

Aggregation contract.

Uniform, average, tail, or task-weighted risk can see different parts of the obstruction.

Regularity contract.

Continuous, measurable, Lipschitz, finite-memory, and neural-parameterized deployments form different classes.

A minimal theorem template.

A complete architecture theorem should contain four clauses.

  1. 1.

    Oracle clause: identify the local oracle set.

  2. 2.

    Obstruction clause: prove a lower bound over the declared architecture.

  3. 3.

    Witness clause: exhibit an architecture or deployment attaining or approaching the bound.

  4. 4.

    Repair clause: identify a contract change that changes the bound, with its own proof.

The regular, coordination, singular, and resource theories in the next chapters instantiate this template.

Chapter 12 Regular Obstruction Transfer and Flow Duality

12.1 The regular regime and quarter transport bound

Assume a unique oracle a⋆​(x)a^{\star}(x) and a defect with local growth

𝖣x​(a)≥μ2​d2​{a,a⋆​(x)}.\mathsf{D}_{x}(a)\geq\frac{\mu}{2}d^{2}\{a,a^{\star}(x)\}.

Let the architecture class consist of LL-Lipschitz maps A:𝖷→𝖠A:\mathsf{X}\to\mathsf{A}. If the oracle field varies faster than LL, the architecture must deviate somewhere.

For two points x,yx,y,

d⁡{A⁡(x),A⁡(y)}≤L​d𝖷​(x,y).d\{A(x),A(y)\}\leq Ld_{\mathsf{X}}(x,y).

By the triangle inequality,

d⁡{a⋆​(x),a⋆​(y)}≤ex+L​d𝖷​(x,y)+ey,d\{a^{\star}(x),a^{\star}(y)\}\leq e_{x}+Ld_{\mathsf{X}}(x,y)+e_{y},

where ex=d⁡{A⁡(x),a⋆​(x)}e_{x}=d\{A(x),a^{\star}(x)\}. Hence

ex+ey≥[d⁡{a⋆​(x),a⋆​(y)}−L​d𝖷​(x,y)]+.e_{x}+e_{y}\geq\bigl[d\{a^{\star}(x),a^{\star}(y)\}-Ld_{\mathsf{X}}(x,y)\bigr]_{+}.

Using u2+v2≥(u+v)2/2u^{2}+v^{2}\geq(u+v)^{2}/2, strong growth gives

𝖣x​{A⁡(x)}+𝖣y​{A⁡(y)}≥μ4​[d⁡{a⋆​(x),a⋆​(y)}−L​d𝖷​(x,y)]+2.\mathsf{D}_{x}\{A(x)\}+\mathsf{D}_{y}\{A(y)\}\geq\frac{\mu}{4}\bigl[d\{a^{\star}(x),a^{\star}(y)\}-Ld_{\mathsf{X}}(x,y)\bigr]_{+}^{2}.

Averaging over selected pairs yields an architecture lower bound.

Theorem 12.1 (Oracle-variation transport bound).

Let Π⁡(P,P)\Pi(P,P) denote the set of couplings of PP with itself. Then

𝔒P​(𝔄L)≥μ8​supπ∈Π⁡(P,P)𝔼(X,Y)∼π​[d⁡{a⋆​(X),a⋆​(Y)}−L​d𝖷​(X,Y)]+2.\mathfrak{O}_{P}(\mathfrak{A}_{L})\geq\frac{\mu}{8}\sup_{\pi\in\Pi(P,P)}\mathbb{E}_{(X,Y)\sim\pi}\bigl[d\{a^{\star}(X),a^{\star}(Y)\}-Ld_{\mathsf{X}}(X,Y)\bigr]_{+}^{2}.

Equivalently, every fixed self-coupling π\pi supplies a valid, possibly weaker, lower certificate by omitting the supremum.

The coefficient μ/8\mu/8 is fixed by the convention that π\pi is a probability coupling with both marginals equal to PP. Alternative unnormalized edge sums require their own normalization; this does not alter the population theorem.

12.2 Finite calibration, dual flow, and population thickening

Finite calibration graphs.

In data analysis the instance space is represented by a graph G=(V,E)G=(V,E). At vertex ii, an estimated local oracle is a~i\widetilde{a}_{i} with uncertainty radius ϵi\epsilon_{i}. Define robust edge demand

bi​j=[d⁡(a~i,a~j)−ϵi−ϵj−L​di​j]+.b_{ij}=\bigl[d(\widetilde{a}_{i},\widetilde{a}_{j})-\epsilon_{i}-\epsilon_{j}-Ld_{ij}\bigr]_{+}.

Every admissible field has vertex errors ei≥0e_{i}\geq 0 satisfying

ei+ej≥bi​j((i,j)∈E).e_{i}+e_{j}\geq b_{ij}\qquad((i,j)\in E).

A quadratic lower certificate is obtained by minimizing

min⁡∑iei≥0⁡wi​ei2subject toei+ej≥bi​j.\min_{e_{i}\geq 0}\sum_{i}w_{i}e_{i}^{2}\quad\text{subject to}\quad e_{i}+e_{j}\geq b_{ij}.

Strong defect growth converts the solution to native objective units.

Dual flow.

The convex program has a flow-like dual. Introduce nonnegative edge multipliers λi​j\lambda_{ij}. The Lagrangian is

∑iwi​ei2+∑(i,j)λi​j​(bi​j−ei−ej).\sum_{i}w_{i}e_{i}^{2}+\sum_{(i,j)}\lambda_{ij}(b_{ij}-e_{i}-e_{j}).

Minimization over eie_{i} gives

ei=12​wi∑j:(i,j)∈Eλi​je_{i}=\frac{1}{2w_{i}}\sum_{j:(i,j)\in E}\lambda_{ij}

when the nonnegativity constraint is inactive; the complete formula uses the positive part. The dual objective becomes

∑(i,j)λi​j​bi​j−∑i14​wi​(∑jλi​j)2.\sum_{(i,j)}\lambda_{ij}b_{ij}-\sum_{i}\frac{1}{4w_{i}}\left(\sum_{j}\lambda_{ij}\right)^{2}.

Maximizing over λ≥0\lambda\geq 0 yields the exact convex lower certificate in the quadratic graph model.

This calculation is a direct Lagrange dual of the displayed finite program, not a claim to originate network-flow duality or order-restricted regression. Its closest classical lineage includes the least-squares isotonic formulation and its cumulative-sum/dual characterizations (Barlow and Brunk, 1972; Rockafellar, 1984). The contribution here is the oracle-mismatch interpretation and conversion of the optimum into native objective units.

Population thickening.

A pointwise mismatch becomes a positive population tax only if the population places mass near the mismatch. Suppose AA and a⋆a^{\star} are regular and at x0x_{0} the distance is at least δ\delta. If both fields are Lipschitz, the distance remains at least δ/2\delta/2 on a ball of radius proportional to δ\delta. A lower mass condition

P⁡{B⁡(x,r)}≥c​rdP\{B(x,r)\}\geq cr^{d}

then gives a population lower bound of order

μ​c​δd+2.\mu c\,\delta^{d+2}.

This step is essential. A deterministic point obstruction on a nonatomic population can otherwise have zero average cost.

12.3 Set-valued oracles and certificate boundaries

For a finite oracle cover, replace point distance by

d​{A⁡(x),𝒪⁡(x)}.d\{A(x),\mathcal{O}(x)\}.

Local branch transport is needed to compare oracle elements across nearby points. If the cover is separated and transport-consistent, a regular lower bound can be applied branchwise. When branches collide, the assumptions fail and the singular theory of Chapter 14 is required.

What the certificate does not prove.

A positive graph certificate proves that the declared baseline architecture cannot follow the estimated oracle field within its uncertainty radii. It does not by itself prove:

  • •

    that the local oracle model is scientifically correct;

  • •

    that an atlas will generalize;

  • •

    that the defect is visible to the final task;

  • •

    that the graph faithfully represents the population geometry.

Each claim requires a later gate.

Chapter 13 Rectangularity, Coordination Tax, and Memory

13.1 Conditional architectures and their rectangular hull

Consider a finite history tree. A deployed law QQ is determined by conditional kernels

qh(⋅∣h)q_{h}(\cdot\mid h)

at each history hh. Let P⋆P^{\star} be an oracle law with kernels ph⋆p_{h}^{\star}. At inverse temperature β\beta, the native defect is

Dβ(Q;P⋆)=1βKL(Q∥P⋆).D_{\beta}(Q;P^{\star})=\frac{1}{\beta}\operatorname{KL}(Q\|P^{\star}).

The architecture obstruction is

Oβ​(𝔄,P⋆)=infQ∈𝔄Dβ​(Q,P⋆).O_{\beta}(\mathfrak{A};P^{\star})=\inf_{Q\in\mathfrak{A}}D_{\beta}(Q;P^{\star}).

Every deployed law satisfies

Dβ​(Q,P⋆)=Oβ​(𝔄,P⋆)+Δβ,𝔄impl​(Q,P⋆).D_{\beta}(Q;P^{\star})=O_{\beta}(\mathfrak{A};P^{\star})+\Delta^{\mathrm{impl}}_{\beta,\mathfrak{A}}(Q;P^{\star}).
Rectangular hull.

The local kernel sets available inside 𝔄\mathfrak{A} can be freed and pasted independently across histories.

Definition 13.1 (Rectangular hull).

Rect⁡(𝔄)\operatorname{Rect}(\mathfrak{A}) is the class obtained by allowing every conditional kernel that occurs locally in some member of 𝔄\mathfrak{A} to be chosen independently at every history where it is admissible.

Write

Ci𝔄(h)={qi(⋅∣h):Qq∈𝔄}C_{i}^{\mathfrak{A}}(h)=\{q_{i}(\cdot\mid h):Q^{q}\in\mathfrak{A}\}

for the locally available kernels at stage ii and history hh.

The rectangular hull removes cross-history coordination constraints while preserving the local options. Its obstruction obeys a Bellman recursion because each history can then be optimized independently, conditional on occupancy. Rectangular uncertainty sets and robust Bellman recursions are classical in robust dynamic programming and recursive multiple-priors models (Iyengar, 2005; Nilim and El Ghaoui, 2005; Epstein and Schneider, 2003), and tractable departures from rectangularity have also been studied (Goyal and Grand-Clément, 2023). Here the object being rectangularized is not an uncertainty set but a deployment architecture. The loss created by forced cross-history sharing is retained explicitly as a coordination tax.

13.2 The coordination decomposition

Since 𝔄⊆Rect⁡(𝔄)\mathfrak{A}\subseteq\operatorname{Rect}(\mathfrak{A}),

Oβ​{Rect⁡(𝔄);P⋆}≤Oβ​(𝔄,P⋆).O_{\beta}\{\operatorname{Rect}(\mathfrak{A});P^{\star}\}\leq O_{\beta}(\mathfrak{A};P^{\star}).

Define

𝖳βcoord​(𝔄,P⋆)=Oβ​(𝔄,P⋆)−Oβ​{Rect⁡(𝔄);P⋆}.\mathsf{T}^{\mathrm{coord}}_{\beta}(\mathfrak{A};P^{\star})=O_{\beta}(\mathfrak{A};P^{\star})-O_{\beta}\{\operatorname{Rect}(\mathfrak{A});P^{\star}\}.
Theorem 13.2 (Rectangular Bellman and coordination-residual decomposition).

Set Wm=0W_{m}=0 and define backward values by

Wi−1(h)=minq∈Ci𝔄​(h){1βKL{q∥pi⋆(⋅∣h)}+∑yq(y)Wi(h,y)}.W_{i-1}(h)=\min_{q\in C_{i}^{\mathfrak{A}}(h)}\left\{\frac{1}{\beta}\operatorname{KL}\{q\|p_{i}^{\star}(\cdot\mid h)\}+\sum_{y}q(y)W_{i}(h,y)\right\}.

For a locally available kernel define

ρi(q;h)=1βKL{q∥pi⋆(⋅∣h)}+∑yq(y)Wi(h,y)−Wi−1(h).\rho_{i}(q;h)=\frac{1}{\beta}\operatorname{KL}\{q\|p_{i}^{\star}(\cdot\mid h)\}+\sum_{y}q(y)W_{i}(h,y)-W_{i-1}(h).

Then

W0=Oβ​{Rect⁡(𝔄);P⋆},ρi​(q,h)≥0.W_{0}=O_{\beta}\{\operatorname{Rect}(\mathfrak{A});P^{\star}\},\qquad\rho_{i}(q;h)\geq 0.

Every Qq∈Rect⁡(𝔄)Q^{q}\in\operatorname{Rect}(\mathfrak{A}) satisfies the exact chain rule

Dβ(Qq;P⋆)=W0+∑i=1m𝔼Qqρi{qi(⋅∣Hi−1);Hi−1}.D_{\beta}(Q^{q};P^{\star})=W_{0}+\sum_{i=1}^{m}\mathbb{E}_{Q^{q}}\rho_{i}\{q_{i}(\cdot\mid H_{i-1});H_{i-1}\}.

Moreover,

𝖳βcoord(𝔄;P⋆)=minQq∈𝔄∑i=1m𝔼Qqρi{qi(⋅∣Hi−1);Hi−1}.\mathsf{T}^{\mathrm{coord}}_{\beta}(\mathfrak{A};P^{\star})=\min_{Q^{q}\in\mathfrak{A}}\sum_{i=1}^{m}\mathbb{E}_{Q^{q}}\rho_{i}\{q_{i}(\cdot\mid H_{i-1});H_{i-1}\}.

Consequently every Q∈𝔄Q\in\mathfrak{A} obeys

Dβ​(Q,P⋆)=Oβ​{Rect⁡(𝔄);P⋆}+𝖳βcoord​(𝔄,P⋆)+Δβ,𝔄impl​(Q,P⋆).D_{\beta}(Q;P^{\star})=O_{\beta}\{\operatorname{Rect}(\mathfrak{A});P^{\star}\}+\mathsf{T}^{\mathrm{coord}}_{\beta}(\mathfrak{A};P^{\star})+\Delta^{\mathrm{impl}}_{\beta,\mathfrak{A}}(Q;P^{\star}).

The theorem assigns a native cost to parameter sharing. A shared network couples decisions across histories; it is not merely a smaller list of local functions. Recent work studies when shared representations help in multitask learning (Li et al., 2025), how learned representations affect offline transfer RL (Bose et al., 2025), and how finite memory creates return error in partially observed RL (Eberhard et al., 2025). Those results motivate the same deployment pressure. The theorem here isolates a narrower quantity: the exact native cost of cross-history coupling after the locally available kernels have been fixed.

Rectangularization is also distinct from operation C in the P/G/X/V/C calculus of Chapter 6. It frees admissible historywise choices; C keeps the declared marginals fixed and changes only their joint coupling.

Local Bellman residuals.

The rectangular dynamic program generates a nonnegative residual at each history. Under the occupancy induced by QQ, the expected sum of local residuals equals

𝖳coord+Δimpl.\mathsf{T}^{\mathrm{coord}}+\Delta^{\mathrm{impl}}.

This produces a diagnostic map: the global tax can be localized to histories where sharing is most expensive.

A shared-kernel example.

Suppose the same kernel qq is used at several histories with strictly positive oracle kernels ph⋆p_{h}^{\star} on a common finite output set. Let the fixed occupancy weights satisfy wh≥0w_{h}\geq 0 and

W=∑hwh>0.W=\sum_{h}w_{h}>0.

Assume also that each ph⋆p_{h}^{\star} is locally admissible when histories are freed, so the corresponding rectangular obstruction is zero.

The shared optimization problem is

infq∈Δ⁡(𝒴)1β∑hwhKL(q∥ph⋆).\inf_{q\in\Delta(\mathcal{Y})}\frac{1}{\beta}\sum_{h}w_{h}\operatorname{KL}(q\|p_{h}^{\star}).

Define

ZW=∑z∏hph⋆​(z)wh/W,q⋆​(z)=ZW−1​∏hph⋆​(z)wh/W.Z_{W}=\sum_{z}\prod_{h}p_{h}^{\star}(z)^{w_{h}/W},\qquad q^{\star}(z)=Z_{W}^{-1}\prod_{h}p_{h}^{\star}(z)^{w_{h}/W}.

Direct expansion gives the exact identity

1β∑hwhKL(q∥ph⋆)=WβKL(q∥q⋆)−WβlogZW.\frac{1}{\beta}\sum_{h}w_{h}\operatorname{KL}(q\|p_{h}^{\star})=\frac{W}{\beta}\operatorname{KL}(q\|q^{\star})-\frac{W}{\beta}\log Z_{W}.

Hence the minimum, and therefore the exact fixed-occupancy shared-kernel coordination tax under the declared weights, is

−Wβ​log⁡ZW.-\frac{W}{\beta}\log Z_{W}.

This is not the full endogenous coordination tax unless a separate occupancy or fixed-point theorem shows that the weights whw_{h} are the occupancies induced by the optimizing shared law. When occupancies vary with qq, they must remain inside the architecture-level optimization. Generalized Hölder gives 0<ZW≤10<Z_{W}\leq 1, so this tax is nonnegative; it vanishes exactly when all oracle kernels carrying positive weight coincide. When the weights are normalized, W=1W=1, this reduces to the usual normalized geometric-pooling formula (Genest and Zidek, 1986).

13.3 Memory compression as base change

Rectangularization removes cross-history coupling; memory compression changes which histories are distinguishable before that coupling is assessed. The next identity treats this compression as a base change, and the source box states which results are imported.

Within that imported scope, let a fine history hh map to a compressed memory state m=ρ⁡(h)m=\rho(h). The KL chain rule decomposes a fine law into a coarse memory law and conditional fiber laws. At architecture level,

Ofine=infQM{Ocoarse​(QM)+Ψ⁡(QM)},O_{\rm fine}=\inf_{Q_{M}}\left\{O_{\rm coarse}(Q_{M})+\Psi(Q_{M})\right\},

where Ψ⁡(QM)\Psi(Q_{M}) is the minimum fine conditional realization tax compatible with the coarse law.

A memory representation can preserve coarse objective values while failing to realize the canonical fine conditional kernels. This is objective faithfulness without obstruction faithfulness.

Saturation and exact base change.

Universal equality between fine and coarse architecture obstructions holds when the fine architecture is saturated by the canonical oracle fiber kernels. Approximate saturation yields an additive upper bound. This is stronger than saying that the coarse statistic is sufficient for one fixed oracle; it is an architecture-level statement over the declared class.

13.4 Zero temperature

As β→∞\beta\to\infty, soft KL-regularized functionals may converge to hard costs. For fixed architecture classes, uniform law-level dequantization passes to architecture minima. For varying classes, Γ\Gamma-convergence and inner/outer limit conditions are needed.

The zero-temperature limit can remain randomized. Temperature removal alone does not force a deterministic architecture. The admissible class and its closure determine the hard limit.

Chapter 14 Singular Fibers, Monodromy, and Catastrophe Taxes

The regular theory assumes a unique oracle or a finite separated cover. At a discriminant, branches collide, the vertical Hessian loses rank, and the oracle incidence map becomes stratified. Distance-to-branch arguments can degenerate precisely where the topology changes.

Here monodromy is the permutation of locally tracked oracle branches after continuation around a loop; when the declared output contract cannot absorb that permutation, the resulting native loss is a catastrophe tax.

The singular theory begins from a normal form whose native residual remains meaningful even when curvature vanishes.

14.1 The radical normal form

Let

Hθ​(a)=|ak−r​ei​ℓ​θ|2,a∈ℂ,θ∈S1,H_{\theta}(a)=|a^{k}-re^{i\ell\theta}|^{2},\qquad a\in\mathbb{C},\quad\theta\in S^{1},

with k≥2k\geq 2, r>0r>0, and ℓ∈ℤ\ell\in\mathbb{Z}. Each fiber has kk zero-defect roots. A continuous root selection exists exactly when kk divides ℓ\ell.

Theorem 14.1 (Exact radical catastrophe tax).
infA∈C⁡(S1,ℂ)supθ∈S1|A​(θ)k−r​ei​ℓ​θ|2={0,k|ℓ,r2,k∤ℓ.\inf_{A\in C(S^{1},\mathbb{C})}\sup_{\theta\in S^{1}}|A(\theta)^{k}-re^{i\ell\theta}|^{2}=\begin{cases}0,&k\mid\ell,\\ r^{2},&k\nmid\ell.\end{cases}

The upper witness lies on the collision stratum. The exact constant survives without strong convexity or branch separation and vanishes continuously as the target loop approaches the discriminant.

14.2 Risk level, general loops, and degree

Uniform versus average risk.

For a nonatomic sampling law on the circle, the infimum average defect over continuous fields is zero even when the uniform tax is r2r^{2}. A selector can follow one branch everywhere except on a narrow seam whose measure tends to zero.

Thus the theorem is a uniform deterministic architecture tax. A positive average tax requires an additional regularity, lower-mass, or complexity condition preventing seam concentration.

General loops and degree.

For a nonvanishing target loop z⁡(θ)z(\theta), winding incompatibility yields two-sided catastrophe bounds controlled by radial clearance from zero. In higher dimensions, let F:ℝd→ℝdF:\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}^{d} be positively homogeneous and consider its normalized map on the sphere. If the target degree is incompatible with the degree of F/|F|F/|F|, a constant-radius target sphere has an exact residual floor analogous to the radical case.

The important pattern is:

homotopy class incompatible with the output map\displaystyle\text{homotopy class incompatible with the output map}
⟹native residual at least the distance to the discriminant.\displaystyle\Longrightarrow\text{native residual at least the distance to the discriminant}.

14.3 Beyond radicals: roots, eigenlines, and partial monodromy

Polynomial roots and critical values.

Let pp be a complex polynomial and let a target loop avoid the critical-value discriminant. Its roots form a covering with monodromy. If the monodromy has no fixed branch, any continuous root-valued deployment must incur residual at least the target loop’s distance to the critical-value set. Near a ramification point of order mm, analytic coordinates reduce the problem to the radical normal form.

Using discriminant complements, monodromy, and braid structure to obstruct continuous algorithms has a classical topology-of-algorithms lineage (Smale, 1987; Vassiliev, 1988). The additional claim here is objective-denominated: the native residual and clearance from the discriminant turn that qualitative obstruction into a numerical loss floor.

Eigenline catastrophe.

Consider a real symmetric 2×22\times 2 matrix family around a conical crossing. The top eigenline forms a projective bundle with odd holonomy. An oriented continuous unit eigenvector must fail after one loop and pays an exact Rayleigh tax. The rank-one projector

P=v​v⊤P=vv^{\top}

is invariant under v↦−vv\mapsto-v and can remain continuous with zero defect.

This example demonstrates that the obstruction may be a representation artifact even when the underlying geometric object is perfectly regular. It sits beside modern impossibility results for continuous canonicalization and topological bottlenecks in learned representations (Dym et al., 2024; Batson et al., 2021; Esmaeili et al., 2023). The exact Rayleigh tax here is a more specific statement in the native spectral loss, not a consequence claimed from those adjacent results.

Missing branches versus monodromy.

Monodromy permutes branches that exist throughout a loop. A missing branch is undefined on part of the path. The two phenomena require partial rather than total transport maps. Forcing every edge transport to be a permutation can manufacture spurious cycles and false global inconsistency. The transport construction in Chapter 23 therefore treats transports as partial bijections and audits both fixed-point behavior and domain survival. Partial maps and their synchronization are established in multi-object matching; the distinction developed here is the oracle/task meaning assigned to disappearance and domain survival, as documented with prior art in Chapter 23.

14.4 Stability

The exact tax is stable under perturbations that preserve the homotopy class and maintain positive clearance from the discriminant. When the target approaches the discriminant, the tax can vanish. This is the correct singular behavior: topology remains incompatible, but the objective price of incompatibility becomes arbitrarily small.

Chapter 15 Atlases, Quotients, and Randomized Repair

15.1 From obstruction diagnosis to a repair contract

A positive obstruction does not imply that the original task is impossible. It means that the declared architecture contract is incompatible with the oracle geometry. A repair changes the contract in a controlled way.

The principal repair families are:

  1. 1.

    local atlases;

  2. 2.

    quotient-valued outputs;

  3. 3.

    set-valued outputs;

  4. 4.

    probability-valued outputs or randomized point rules;

  5. 5.

    memory refinement or rectangularization;

  6. 6.

    nonlinear semantic projection;

  7. 7.

    test-time local refinement.

The correct repair is the smallest contract change that removes the certified obstruction while preserving downstream information. This criterion rules out a flat menu of interchangeable fixes. Some obstructions arise because one representative cannot be chosen globally; others arise from forced sharing, an invalid semantic interface, or an insufficient deployment computation. The remainder of the chapter follows these mechanisms and then returns to the statistical problem of selecting among their repairs.

15.2 Local and symmetry-respecting repair

Let {Uj}j=1K\{U_{j}\}_{j=1}^{K} cover 𝖷\mathsf{X}. On each chart UjU_{j}, suppose a continuous oracle section aj⋆a_{j}^{\star} exists. A hard atlas architecture consists of a gate g⁡(x)g(x) and local experts Aj​(x)A_{j}(x). The minimum number of local sections needed to cover a fibration is closely related to sectional category and Schwarz genus (Schwarz, 1961); the theorem below uses only the existence of a declared cover and does not claim a minimal chart number. Multi-chart representation learning and chart-based autoencoders provide a separate machine-learning lineage (Schonsheck et al., 2019; Kalatzis et al., 2021; Stolberg-Larsen and Sommer, 2021). In this chapter the equivalence between a cover by at most KK local sections and a KK-chart atlas is a definitional inversion. The theorem below is only the witness lemma that such declared sections saturate the atlas class; it does not claim to invent multi-chart models or to learn the cover (Huang and Wang, 2026l).

Theorem 15.1 (Atlas saturation).

Suppose the declared charts form a measurable cover, the hard-atlas grammar contains a measurable gate gg satisfying x∈Ug⁡(x)x\in U_{g(x)}, and every local expert class contains an exact oracle section on its chart. Then the hard atlas class has zero uniform obstruction:

inf(g,A1,…,AK)supx𝖣x​{Ag⁡(x)​(x)}=0.\inf_{(g,A_{1},\ldots,A_{K})}\sup_{x}\mathsf{D}_{x}\{A_{g(x)}(x)\}=0.

The theorem is existential: it neither learns the cover nor proves that the chosen chart count is minimal.

An atlas retains point-valued representatives but localizes where they must be chosen. When the labels themselves carry no downstream meaning, the more economical repair is instead to change the output object.

Suppose a symmetry group GG acts on the auxiliary fiber and the defect is invariant:

𝖣x​(g​a)=𝖣x​(a).\mathsf{D}_{x}(ga)=\mathsf{D}_{x}(a).

If the downstream task depends only on the orbit [a]∈𝖠/G[a]\in\mathsf{A}/G, then the quotient is the natural output. A global quotient section may exist even when no global representative section does.

Examples include:

  • •

    eigenprojectors instead of oriented eigenvectors;

  • •

    unordered mixture components instead of labeled lists;

  • •

    subspaces instead of bases;

  • •

    equivalence classes of gauges instead of coordinates.

For the radical family, the full root set is globally defined. A set-valued output can therefore achieve zero defect. Likewise, the uniform distribution over roots is invariant under monodromy.

Probability-valued versus randomized repair.

A probability-valued output returns a law KxK_{x} and therefore requires a task and loss defined on laws. A randomized point-valued deployment instead draws A∼KxA\sim K_{x} and, under expected native loss, pays

∫𝖣x​(a)​Kx​(𝑑a).\int\mathsf{D}_{x}(a)\,K_{x}(\,\mathrm{d}a).

The two contracts remain distinct even when they use the same kernel. Neither is the deterministic ambient average ∫a​Kx​(𝑑a)\int a\,K_{x}(\,\mathrm{d}a), when that average is defined; the average may leave the oracle set.

These repairs change downstream semantics. A task that needs one labeled root may still require a chart or additional side information. A symmetric task can operate directly on the set or law.

The quotient, set-valued, and probability-valued constructions also explain why a superficially simpler aggregation can be unsafe. A tempting response to multiple local branches is to average representatives. In the square-root example, averaging aa and −a-a gives zero, which lies on the discriminant and pays the full catastrophe tax. Ambient averaging can therefore destroy oracle information.

Safe aggregation must respect the quotient or use a native barycenter under the declared defect. Thus atlas and quotient repair solve different problems: the former permits several coherent local representatives, whereas the latter removes distinctions that the task is not entitled to observe. Neither authorizes an arbitrary average in the ambient representation space.

15.3 Repairing deployment mechanisms

In sequential systems, the repair may be to enlarge the memory state so that histories requiring different local kernels no longer collide. Alternatively, one can relax shared parameters and allow independent local kernels, moving toward the rectangular hull.

The benefit is measured by the coordination tax removed. The cost is increased state, memory, communication, or generalization complexity.

Forced sharing is not the only mechanism-level failure. A legal linear calculation may also leave the semantic output set, in which case the repair belongs at the validity interface rather than in the memory state.

The graph-CDF example uses a different repair. The raw high-order field is projected onto the valid semantic set. This changes neither the output type nor the local oracle family, but it replaces an invalid linear mechanism by a nonlinear interface.

The projection is justified only because it is nonexpansive in the native risk geometry. An arbitrary clipping or renormalization step requires its own theorem.

Deployment computation provides a third mechanism-level intervention. A semi-amortized system starts from a shared prediction and performs local optimization at test time. This can reduce implementation error and, if the allowed iteration budget is part of the architecture, enlarge the effective class. Laboratory 24.2.1 audits this distinction on MNIST by declaring the zero-step and refined deployment classes before evaluating the held-out native objective.

Test-time refinement is not equivalent to atlas repair. It may still follow the wrong labeled branch or remain trapped by a representation obstruction. The repair must be matched to the certificate.

Memory refinement, semantic projection, and test-time optimization therefore alter different clauses of the contract. Their costs cannot be compared by parameter count alone; each must be charged in the resource and loss scale declared for deployment.

15.4 Selection, validation, and repair frontiers

Suppose a finite library {𝔄(1),…,𝔄(M)}\{\mathfrak{A}^{(1)},\ldots,\mathfrak{A}^{(M)}\} contains candidate repairs. Calibration data produce lower and upper obstruction certificates; tuning data train the candidates; test data compare their operational performance. This separation avoids selecting and certifying the same architecture on the same random fluctuations.

For atlas repairs, this decision can be recorded as a frontier rather than a single winning chart count. For tolerance τ\tau, define the minimum number of charts required to attain uniform defect at most τ\tau. The resulting integer-valued atlas curve can jump. Its inverse—the best loss attainable with KK charts—is often more stable under perturbation and is the preferred statistical object.

The frontier keeps the structural and statistical questions separate. It records what each chart budget can realize, while sample splitting determines which point on that frontier is supported by the available evidence.
