Proof of atlas saturation

Dependencies. The cover must be genuine, the gate must route only to charts containing the input, and each local expert class must contain an exact local oracle section. No learning or minimal-chart claim is involved.

Proof.

For each chart UjU_{j}, let aj⋆:Uj→𝖠a_{j}^{\star}:U_{j}\to\mathsf{A} be an exact local oracle section contained in the declared expert class, so that

𝖣x​{aj⋆​(x)}=0(x∈Uj).\mathsf{D}_{x}\{a_{j}^{\star}(x)\}=0\qquad(x\in U_{j}).

Because the charts cover 𝖷\mathsf{X}, choose a measurable selector g⁡(x)g(x) with x∈Ug⁡(x)x\in U_{g(x)}; for a finite open cover on a standard Borel space, one may take the smallest chart index containing xx. Set Aj=aj⋆A_{j}=a_{j}^{\star}. Then for every xx,

𝖣x​{Ag⁡(x)​(x)}=0.\mathsf{D}_{x}\{A_{g(x)}(x)\}=0.

Therefore the supremum over xx is zero. Since defects are nonnegative, no architecture can attain a negative value, and the infimum over the atlas class is exactly zero. ∎

Part IV Historical and Conceptual Notes

Three obstruction mechanisms, three literatures

Regular transport bounds combine Lipschitz approximation, couplings, and curvature exchange. Rectangular Bellman recursion belongs to robust control and recursive multiple-priors theory (Epstein and Schneider, 2003; Iyengar, 2005; Nilim and El Ghaoui, 2005). Loop lifting, winding, degree, discriminants, and Schwarz genus are classical topology and singularity theory (Hatcher, 2002; Milnor, 1997; Schwarz, 1961). Part IV does not relabel these ingredients as discoveries of elimination geometry.

Its organizing distinction is the deployment quantifier. A regular architecture may be unable to track an oracle that varies too quickly; a shared conditional architecture may be unable to paste locally available kernels; and a continuous point-valued output may be unable to choose one branch around a singular loop. These failures demand different witnesses and different repairs.

Regime Classical engine Book/program quantity Matched repair
Regular variation Lipschitz comparison and transport native oracle- variation lower certificate more regularity budget, local refinement, or additional charts
Coordination rectangular Bellman recursion and KL chain rule exact cost of cross-history sharing in forward-KL units memory refinement, rectangularization, or a different sharing rule
Singular topology winding, monodromy, degree, genus uniform objective-denominated catastrophe tax atlas, quotient, set-valued, or randomized output

The rectangular residual decomposition is a source-program architecture specialization of classical rectangularity. Atlas saturation is a direct witness lemma. The exact radical value r2r^{2} is a useful quantitative winding corollary in native-objective units; it is not presented as a new topological mechanism.

Part V Resources, Operational Semantics, and Composition
Resources determine which oracle distinctions can be retained; task and context classes determine which surviving distinctions are operationally visible.

Chapter 16 Resource-Constrained Architecture Rate–Distortion

16.1 The architecture as carrier and decoder

Here carrier means the deployment information state passed to an action decoder. It is not the reduced slack carrier of Section 10.3, which removes representation gauge before deployment is considered. Section 10.4 supplies the conditional extraction gate from a quotient-reduced lift to a deployment carrier; without such a gate the two remain distinct.

An architecture first produces a carrier ZZ and then decodes it:

X→ϕZ→𝑔A.X\xrightarrow{\phi}Z\xrightarrow{g}A.

The terminology deliberately recalls rate–distortion theory, where a source is compressed subject to a fidelity criterion (Shannon, 1959; Cover and Thomas, 2006). Here the distortion is not chosen independently of the learning problem: it is the native objective defect, and the resource grammar may constrain both the carrier and its decoder. Across inputs, the oracle map x↦a⋆​(x)x\mapsto a^{\star}(x) determines which distinctions a deployment carrier must preserve. Within each fiber, the native defect determines the price of merging those distinctions. The carrier need not retain all information in xx; it need only be sufficient for the oracle signature. Conversely, width, state count, or cone size is not effective capacity unless the retained state preserves those signatures and makes them decodable.

A resource grammar indexed by (m,r)(m,r) restricts carrier size, number of labels, communication, coherence, smoothness, or decoder complexity. Write 𝔊m,r\mathfrak{G}_{m,r} for its declared class of admissible carrier–decoder pairs (Z,g)(Z,g), and put

𝒵m,r={Z:there exists ​g​ with ​(Z,g)∈𝔊m,r}.\mathcal{Z}_{m,r}=\{Z:\text{there exists }g\text{ with }(Z,g)\in\mathfrak{G}_{m,r}\}.

The architecture can fail in two ways.

  1. 1.

    The carrier erases distinctions among oracle signatures.

  2. 2.

    The carrier retains the information, but the decoder class cannot realize the optimal readout.

16.2 Canonical Bregman carrier

Reuse the dual oracle signature S=∇Φ​{a⋆​(X)}S=\nabla\Phi\{a^{\star}(X)\} from Section 10.4. For a carrier ZZ, put

SZ=𝔼⁡(S∣Z).S_{Z}=\mathbb{E}(S\mid Z).

The optimal unconstrained decoder is

aZ†=∇Φ⋆​(SZ).a_{Z}^{\dagger}=\nabla\Phi^{\star}(S_{Z}).

This follows from conditional Bregman projection; conditional expectation as the optimal Bregman predictor and the associated centroid identity are classical (Banerjee et al., 2005a). The resource split below specializes that identity to a carrier–decoder grammar (Huang and Wang, 2026h).

The carrier information loss is

𝒞Φ(Z)=𝔼DΦ{aZ†(Z)∥a⋆(X)}.\mathcal{C}_{\Phi}(Z)=\mathbb{E}D_{\Phi}\{a_{Z}^{\dagger}(Z)\|a^{\star}(X)\}.

For a carrier admitted by the grammar, define decoder nonsaturation by

Ψm,r(Z)=infg:(Z,g)∈𝔊m,r𝔼DΦ{g(Z)∥aZ†(Z)}.\Psi_{m,r}(Z)=\inf_{g:(Z,g)\in\mathfrak{G}_{m,r}}\mathbb{E}D_{\Phi}\{g(Z)\|a_{Z}^{\dagger}(Z)\}.

The infimum is +∞+\infty if the carrier has no admissible decoder. The native architecture distortion is the best original objective defect among admissible pairs,

𝒟nat(m,r)=inf(Z,g)∈𝔊m,r𝔼DΦ{g(Z)∥a⋆(X)}.\mathcal{D}_{\rm nat}(m,r)=\inf_{(Z,g)\in\mathfrak{G}_{m,r}}\mathbb{E}D_{\Phi}\{g(Z)\|a^{\star}(X)\}.

The divergence orientation is chosen to match the exact Bregman Pythagorean identity.

Theorem 16.1 (Canonical architecture rate–distortion decomposition).

Under the common-fiber Legendre assumptions,

𝒟nat​(m,r)=infZ∈𝒵m,r{𝒞Φ​(Z)+Ψm,r​(Z)}.\mathcal{D}_{\rm nat}(m,r)=\inf_{Z\in\mathcal{Z}_{m,r}}\bigl\{\mathcal{C}_{\Phi}(Z)+\Psi_{m,r}(Z)\bigr\}.

The formula is a second elimination over carriers. Width or parameter count is only one possible resource coordinate; the canonical retained state is the conditional dual oracle signature. The resource grammar is upstream of the P/G/X/V/C calculus in Chapter 6: it declares the feasible architecture within which an operation is performed. Changing that grammar is not a sixth mode.

16.3 Discrete and continuous carrier extraction

Hard carrier extraction.

Suppose ZZ takes at most mm labels and a weighted Potts coherence budget limits label changes on a graph. The inverse minimum qq-cut profile gives the exact number of usable labels under the budget. On paths and trees this capacity has a closed form; related cardinality-constrained and multiway-cut algorithms are classical (Goldschmidt and Hochbaum, 1994; Frederickson and Solis-Oba, 1998; Engelberg et al., 2007).

Precisely, for a weighted graph G=(V,E,w)G=(V,E,w) let c⁡(G∖F)c(G\setminus F) denote the number of connected components after deleting F⊆EF\subseteq E, and define

λq(G)=min{∑e∈Fwe:F⊆E,c(G∖F)≥q},λ1(G)=0.\lambda_{q}(G)=\min\left\{\sum_{e\in F}w_{e}:F\subseteq E,\ c(G\setminus F)\geq q\right\},\qquad\lambda_{1}(G)=0.

The hard-label capacity under label budget mm and cut budget rr is

κGhard​(m,r)=min⁡{m,max⁡{q:λq​(G)≤r}}.\kappa_{G}^{\rm hard}(m,r)=\min\left\{m,\max\{q:\lambda_{q}(G)\leq r\}\right\}.

It is exact for the declared Potts grammar: every feasible labeling is constant on the components left by its cut set, and conversely those components may be assigned distinct labels up to the cap mm.

If oracle signatures are well separated by type, the visible cardinality bound is attained. Strong convexity then converts limited label capacity into a quantization floor.

Continuous carriers.

For a normalized continuous conic carrier with a Lipschitz readout and quadratic graph coherence, metric entropy controls the number of distinguishable oracle signatures at resolution ϵ\epsilon. The matching lower exponent requires a co-Lipschitz readout on an interior region and a resource grammar admitting arbitrarily dense deployments in that region; the finite-site capacity cap still applies.

This produces a resource-to-information map of the form

log⁡N⁡(ϵ)≲d​log⁡(1+C⁡(m,r)ϵ).\log N(\epsilon)\lesssim d\log\left(1+\frac{C(m,r)}{\epsilon}\right).

Strong defect growth converts a covering-radius lower bound into native distortion.

16.4 Finite frontiers and phase diagrams

The finite Bregman quantization frontier.

For a finite oracle set with weights pip_{i} and codebook size qq, the optimal Bregman quantization error is

minc1,…,cq∑ipiminjDΦ(cj∥ai⋆).\min_{c_{1},\ldots,c_{q}}\sum_{i}p_{i}\min_{j}D_{\Phi}(c_{j}\|a_{i}^{\star}).

Within each assigned cell the optimal codeword is the dual-coordinate centroid. Separated signatures give a positive lower bound whenever qq is smaller than the number of distinguishable types. This is the usual vector quantization problem in the native Bregman geometry (Gray and Neuhoff, 1998; Graf and Luschgy, 2000; Friedrich et al., 2008).

Resource phase diagrams.

On an nn-vertex path whose edges all have the common weight w>0w>0, with hard routing and quadratic local loss, the effective carrier size is

qeff=min⁡{m,n,1+⌊r/w⌋}.q_{\rm eff}=\min\{m,n,1+\lfloor r/w\rfloor\}.

The native distortion reduces to balanced scalar quantization. The operational audit distance becomes a clipped discrete covering radius. This yields an exact capacity–resolution phase diagram.

16.5 An exact data-selection frontier

The preceding examples constrain a carrier chosen from a fixed codebook. A different finite resource contract arises when the carrier must itself be a small submultiset of the observed data and the decoder is fixed in advance. This setting yields an exact distortion curve rather than only an upper or lower rate.

Let D={z1,…,zN}⊂ℝdD=\{z_{1},\ldots,z_{N}\}\subset\mathbb{R}^{d} be a finite multiset, and write

LD​(h)=1N​∑i=1N‖h−zi‖2,μD=1N​∑i=1Nzi,VD=LD​(μD).L_{D}(h)=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\|h-z_{i}\|^{2},\qquad\mu_{D}=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}z_{i},\qquad V_{D}=L_{D}(\mu_{D}).

For an integer n≥1n\geq 1, an nn-point carrier stores indices i1,…,ini_{1},\ldots,i_{n}, with repetition allowed, and the decoder returns μ^=n−1​∑r=1nzir\widehat{\mu}=n^{-1}\sum_{r=1}^{n}z_{i_{r}}. For VD>0V_{D}>0, define its normalized worst-case native distortion by

𝒟sel​(d,n)=supD⊂ℝdmini1,…,in⁡‖μ^−μD‖2VD.\mathcal{D}_{\rm sel}(d,n)=\sup_{D\subset\mathbb{R}^{d}}\min_{i_{1},\ldots,i_{n}}\frac{\|\widehat{\mu}-\mu_{D}\|^{2}}{V_{D}}.

The bias–variance identity is the first certified elimination:

LD​(h)=VD+‖h−μD‖2.L_{D}(h)=V_{D}+\|h-\mu_{D}\|^{2}.

Thus the usual worst-case loss ratio is exactly F⁡(d,n)=1+𝒟sel​(d,n)F(d,n)=1+\mathcal{D}_{\rm sel}(d,n); selection budget becomes a resource coordinate measured directly in excess squared loss.

The proof exposes why this is more than a cardinality bound. A variance-nonincreasing Carathéodory reduction first preserves the mean while leaving at most d+1d+1 support points. For a centered reduced law ∑ipi​xi=0\sum_{i}p_{i}x_{i}=0 with variance V=∑ipi​‖xi‖2V=\sum_{i}p_{i}\|x_{i}\|^{2}, suppose the residual-capacity inequalities admit integer anchor counts sis_{i} with ∑isi=n−1\sum_{i}s_{i}=n-1 and (n−1)​si≤n2​pi(n-1)s_{i}\leq n^{2}p_{i}. Put u=∑isi​xiu=\sum_{i}s_{i}x_{i}, S=∑isi​‖xi‖2S=\sum_{i}s_{i}\|x_{i}\|^{2}, and

qi=n2​pi−(n−1)​si2​n−1,Γ⁡(s)=(n−1)​S−‖u‖2≥0.q_{i}=\frac{n^{2}p_{i}-(n-1)s_{i}}{2n-1},\qquad\Gamma(s)=(n-1)S-\|u\|^{2}\geq 0.

For J∼qJ\sim q, the remaining randomized point satisfies the exact ledger

𝔼​‖u+xJn‖2=V2​n−1−Γ⁡(s)n2​(2​n−1).\mathbb{E}\left\|\frac{u+x_{J}}{n}\right\|^{2}=\frac{V}{2n-1}-\frac{\Gamma(s)}{n^{2}(2n-1)}.

Taking the best point in the finite support of qq eliminates the auxiliary randomness and returns a legal deterministic selector.

Capacity failure requires a mechanism-specific repair. At n=3n=3, the remaining four-atom region is closed by a finite correlated-count certificate. For n≥4n\geq 4, failure forces a heavy pair; merging those two atoms releases variance λ​‖x1−x2‖2\lambda\|x_{1}-x_{2}\|^{2} with λ≥(2​n−1)/(4​n2)\lambda\geq(2n-1)/(4n^{2}). If V′V^{\prime} is the merged variance, randomized nearest-integer splitting back to legal data points obeys

V′2​n−1+‖x1−x2‖24​n2≤V2​n−1.\frac{V^{\prime}}{2n-1}+\frac{\|x_{1}-x_{2}\|^{2}}{4n^{2}}\leq\frac{V}{2n-1}.

The coarse-graining credit therefore pays the entire fiber-realization cost. The all-dimensional budget-two column closes differently: a sharp pair certificate after sparse reduction meets the centered regular-simplex lower bound at the displayed dimension transition. The theorem is logically self-contained rather than a corollary of the general calculus; what transfers is the discipline of exposing a native defect, eliminating only recoverable auxiliary objects, and closing every pushforward–recovery step in one currency.

16.6 Resource limits and operational boundaries

Resource limits and foundation models.

The theory suggests several resource coordinates for large AI systems:

  • •

    context length and memory state;

  • •

    number of experts or active routes;

  • •

    communication bandwidth among modules;

  • •

    test-time iteration budget;

  • •

    output vocabulary or structured state dimension;

  • •

    coherence imposed by parameter tying.

The relevant question is not whether a model has many parameters in total, but how much oracle-relevant distinction survives the declared carrier and can be extracted by the decoder.

What rate–distortion does not settle.

A positive native distortion need not affect a downstream task. The task may be invariant to the lost distinctions. Operational visibility requires the transmission and exposure gates of Chapter 17.

Chapter 17 Operational Semantics and Contextual Observability

17.1 From internal difference to task-observable kernels

Two pipelines can have different internal kernels while producing the same value for every downstream task that is legally allowed to use them. Conversely, two modules that agree at one base input can become distinguishable after insertion into a larger context.

Operational semantics asks when one pipeline can safely replace another under a declared task and context grammar. To make this question quantitative, represent a finite elimination pipeline by the cost it exposes between its boundary states. Such a pipeline is represented by a min-plus kernel K⁡(y,x)K(y,x): the least internal cost of transforming input state xx to output state yy. Given upstream potential ff and downstream terminal cost gg, the optimized value is

𝖵K​(f,g)=infx,y{f⁡(x)+K⁡(y,x)+g⁡(y)}.\mathsf{V}_{K}(f,g)=\inf_{x,y}\{f(x)+K(y,x)+g(y)\}.

A task contract 𝔗\mathfrak{T} is a declared collection of admissible pairs (f,g)(f,g).

This representation separates internal implementation from the values that a legal observer can extract. The next construction makes that separation canonical for a fixed task contract.

17.2 Task envelopes and contextual completion

Define the task envelope

(𝖤𝔗​K)​(y,x)=sup(f,g)∈𝔗{𝖵K​(f,g)−f⁡(x)−g⁡(y)}.(\mathsf{E}_{\mathfrak{T}}K)(y,x)=\sup_{(f,g)\in\mathfrak{T}}\{\mathsf{V}_{K}(f,g)-f(x)-g(y)\}.

The envelope is the pointwise least kernel that preserves all declared task values. The construction is related in spirit to classical residuation and convex conjugacy, while Attouch–Wets metrics concern convergence of epigraphs on unbounded spaces rather than the finite sup-norm identity stated here (Attouch and Wets, 1986). Proposition 17.1 is therefore proved directly from this task envelope and should not be read as an Attouch–Wets theorem (Huang and Wang, 2026j). For two kernels of the same type, define the base task observational distance by

d𝔗​(K,L)=sup(f,g)∈𝔗|𝖵K​(f,g)−𝖵L​(f,g)|.d_{\mathfrak{T}}(K,L)=\sup_{(f,g)\in\mathfrak{T}}\bigl|\mathsf{V}_{K}(f,g)-\mathsf{V}_{L}(f,g)\bigr|.
Proposition 17.1 (Task-envelope isometry).

The envelope preserves exactly the values 𝖵K​(f,g)\mathsf{V}_{K}(f,g) for (f,g)∈𝔗(f,g)\in\mathfrak{T}, and the task observational distance between KK and LL equals

‖𝖤𝔗​K−𝖤𝔗​L‖∞.\|\mathsf{E}_{\mathfrak{T}}K-\mathsf{E}_{\mathfrak{T}}L\|_{\infty}.

Task equivalence at the exposed boundary is not yet a compositional notion. A module that is invisible in isolation may become visible after legal preprocessing or postprocessing, so the task contract must be closed under the deployment grammar.

A grammar 𝔊\mathfrak{G} specifies legal pre- and post-compositions. The base task set must be closed under pullback through every legal context. Let

Cl𝔊⁡𝔗\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathfrak{G}}\mathfrak{T}

be the least context-stable task system containing 𝔗\mathfrak{T}. Define

𝖰𝔊,𝔗​K=𝖤Cl𝔊⁡𝔗​K.\mathsf{Q}_{\mathfrak{G},\mathfrak{T}}K=\mathsf{E}_{\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathfrak{G}}\mathfrak{T}}K.

Equivalently, if BB and AA range over type-compatible legal pre- and postcontexts, define

d𝔊,𝔗ctx​(K,L)=supA,Bd𝔗​(A⊗K⊗B,A⊗L⊗B).d_{\mathfrak{G},\mathfrak{T}}^{\rm ctx}(K,L)=\sup_{A,B}d_{\mathfrak{T}}(A\otimes K\otimes B,A\otimes L\otimes B).

Identity contexts are included, so this contextual distance dominates the base task distance. A pseudometric ρ\rho on type-compatible kernels is called task-adequate when d𝔗​(K,L)≤ρ⁡(K,L)d_{\mathfrak{T}}(K,L)\leq\rho(K,L), and grammar-nonexpansive when

ρ⁡(A⊗K⊗B,A⊗L⊗B)≤ρ⁡(K,L)\rho(A\otimes K\otimes B,A\otimes L\otimes B)\leq\rho(K,L)

for every legal precontext BB and postcontext AA.

Theorem 17.2 (Contextual completion and full abstraction).

The contextual distance is

d𝔊,𝔗ctx​(K,L)=‖𝖰𝔊,𝔗​K−𝖰𝔊,𝔗​L‖∞.d_{\mathfrak{G},\mathfrak{T}}^{\rm ctx}(K,L)=\|\mathsf{Q}_{\mathfrak{G},\mathfrak{T}}K-\mathsf{Q}_{\mathfrak{G},\mathfrak{T}}L\|_{\infty}.

It is the least task-adequate grammar-nonexpansive pseudometric. Its zero set is the greatest grammar congruence contained in base task equivalence, and 𝖰𝔊,𝔗​K\mathsf{Q}_{\mathfrak{G},\mathfrak{T}}K is the pointwise least representative of the fully abstract quotient.

17.3 From native defect to operational separation

The preceding theorem supplies the operational quotient of pipeline space. Suppose an architecture defect produces a nonnegative increment in a pipeline kernel. Two gates are needed. The first is the transmission gate: the native defect must actually increase the operational kernel rather than being absorbed by another internal choice. The second is the exposure gate: the closed task contract must contain a context that selects the affected states. Only then does a positive native architecture floor imply a positive contextual separation.

The amount transmitted through these gates depends on the resolution of the task family. For Lipschitz task contracts, the envelope becomes a double metric erosion. If a defect spike is narrower than the task resolution, it may be clipped or smoothed away. The exact resolution profile records the observable separation as task Lipschitz budgets vary.

Finite task families yield a visibility transform with an exact margin-clipped lower bound. Compact metric task classes yield a resolution coefficient determined by task and kernel Lipschitz moduli.

Thus the operational image of a native defect is generally a profile rather than a binary label. At coarse task resolution a real internal seam can be invisible; as the contract becomes more discriminating, the same seam can produce a positive contextual distance.

17.4 Ordering curvature and contextual witnesses

For nn operations, each permutation produces a kernel KπK_{\pi}. The contextual ordering curvature is the diameter

maxπ,σ⁡d𝔊,𝔗ctx​(Kπ,Kσ).\max_{\pi,\sigma}d_{\mathfrak{G},\mathfrak{T}}^{\rm ctx}(K_{\pi},K_{\sigma}).

Pairwise swap budgets can bound the global curvature through an inversion-weighted Kendall sum (Kendall, 1938). Pairwise commutation at one input does not imply contextual interchange coherence.

The need for context is already visible in a minimal finite-memory witness. A two-state screening pipeline can be constructed so that every operation order is invisible under a zero-input contract, yet a legal precontext creates a value gap of one. The full resolution profile is

max⁡{0,min⁡(1,a−1,b)}\max\{0,\min(1,a-1,b)\}

for task budgets (a,b)(a,b). The example demonstrates why one fixed audit input is insufficient for safe module substitution.

This conclusion parallels contextual equivalence and full abstraction in programming-language semantics (Milner, 1977; Plotkin, 1977). Here the boundary objects are optimization kernels and the task contract is quantitative, so the resulting quotient is both semantic and metric.

Proof of contextual completion and full abstraction

Dependencies. The grammar contains identity or formal empty contexts and is closed under typed composition. Context closure is defined by pulling every base task back through every legal pre- and post-context.

Proof.

For a precontext BB, postcontext AA, and external task (h,k)(h,k), both

𝖵A⊗K⊗B​(h,k)and𝖵K​(fB,h,gA,k)\mathsf{V}_{A\otimes K\otimes B}(h,k)\quad\text{and}\quad\mathsf{V}_{K}(f_{B,h},g_{A,k})

are the minimum of

h⁡(w)+B⁡(x,w)+K⁡(y,x)+A⁡(z,y)+k⁡(z)h(w)+B(x,w)+K(y,x)+A(z,y)+k(z)

over (w,x,y,z)(w,x,y,z). Thus contextual testing is exactly testing KK with the pullback-closed task system Cl𝔊⁡𝔗\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathfrak{G}}\mathfrak{T}. Applying the preceding task-envelope isometry gives

d𝔊,𝔗ctx​(K,L)=‖𝖰𝔊,𝔗​K−𝖰𝔊,𝔗​L‖∞.d_{\mathfrak{G},\mathfrak{T}}^{\rm ctx}(K,L)=\|\mathsf{Q}_{\mathfrak{G},\mathfrak{T}}K-\mathsf{Q}_{\mathfrak{G},\mathfrak{T}}L\|_{\infty}.

The supremum of absolute differences of scalar functionals is a pseudometric. Identity contexts show task adequacy. If fixed contexts are first placed around KK and LL, any further context combines with them into another legal context; hence the metric is grammar-nonexpansive.

Let ρ\rho be any task-adequate grammar-nonexpansive pseudometric. For every legal context,

d𝔗​(A⊗K⊗B,A⊗L⊗B)\displaystyle d_{\mathfrak{T}}(A\otimes K\otimes B,A\otimes L\otimes B) ≤ρ⁡(A⊗K⊗B,A⊗L⊗B)\displaystyle\leq\rho(A\otimes K\otimes B,A\otimes L\otimes B)

Taking the supremum over contexts proves that the contextual metric is the least such pseudometric.

Its zero set is a congruence by grammar nonexpansiveness and lies inside base task equivalence by task adequacy. Conversely, if ∼\sim is any grammar congruence contained in base task equivalence and K∼LK\sim L, then all contextual substitutions remain ∼\sim-related and hence base-task equivalent. Every contextual value difference is zero, so KK and LL have contextual distance zero. This proves the greatest-sound-congruence property.

Finally, apply task-envelope reconstruction to the closed contract. The envelope is deflationary, monotone, idempotent, preserves every closed task, and is the unique pointwise-least member of its equivalence class. Equality of contextual envelopes is equivalent to zero contextual distance, completing the fully abstract quotient statement. ∎

Chapter 18 Composition, Base Change, and Dequantization

Here base change means passage between fine and coarse representations, memories, or architecture levels. It preserves obstruction only under a proved commuting or exact decomposition theorem; equality of one optimized objective value is not sufficient.

18.1 Conditional chain rules and architecture composition

Candidate-level identities need not survive minimization over a restricted architecture. A local certificate may also fail after conditioning, pushforward, or a zero-temperature limit. We therefore distinguish several levels of composition, each of which can fail independently.

  1. 1.

    Law-level or candidate-level defect identities.

  2. 2.

    Architecture-level infima.

  3. 3.

    Representation or base-change maps.

  4. 4.

    Operational contextual composition.

  5. 5.

    Temperature limits.

Conditional KL chain rule.

Let QX​YQ_{XY} and PX​YP_{XY} be joint laws. The chain rule is

KL(QX​Y∥PX​Y)=KL(QX∥PX)+𝔼QXKL(QY|X∥PY|X).\operatorname{KL}(Q_{XY}\|P_{XY})=\operatorname{KL}(Q_{X}\|P_{X})+\mathbb{E}_{Q_{X}}\operatorname{KL}(Q_{Y\mid X}\|P_{Y\mid X}).

The conditional term is weighted by the trial law QXQ_{X}. Replacing this weight by the oracle law without a theorem changes the identity.

The chain rule is the prototype of a vertical fiber decomposition: coarse defect plus expected conditional defect.

Entropy-regularized and KL-control formulations of stochastic control are an established neighboring literature: path-integral and linearly-solvable control, maximum-entropy inverse control, control as inference, and soft actor–critic all exploit closely related exponential tilting or KL-penalized objectives (Kappen, 2005; Todorov, 2006; Todorov, 2009; Ziebart et al., 2010; Levine, 2018; Haarnoja et al., 2018). Accordingly, the soft chain identity below is not presented as a new control identity. Its role here is to state the exact normalization and common-loss-scale conditions under which local EG certificates may be composed.

Soft kernels compose in one objective loss scale.

Let

In particular, the global free-energy defect is nonnegative and vanishes exactly at the oracle path law, up to null histories.

18.2 Base change and data processing

Conditional chain rules live at the candidate-law level. Passing them through a representation map and an architecture infimum requires the feasible fine fiber to remain visible. The source box identifies the imported results that justify this step.

Within that imported scope, fix a base-change map from a fine deployment to a coarse deployment. Taking architecture infima gives an exact infimal theorem only when the feasible fine fibers are tracked as a function of the coarse law. The fine obstruction is

Ofine=infQcoarse{Ocoarse​(Qcoarse)+Ψ⁡(Qcoarse)}.O_{\rm fine}=\inf_{Q_{\rm coarse}}\left\{O_{\rm coarse}(Q_{\rm coarse})+\Psi(Q_{\rm coarse})\right\}.

The fiber term depends on coarse occupancy. Replacing it by a constant can be wrong.

Universal equality between fine and coarse obstructions requires canonical-fiber saturation. Objective preservation alone is insufficient.

Pushforward and data processing.

A measurable map reduces relative entropy:

KL(Q∥P)≥KL(T#Q∥T#P).\operatorname{KL}(Q\|P)\geq\operatorname{KL}(T_{\#}Q\|T_{\#}P).

The chain rule used above and this data-processing inequality belong to the classical relative-entropy calculus (Cover and Thomas, 2006; Csiszár, 1975). The difference is a data-processing gap. Equality can imply sufficiency or recoverability under additional assumptions; at architecture level, pushforward can remove an obstruction by quotienting irrelevant labels yet create a fiber-realization tax when the fine architecture cannot reconstruct the canonical conditional law.

18.3 When conditional elimination destroys encoder semantics

The Markovity Conjecture asks whether one may impose U−X−VU-X-V without losing the optimum of a Marton dual problem. The useful EG question is more local: what exactly is eliminated, which observables survive, and which carrier semantics can be destroyed? For a two-receiver broadcast channel, write

GΘ​(p)=−α​H​(Y)−(λ−α)​H​(Z)+I⁡(U,Y)+λ​I​(V,Z)−I⁡(U,V)+𝔼⁡[aX],G_{\Theta}(p)=-\alpha H(Y)-(\lambda-\alpha)H(Z)+I(U;Y)+\lambda I(V;Z)-I(U;V)+\mathbb{E}[a_{X}], (18.7)

where Θ\Theta collects the channel and dual parameters. Conditional Markovization is the declared elimination

(𝖬​p)​(u,v,x)=p⁡(x)​p​(u∣x)​p​(v∣x).(\mathsf{M}p)(u,v,x)=p(x)p(u\mid x)p(v\mid x).

It removes dependence between UU and VV given XX, while preserving the (U,X)(U,X) and (V,X)(V,X) marginals. Thus it preserves everything seen separately by the two receivers, but it need not preserve the semantics H⁡(X∣U,V)=0H(X\mid U,V)=0 of a deterministic encoder. For such an encoder, the exact native ledger is

GΘ​(𝖬​p)−GΘ​(p)=Ip​(U;V∣X)⏟dependence credit−H𝖬​p​(X∣U,V)⏟semantic ambiguity tax.G_{\Theta}(\mathsf{M}p)-G_{\Theta}(p)=\underbrace{I_{p}(U;V\mid X)}_{\text{dependence credit}}-\underbrace{H_{\mathsf{M}p}(X\mid U,V)}_{\text{semantic ambiguity tax}}. (18.8)

The first term is the advertised reward for eliminating conditional dependence. The second is a typed realization loss: after productization, the same pair (u,v)(u,v) may become compatible with several input symbols. In EG language,

𝖬⁡{p:Hp​(X∣U,V)=0}⊈{p:Hp​(X∣U,V)=0}.\mathsf{M}\bigl\{p:H_{p}(X\mid U,V)=0\bigr\}\not\subseteq\bigl\{p:H_{p}(X\mid U,V)=0\bigr\}.

The operation preserves visible marginals but can leave the deterministic carrier class. Rectangular symbol fibers are exactly the zero-tax case.

This ledger changed the search. Instead of asking a local optimizer to find a Markov point directly, the search looked for a nonrectangular deterministic branch on which the semantic tax exceeds the dependence credit. It then separated three logically different gates,

L𝖬​(p)⟶Γrect​(π,m)⟶𝒪rect​(Θ),L_{\mathsf{M}}(p)\quad\longrightarrow\quad\Gamma_{\rm rect}(\pi,m)\quad\longrightarrow\quad\mathcal{O}_{\rm rect}(\Theta), (18.9)

namely loss under direct Markovization, the best rectangular map switch at fixed cell masses, and loss after complete reoptimization over every deterministic rectangular architecture. Failure at either of the first two gates is only a candidate certificate. A counterexample requires the third.

This distinction also exposed the computational blind spot. The ABCA branch is a local maximum separated from the dominant rectangular branch by a finite map-switch barrier. Convergent local searches therefore fall into the rectangular basin and report its value; sampling more starting points does not certify that the other architecture is absent. The finite-change KL/Bregman ledger priced the branch switch, while the EG gate structure routed the final task to branchwise interval certification rather than another local optimization run.

Here ℛdet\mathcal{R}_{\rm det} contains all finite deterministic encoders whose nonempty fibers are rectangles. Write

F⁡(Θ)\displaystyle F(\Theta) =suppGΘ​(p),\displaystyle=\sup_{p}G_{\Theta}(p), Frect​(Θ)\displaystyle F_{\rm rect}(\Theta) =supp∈ℛdetGΘ​(p),\displaystyle=\sup_{p\in\mathcal{R}_{\rm det}}G_{\Theta}(p),
𝒪rect​(Θ)\displaystyle\mathcal{O}_{\rm rect}(\Theta) =F⁡(Θ)−Frect​(Θ).\displaystyle=F(\Theta)-F_{\rm rect}(\Theta).

For every deterministic rectangular candidate qq, the exact architecture ledger is

F⁡(Θ)−GΘ​(q)=𝒪rect​(Θ)⏟architecture error+Frect​(Θ)−GΘ​(q)⏟implementation error.F(\Theta)-G_{\Theta}(q)=\underbrace{\mathcal{O}_{\rm rect}(\Theta)}_{\text{architecture error}}+\underbrace{F_{\rm rect}(\Theta)-G_{\Theta}(q)}_{\text{implementation error}}. (18.10)

It shows why more optimization inside the rectangular class cannot repair the result: it can remove the implementation term, never the architecture term.

Only a short proof bridge is needed after the interval certificate. First, a Markov-class cardinality lemma gives finite attainment. Second, with pU​Vp_{UV} fixed, GΘG_{\Theta} is convex in K=p⁡(x∣u,v)K=p(x\mid u,v). Equality at a global maximum, together with the strict marginal-entropy curvature of −α​H​(Y)−(λ−α)​H​(Z)-\alpha H(Y)-(\lambda-\alpha)H(Z), forces the original maximizing kernel itself to be deterministic whenever a positively weighted output sees every input change. This step uses neither Markovity nor full grid support. For the exact channel, TYT_{Y} is nonsingular. Finally, the published full-support theorem (Gohari et al., 2014, Theorem 1) completes the active grid; determinism plus U−X−VU-X-V then makes every symbol fiber a rectangle. Thus the interval separation excludes the literal Markov optimum as well. The rectangle-cover and generalized-AND/XOR route is not part of this proof.

The proof is classical information theory plus rigorous numerics; it does not depend on EG terminology. EG supplied the discovery and certification architecture: type the eliminated relation, measure the native semantic tax, separate candidate-level failure from architecture-level obstruction, and let the failed gate decide which certificate to build. That is the transferable lesson. The result refutes neither Marton’s achievable region nor the separate Additivity Conjecture.

18.4 Hard limits and composition boundaries

Zero temperature.

A Gibbs defect has the form

1βKL(Q∥Pβ⋆).\frac{1}{\beta}\operatorname{KL}(Q\|P_{\beta}^{\star}).

As β→∞\beta\to\infty, the soft objective approaches hard excess cost under uniform dequantization conditions. For a fixed finite class, minima converge. For temperature-dependent architecture classes, one needs Γ\Gamma-convergence and control of inner and outer limits.

A useful rate has the form

Λβ+osc⁡(D∞)​hβ,\frac{\Lambda}{\beta}+\operatorname{osc}(D_{\infty})h_{\beta},

where hβh_{\beta} measures class convergence. Shared coordination taxes can dequantize at the sharper thermal rate when nested minima share the same perturbation.

Randomized hard limits.

The zero-temperature limit of a soft architecture need not be deterministic. If the architecture closure contains randomized mixtures but not pure selectors, the hard limit can remain randomized. Determinism is a property of the admissible class, not a consequence of low temperature alone.

Interchange curvature.

Two operations may commute individually but fail in a larger context. The Foundations program records this failure by interchange curvature. Operational semantics refines the question: which contexts and tasks can detect the noncommutation?

Examples include:

  • •

    conditioning before versus after representation compression;

  • •

    coupling before versus after elimination;

  • •

    quantization before versus after task projection;

  • •

    temperature limit before versus after architecture restriction.

A composition checklist.

Before composing two certificates, verify:

  1. 1.

    the defects use compatible orientation and units;

  2. 2.

    the conditioning weight is correct;

  3. 3.

    feasible fibers are nonempty and measurable;

  4. 4.

    architecture infima commute only under saturation/rectangularity conditions;

  5. 5.

    representation maps preserve the declared oracle object;

  6. 6.

    limits are uniform or controlled by epi/Γ\Gamma-convergence;

  7. 7.

    downstream tasks expose the retained difference.

Appendix to Chapter 18: complete proofs

Proof of the soft conditional chain theorem

Dependencies. The normalized transitions in (18.2) must be probability kernels, the trial law must be absolutely continuous with respect to the reference path law, and all relative entropies must be well defined. Standard Borel state spaces provide the required regular conditional laws.

Proof.

By multiplying the transition densities in (18.2),

d​Px0β,⋆d​Mx0(x1:m)=exp{−β∑i=1mbiβ(xi,xi−1)}.\frac{dP_{x_{0}}^{\beta,\star}}{dM_{x_{0}}}(x_{1:m})=\exp\!\left\{-\beta\sum_{i=1}^{m}b_{i}^{\beta}(x_{i},x_{i-1})\right\}.

The backward values telescope:

∑i=1mbiβ​(xi,xi−1)\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{m}b_{i}^{\beta}(x_{i},x_{i-1}) =∑i=1m{Ki​(xi,xi−1)+Viβ​(xi)−Vi−1β​(xi−1)}\displaystyle=\sum_{i=1}^{m}\{K_{i}(x_{i},x_{i-1})+V_{i}^{\beta}(x_{i})-V_{i-1}^{\beta}(x_{i-1})\}
=∑i=1mKi​(xi,xi−1)+G⁡(xm)−V0β​(x0).\displaystyle=\sum_{i=1}^{m}K_{i}(x_{i},x_{i-1})+G(x_{m})-V_{0}^{\beta}(x_{0}).

Consequently,

1βKL(Q∥Px0β,⋆)\displaystyle\frac{1}{\beta}\operatorname{KL}(Q\|P_{x_{0}}^{\beta,\star}) =1βKL(Q∥Mx0)+𝔼Q{∑i=1mbiβ(Xi,Xi−1)}\displaystyle=\frac{1}{\beta}\operatorname{KL}(Q\|M_{x_{0}})+\mathbb{E}_{Q}\!\left\{\sum_{i=1}^{m}b_{i}^{\beta}(X_{i},X_{i-1})\right\}
=ℋβ​(Q,x0)−V0β​(x0),\displaystyle=\mathcal{H}_{\beta}(Q;x_{0})-V_{0}^{\beta}(x_{0}),

which proves (18.5).

The relative-entropy chain rule for the two path laws gives

KL(Q∥Px0β,⋆)=∑i=1m𝔼QKL(Qi(⋅∣X0:i−1)∥Piβ,⋆(⋅∣Xi−1)).\operatorname{KL}(Q\|P_{x_{0}}^{\beta,\star})=\sum_{i=1}^{m}\mathbb{E}_{Q}\operatorname{KL}\!\left(Q_{i}(\cdot\mid X_{0:i-1})\,\middle\|\,P_{i}^{\beta,\star}(\cdot\mid X_{i-1})\right).

Divide by β\beta and use (18.4) to obtain (18.6). Each summand is nonnegative. Their sum is zero exactly when the conditional laws agree at every stage outside a QQ-null set; sequential factorization then gives Q=Px0β,⋆Q=P_{x_{0}}^{\beta,\star}. The converse is immediate. ∎

Part V Historical and Conceptual Notes

Three neighboring traditions

The carrier–decoder language meets classical rate–distortion and quantization (Shannon, 1959; Cover and Thomas, 2006; Gray and Neuhoff, 1998); its exact conditional split uses classical Bregman centroid geometry (Banerjee et al., 2005a). Task envelopes use residuation and idempotent projection (Cohen et al., 2004), while contextual equivalence and full abstraction come from programming-language semantics (Milner, 1977; Plotkin, 1977). The soft composition theorem uses the Gibbs variational formula and relative-entropy chain rule (Csiszár, 1975; Cover and Thomas, 2006).

Part V’s claim is not that these three traditions were previously absent. It states which interfaces must be declared before they can be combined.

Question Classical object Part V qualification
What must the carrier retain? source coding, quantization, conditional prediction retain the conditional dual oracle signature needed by the native eliminated objective
What can a task observe? contextual equivalence and full abstraction close a declared task class under a declared min-plus context grammar and use its canonical envelope
When do local costs add? Gibbs normalization and KL chain rule use one reference family, temperature, and telescoping normalization; arbitrary local scores are not composable by declaration

The architecture rate–distortion theorem and the two operational theorems are source-program realizations built on those classical cores. The soft conditional-chain theorem is a classical identity in the book’s typed notation. In particular, contextual observability is a gate or transform, not a third scalar added to carrier loss and decoder nonsaturation.

Part VI Statistical Certification
Data produce a confidence world, not one privileged population story. Its identified image is the complete finite-data answer to a declared query; a resolved certificate is authorized only when that image lies on one side of the operational boundary.

Chapter 19 Confidence Worlds and Statistical Elimination Geometry

Population elimination geometry assumes that the defect, oracle field, architecture grammar, and operational kernel are known. In data analysis they are estimated. Finite data do not select one population world; they leave a set of worlds with inferential standing. Structural conclusions must therefore be transported through that set rather than evaluated only at a point estimate or a favored posterior story.

The statistical layer has one basic chain:

data⟼Cn⟼JCn​(q)⟼δCnq⟼authorized action.\text{data}\longmapsto C_{n}\longmapsto J_{C_{n}}(q)\longmapsto\delta_{C_{n}}^{q}\longmapsto\text{authorized action}.

The confidence world CnC_{n} supplies validity, its identified image JCn​(q)J_{C_{n}}(q) records the full query-relevant uncertainty, and the typed certificate δCnq\delta_{C_{n}}^{q} reports whether the declared boundary is resolved. Only after these objects are fixed should one ask how to acquire more information or deploy a common witness.

19.1 Confidence worlds and finite-data permission

Let 𝒲\mathcal{W} be the universe of complete population worlds. A world specifies every population object needed by the declared query, including nuisance components that may affect its sampling law or future experiments.

Definition 19.1 (Confidence world).

A fixed-record confidence world is a data-dependent random set Cn⊆𝒲C_{n}\subseteq\mathcal{W} satisfying the declared coverage contract, for example the uniform guarantee

infw∈𝒲ℙw{w∈Cn}≥1−α.\inf_{w\in\mathcal{W}}\mathbb{P}_{w}\{w\in C_{n}\}\geq 1-\alpha. (19.1)

It is the set of worlds that remain entitled to participate in the current certificate, not the set of worlds assigned the largest prior or posterior mass.

The construction is a world-level confidence set followed by projection, not a new replacement for confidence-region theory. Simultaneous confidence regions and projection have a long statistical lineage (Scheffé, 1953; Dufour, 1997); universal confidence sets for optimization solutions provide an especially close formal neighbor (Vogel, 2008). The term confidence world records that the set must contain every population component needed by the downstream architecture query.

Coverage is part of the object, not a footnote attached after a claim. The contract must say whether the guarantee is pointwise, uniform, or asymptotic and whether it protects one query, a simultaneous query class, or a data-selected query. If adaptive stopping is allowed, the appropriate object is an anytime confidence-world sequence satisfying

infw∈𝒲ℙw{w∈Ct for every t≥0}≥1−α,\inf_{w\in\mathcal{W}}\mathbb{P}_{w}\{w\in C_{t}\text{ for every }t\geq 0\}\geq 1-\alpha, (19.2)

with every protected query evaluated on the same time-uniform event. This is the confidence-sequence contract of time-uniform inference (Howard et al., 2021), lifted to the complete-world object.

Confidence worlds may be built from parametric confidence regions, distributionally robust sets, moment inequalities, partial-identification regions, valid bootstrap bands, or simultaneous module-wise envelopes. The construction method may change; the coverage and reporting contract may not be left implicit. Conformal prediction (Vovk et al., 2005) can supply a predictive set or one component of such an envelope under its own exchangeability contract; it is not an ancestor of, or substitute for, projection of a population confidence world.

19.2 Identified images, margins, and honest certificates

Before inspecting the data, a query contract declares the population functional or truth map, its tolerance or action boundary, the observer, deployment quantifier, admissible experiment class, and stopping rule. For a real-valued functional Γq\Gamma_{q}, the confidence world induces the identified image

JC​(q)={Γq​(w):w∈C}.J_{C}(q)=\{\Gamma_{q}(w):w\in C\}. (19.3)

This image, rather than a terminal color, is the complete finite-data answer to the query. The color is its projection relative to a declared boundary. Projection of confidence regions and inference under partial identification are established ideas (Dufour, 1997; Imbens and Manski, 2004; Chernozhukov et al., 2007). The book’s contribution is the typed architecture/deployment interpretation of the projected image, not the statistical operation of taking an image of a set.

Definition 19.2 (Standard confidence certificate).

Let q:𝒲→{F,I}q:\mathcal{W}\to\{F,I\} be a declared truth map. For any C⊆𝒲C\subseteq\mathcal{W}, define

δCq={M,C=∅,d,q⁡(C)={d}​ for some ​d∈{F,I},U,|q⁡(C)|≥2.\delta_{C}^{q}=\begin{cases}M,&C=\varnothing,\\ d,&q(C)=\{d\}\text{ for some }d\in\{F,I\},\\ U,&|q(C)|\geq 2.\end{cases} (19.4)

Here MM records model conflict, while UU records genuine disagreement among compatible worlds. Neither state authorizes a binary population claim.

For the threshold query

q(w)=F⟺Γq(w)≤εq,q(w)=F\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\Gamma_{q}(w)\leq\varepsilon_{q},

suppose the nonempty identified image is the interval JC​(q)=[LC,UC]J_{C}(q)=[L_{C},U_{C}]. Then

δCq={F,UC≤εq,I,LC>εq,U,LC≤εq<UC.\delta_{C}^{q}=\begin{cases}F,&U_{C}\leq\varepsilon_{q},\\ I,&L_{C}>\varepsilon_{q},\\ U,&L_{C}\leq\varepsilon_{q}<U_{C}.\end{cases}

The associated certificate margin is

mC​(q)={εq−UC,δCq=F,LC−εq,δCq=I,0,δCq=U.m_{C}(q)=\begin{cases}\varepsilon_{q}-U_{C},&\delta_{C}^{q}=F,\\ L_{C}-\varepsilon_{q},&\delta_{C}^{q}=I,\\ 0,&\delta_{C}^{q}=U.\end{cases} (19.5)

No margin is assigned to the model-conflict state. A positive margin records how far the entire identified image lies from a label change; the full map ε↦δCq​(ε)\varepsilon\mapsto\delta_{C}^{q}(\varepsilon) is the tolerance profile. Reporting the image and margin permits another stakeholder to audit a different declared tolerance without reconstructing the population world set.

The threshold readout is also continuous with the classical equivalence and noninferiority literature (Blackwelder, 1982; Berger and Hsu, 1996; Piaggio et al., 2006; Schuirmann, 1987; Lakens, 2017). The familiar two-one-sided-tests procedure is a two-sided sibling of this set rule, not its source: here a single resolved label is authorized only when the entire covered image lies on the declared side of the boundary.

Theorem 19.3 (Honesty and maximal decisiveness).

On the coverage event, every resolved output of the standard confidence certificate is correct. Among the comparator rules just declared, it is maximally decisive: it returns the common truth label whenever all compatible worlds agree and returns unresolved otherwise.

Three kinds of unresolvedness.

Statistical unresolvedness means that compatible population worlds imply opposite answers; computational unresolvedness means that the exact identified image is defined but has not been computed; search unresolvedness means that no witness has been found within the declared budget. The remedies differ: more computation cannot resolve the first, and more data cannot by itself repair a misspecified grammar.

The compatible-world logic is rooted in partial identification (Manski, 2003), with projection confidence procedures providing a nearby inferential comparison (Kaido et al., 2019). The book’s additional step is to require one auditable architecture certificate under the declared deployment quantifier.

As a running anchor, Section 20.4.2 constructs one 95% simultaneous confidence world for the 12 department–sex admission probabilities in UCBAdmissions. Its projection through the maximum department difference is [−0.0895,0.3109][-0.0895,0.3109]; relative to the tolerance 0.100.10, the standard certificate is UU. The full audit later shows why a tiny pooled pp-value does not replace this worldwise conclusion.

19.3 Defect envelopes and architecture grammars

The generic objects become structural by projecting a confidence world through the defect field and the architecture grammar. Suppose a simultaneous event provides lower and upper defect envelopes

D¯x​(a)≤Dx⋆​(a)≤D¯x​(a)\underline{D}_{x}(a)\leq D_{x}^{\star}(a)\leq\overline{D}_{x}(a)

for all relevant (x,a)(x,a). Suppose also that the true architecture lies between inner and outer grammars

𝔄¯r⊆𝔄r⋆⊆𝔄¯r\underline{\mathfrak{A}}_{r}\subseteq\mathfrak{A}_{r}^{\star}\subseteq\overline{\mathfrak{A}}_{r}

for every resource budget rr.

Simultaneous objective and feasible-set envelopes of this type are standard tools in stochastic and robust optimization (Vogel, 2008; Berk et al., 2013); the point here is to preserve their common event through elimination.

Use monotone ρ=Pn\rho=P_{n} for empirical risk, or ρ=P\rho=P for confidence-controlled population risk.

O¯​(r)\displaystyle\underline{O}(r) =infA∈𝔄¯rρ⁡(D¯A),\displaystyle=\inf_{A\in\overline{\mathfrak{A}}_{r}}\rho(\underline{D}_{A}),
O⋆​(r)\displaystyle O^{\star}(r) =infA∈𝔄r⋆ρ⁡(DA⋆),\displaystyle=\inf_{A\in\mathfrak{A}_{r}^{\star}}\rho(D_{A}^{\star}),
O¯​(r)\displaystyle\overline{O}(r) =infA∈𝔄¯rρ⁡(D¯A).\displaystyle=\inf_{A\in\underline{\mathfrak{A}}_{r}}\rho(\overline{D}_{A}).

The directions are deliberately reversed: a larger architecture and smaller defect produce a lower bound; a smaller architecture and larger defect produce an upper bound.

Theorem 19.4 (Honest elimination bracket).

On the simultaneous confidence event,

O¯​(r)≤O⋆​(r)≤O¯​(r)\underline{O}(r)\leq O^{\star}(r)\leq\overline{O}(r)

for all declared resource budgets rr simultaneously.

At threshold τ\tau, the bracket gives the safe readout

certified feasible :O¯≤τ,\displaystyle:\quad\overline{O}\leq\tau,
certified impossible :O¯>τ,\displaystyle:\quad\underline{O}>\tau,
unresolved :O¯≤τ<O¯.\displaystyle:\quad\underline{O}\leq\tau<\overline{O}.

If [O¯,O¯][\underline{O},\overline{O}] is the exact identified image of the frontier over CnC_{n}, this is the standard certificate above. If it is only an outer enclosure, the two resolved declarations remain honest, while the unresolved region can also contain conservatism from the enclosure.

19.4 Persistent atlases and operational transport

Persistent atlas number.

Uniformity over rr permits data-dependent resource selection without a second pointwise argument. For tolerance τ\tau, define the minimum chart number using the convention that a “KK-chart deployment” has at most KK nonempty charts; an atlas with fewer charts may be padded by empty or repeated charts. Thus feasibility is monotone in KK. Put

KD​(τ)=min⁡{K:there exists a K-chart deployment with uniform defect≤τ}.K_{D}(\tau)=\min\left\{K:\text{there exists a $K$-chart deployment with uniform defect}\leq\tau\right\}.

The integer-valued curve can jump under small perturbations. Define the inverse frontier

LD​(K)=inf{τ:KD​(τ)≤K}.L_{D}(K)=\inf\{\tau:K_{D}(\tau)\leq K\}.

The inversion between a cover by at most KK local sections and a KK-chart description is definitional. It is not the theorem below. Chart autoencoders, multi-chart flows, and atlas generative models already use multi-chart representations (Schonsheck et al., 2019; Kalatzis et al., 2021; Stolberg-Larsen and Sommer, 2021); the theorem concerns stability of the declared loss frontier under a uniform defect perturbation.

The sharp interleaving and inverse-frontier stability theorem is developed canonically in the Statistical EG companion (Huang and Wang, 2026m). The EGML companion reuses that interface for its learning-facing atlas and one-sided certificate ledger (Huang and Wang, 2026d); the book records the mathematical statement once, in the stronger extended-valued form below.

Theorem 19.5 (Atlas interleaving and stable inverse).

If

‖D−D^‖∞≤ϵ,\|D-\widehat{D}\|_{\infty}\leq\epsilon,

then the atlas curves are horizontally interleaved by ϵ\epsilon, and

LD^​(K)≤LD​(K)+ϵ,LD​(K)≤LD^​(K)+ϵL_{\widehat{D}}(K)\leq L_{D}(K)+\epsilon,\qquad L_{D}(K)\leq L_{\widehat{D}}(K)+\epsilon

in the extended order for every KK. Whenever either inverse frontier is finite, both are finite and therefore

|LD​(K)−LD^​(K)|≤ϵ.|L_{D}(K)-L_{\widehat{D}}(K)|\leq\epsilon.

The constant one on the finite part is sharp.

The inverse chart-budget/loss frontier is therefore the statistically stable object. This filtration-and-confidence viewpoint is adjacent to confidence sets for persistence diagrams (Fasy et al., 2014), but the object stabilized here is an architecture loss frontier rather than a homological summary. The underlying interleaving logic is the standard stability mechanism for filtered objects (de Silva et al., 2018; Mémoli et al., 2024).

Nonexpansive operational transport.

Task envelopes and contextual closure are nonexpansive in sup norm. Consequently, if internal kernels are simultaneously bracketed, observable architecture frontiers inherit the same confidence event without a new stochastic proof. This is an important design principle: prove deterministic nonexpansiveness once, then reuse the statistical envelope.

19.4.1 Pointwise feasibility versus common deployment

The standard confidence certificate asks whether each compatible population world is feasible. Deployment demands a stronger quantifier: one architecture must work throughout the confidence world. Let CC be a nonempty set of compatible worlds, let 𝔄R\mathfrak{A}_{R} be the class admitted by resource budget RR, and let ℓθ​(A)≥0\ell_{\theta}(A)\geq 0 be the declared audit loss. At tolerance η\eta, put

𝔉Rη​(θ)={A∈𝔄R:ℓθ​(A)≤η}.\mathfrak{F}_{R}^{\eta}(\theta)=\{A\in\mathfrak{A}_{R}:\ell_{\theta}(A)\leq\eta\}.

Define

Vlo​(C,R)\displaystyle V_{\rm lo}(C;R) =infθ∈CinfA∈𝔄Rℓθ​(A),\displaystyle=\inf_{\theta\in C}\inf_{A\in\mathfrak{A}_{R}}\ell_{\theta}(A), (19.6)
Vpw​(C,R)\displaystyle V_{\rm pw}(C;R) =supθ∈CinfA∈𝔄Rℓθ​(A),\displaystyle=\sup_{\theta\in C}\inf_{A\in\mathfrak{A}_{R}}\ell_{\theta}(A), (19.7)
Vcd​(C,R)\displaystyle V_{\rm cd}(C;R) =infA∈𝔄Rsupθ∈Cℓθ​(A).\displaystyle=\inf_{A\in\mathfrak{A}_{R}}\sup_{\theta\in C}\ell_{\theta}(A). (19.8)
Theorem 19.6 (Common-deployment quantifier theorem).

For every nonempty CC and 𝔄R\mathfrak{A}_{R},

Vlo​(C,R)≤Vpw​(C,R)≤Vcd​(C,R).V_{\rm lo}(C;R)\leq V_{\rm pw}(C;R)\leq V_{\rm cd}(C;R).

Under the attainment condition:

  1. 1.

    Vlo>ηV_{\rm lo}>\eta exactly when every compatible world is individually impossible at budget RR;

  2. 2.

    Vpw≤ηV_{\rm pw}\leq\eta exactly when every compatible world is individually feasible;

  3. 3.

    Vcd≤ηV_{\rm cd}\leq\eta exactly when ⋂θ∈C𝔉Rη​(θ)\bigcap_{\theta\in C}\mathfrak{F}_{R}^{\eta}(\theta) is nonempty.

Both inequalities can be strict. In particular, pointwise feasibility in every compatible world need not provide a common deployable witness.

Example 19.7 (A minimal common-witness conflict).

Let C={θ0,θ1}C=\{\theta_{0},\theta_{1}\}, 𝔄R={A0,A1}\mathfrak{A}_{R}=\{A_{0},A_{1}\}, and let the loss table be

θ0θ1A001A110.\begin{array}[]{c|cc}&\theta_{0}&\theta_{1}\\ \hline\cr A_{0}&0&1\\ A_{1}&1&0\end{array}.

At tolerance η=0\eta=0, each world has a zero-loss architecture, so Vpw=0V_{\rm pw}=0, but every fixed architecture has worst-world loss one, so Vcd=1V_{\rm cd}=1. Pointwise feasibility is complete while common deployment fails.

Suppose now that (Ct)t≥0(C_{t})_{t\geq 0} is an anytime-valid confidence sequence, so one time-uniform event of probability at least 1−α1-\alpha satisfies θ∈Ct\theta\in C_{t} for every tt. At any stopping time τ\tau, every ℱτ\mathcal{F}_{\tau}-measurable witness in the feasible-set intersection is then valid in the true world. A fixed-time simultaneous confidence set alone does not justify this optional-stopping conclusion. Nor does a confidence world license choosing a different witness for each still-compatible world and presenting that family as one deployed system.

19.4.2 Distribution-free prediction under conditional and shift contracts

Prediction sets make the common-deployment quantifier visible without any architecture terminology. Under exchangeability, a conformal rule can guarantee marginal coverage for a future observation. That contract does not imply exact conditional coverage at every covariate value over a rich distribution class: distribution-free conditional guarantees can force essentially uninformative sets unless the conditioning class, distribution family, or target notion is restricted (Barber et al., 2021). Pointwise existence of a short, well-calibrated set in each compatible world therefore does not exhibit one data-dependent set rule that is simultaneously short and conditionally valid throughout the confidence world.

Covariate shift supplies a different repair only under a different declared experiment. Weighted conformal methods can recover a target-population coverage statement when the conditional law of the response given covariates is invariant and the source-to-target density ratio is known or estimated well enough for the stated guarantee (Tibshirani et al., 2019). The ratio is an information carrier, not a free optimizer improvement. If the conditional law also shifts, or target support lies outside source support, reweighting does not close the contract.

The typed repair choices are consequently distinct: enlarge the output to a set, allow abstention or an “unresolved” action, collect target-domain calibration data, or restrict the target/conditioning domain. Tuning the same point predictor cannot by itself supply missing exchangeability, overlap, or conditional information.

19.4.3 Statistical ancestry: pointwise success is not uniform deployment

The common-deployment quantifier is not detached from classical statistics. The Hodges–Le Cam superefficiency example already shows that an estimator may have exceptional asymptotic risk at one fixed parameter while paying for that behavior on a neighborhood that contracts with sample size (Le Cam, 1953). Hájek’s convolution and local asymptotic minimax theory then made regularity and locally uniform risk comparison central (Hájek, 1970; Hájek, 1972). The lesson is not that pointwise results are false. It is that their quantifiers cannot be exchanged without proof.

Sparse estimation exhibits the same problem sharply. An oracle property is normally a statement at each fixed parameter: asymptotically, the procedure behaves like an estimator that knew the true submodel in advance. Leeb–Pötscher show why such pointwise asymptotics can coexist with severe nonuniformity and poor maximal risk (Leeb and Pötscher, 2005; Leeb and Pötscher, 2008). Thus

∀θ​∃n0​(θ)⇏∃n0​∀θ.\forall\theta\ \exists n_{0}(\theta)\quad\not\Rightarrow\quad\exists n_{0}\ \forall\theta.

The deployment rule and sample size are fixed before the unknown world is revealed; the second order of quantifiers is the relevant one.

19.5 A complete quantifier case: sparse model-selection procedures with pointwise oracle guarantees

The class at issue consists of support-selecting procedures whose oracle guarantees are pointwise in the underlying parameter. It includes nonconcave penalization, data-adaptive weighted penalization, and exact or algorithmic ℓ0\ell_{0} subset selection. SCAD, Adaptive LASSO, and BSS/BeSS below are coordinate-level representatives of this class, not its name.

Consider one coordinate of an orthogonal Gaussian regression experiment,

Zj=βj+σn​εj,εj∼N⁡(0,1),Z_{j}=\beta_{j}+\frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{n}}\varepsilon_{j},\qquad\varepsilon_{j}\sim N(0,1),

with every penalized objective normalized as

12​(Zj−b)2+penn⁡(b).\frac{1}{2}(Z_{j}-b)^{2}+\operatorname{pen}_{n}(b).

This coordinate model exposes the thresholds exactly. General designs add design identifiability, pilot, and optimization conditions, but do not remove the quantifier conflict.

19.5.1 SCAD: fixed-signal unbiasedness leaves a moving transition band

For SCAD parameter a>2a>2, the orthogonal coordinate solution is

β^jSCAD={sgn⁡(Zj)​(|Zj|−λn)+,|Zj|≤2​λn,(a−1)​Zj−sgn⁡(Zj)​a​λna−2,2​λn<|Zj|≤a​λn,Zj,|Zj|>a​λn.\widehat{\beta}_{j}^{\rm SCAD}=\begin{cases}\operatorname{sgn}(Z_{j})(|Z_{j}|-\lambda_{n})_{+},&|Z_{j}|\leq 2\lambda_{n},\\[5.69054pt] \displaystyle\frac{(a-1)Z_{j}-\operatorname{sgn}(Z_{j})a\lambda_{n}}{a-2},&2\lambda_{n}<|Z_{j}|\leq a\lambda_{n},\\[8.53581pt] Z_{j},&|Z_{j}|>a\lambda_{n}.\end{cases}

Under the usual oracle scaling λn→0\lambda_{n}\to 0 and n​λn→∞\sqrt{n}\lambda_{n}\to\infty, every fixed nonzero coordinate eventually enters the unpenalized region, while a fixed zero coordinate is deleted with probability tending to one (Fan and Li, 2001). But for the moving world βj,n=c​λn\beta_{j,n}=c\lambda_{n}, 0<c<10<c<1, one has Zj/λn→cZ_{j}/\lambda_{n}\to c in probability. The coordinate is therefore set to zero with probability tending to one, and

n​𝔼βj,n​(β^jSCAD−βj,n)2≥(c2+o⁡(1))​n​λn2⟶∞.n\,\mathbb{E}_{\beta_{j,n}}(\widehat{\beta}_{j}^{\rm SCAD}-\beta_{j,n})^{2}\geq(c^{2}+o(1))n\lambda_{n}^{2}\longrightarrow\infty.

SCAD removes persistent shrinkage bias for fixed large signals; it relocates, rather than eliminates, the price to a threshold band moving toward zero.

19.5.2 Adaptive LASSO: the conflict moves into a random weight

Use the same score as pilot and let wj=|Zj|−γw_{j}=|Z_{j}|^{-\gamma}, γ>0\gamma>0. The coordinate solution is

β^jAL=sgn⁡(Zj)​(|Zj|−λn|Zj|γ)+.\widehat{\beta}_{j}^{\rm AL}=\operatorname{sgn}(Z_{j})\left(|Z_{j}|-\frac{\lambda_{n}}{|Z_{j}|^{\gamma}}\right)_{+}.

Its effective threshold is

tn=λn1/(γ+1),β^jAL≠0⟺|Zj|>tn.t_{n}=\lambda_{n}^{1/(\gamma+1)},\qquad\widehat{\beta}_{j}^{\rm AL}\neq 0\Longleftrightarrow|Z_{j}|>t_{n}.

In the present normalization, the classical pointwise oracle conditions can be written

n​λn→0,n(γ+1)/2​λn→∞.\sqrt{n}\lambda_{n}\to 0,\qquad n^{(\gamma+1)/2}\lambda_{n}\to\infty.

The first makes the penalty negligible at a fixed nonzero coordinate; the second is equivalent to n​tn→∞\sqrt{n}t_{n}\to\infty and deletes a fixed zero coordinate (Zou, 2006). At the moving world βj,n=c​tn\beta_{j,n}=ct_{n}, 0<c<10<c<1, however, Zj/tn→cZ_{j}/t_{n}\to c, so deletion occurs with probability tending to one and

n​𝔼βj,n​(β^jAL−βj,n)2≥(c2+o⁡(1))​n​tn2⟶∞.n\,\mathbb{E}_{\beta_{j,n}}(\widehat{\beta}_{j}^{\rm AL}-\beta_{j,n})^{2}\geq(c^{2}+o(1))nt_{n}^{2}\longrightarrow\infty.

Adaptive weighting resolves an important fixed-zero/fixed-nonzero conflict of ordinary LASSO, but near zero the pilot amplifies its own noise. The nonuniform region becomes a pilot-dependent lockout region.

19.5.3 BSS and BeSS: a method-specific repair cannot create information

The one-dimensional ℓ0\ell_{0} objective

12(Zj−b)2+μn𝟏{b≠0}\frac{1}{2}(Z_{j}-b)^{2}+\mu_{n}\mathbf{1}\{b\neq 0\}

has the global hard-threshold solution

β^jBSS=Zj𝟏{|Zj|>un},un=2​μn.\widehat{\beta}_{j}^{\rm BSS}=Z_{j}\mathbf{1}\{|Z_{j}|>u_{n}\},\qquad u_{n}=\sqrt{2\mu_{n}}.

If un→0u_{n}\to 0 and n​un→∞\sqrt{n}u_{n}\to\infty, it has the same fixed-parameter oracle pattern and the same failure of uniformity at βj,n≍un\beta_{j,n}\asymp u_{n}. For one already frozen Adaptive-LASSO rule, choosing un/tn→0u_{n}/t_{n}\to 0 lets BSS recover signals in the corridor

un≪|βj,n|≲tn.u_{n}\ll|\beta_{j,n}|\lesssim t_{n}.

That is a genuine rule-specific repair. It is not a new information bound: the Adaptive-LASSO sequence could itself be retuned, and both rules still use the same observation.

For a general design, exact BSS additionally needs a subset-identifiability margin, while an approximate solver must spend part of that margin on optimization error. BeSS searches subsets by a primal–dual active-set algorithm and selects model size by an additional sequential or golden-section rule (Wen et al., 2020). Even if BeSS is assumed to return the exact global BSS solution, it removes only failures caused by pilot weights, convex relaxation, or optimization. Exact support recovery still requires signal separation and design identifiability (Guo et al., 2020).

19.5.4 The information-limited core and the honest action

Compare the local worlds

βj(0)=0,βj,n(1)=hn.\beta_{j}^{(0)}=0,\qquad\beta_{j,n}^{(1)}=\frac{h}{\sqrt{n}}.

Their Kullback–Leibler divergence is h2/(2​σ2)h^{2}/(2\sigma^{2}) and does not diverge with nn. Every support selector S^n\widehat{S}_{n} therefore obeys the two-point testing bound

Pβ(0)​(j∈S^n)+Pβn(1)​(j∉S^n)≥1−TV⁡{Pβ(0),Pβn(1)}>0.P_{\beta^{(0)}}(j\in\widehat{S}_{n})+P_{\beta_{n}^{(1)}}(j\notin\widehat{S}_{n})\geq 1-\operatorname{TV}\{P_{\beta^{(0)}},P_{\beta_{n}^{(1)}}\}>0.

No support-selecting sparse procedure with only a pointwise oracle guarantee can uniformly recover support on a parameter class containing these local worlds; this includes all three representative mechanisms above. In a high-dimensional multiple-coordinate problem, the corresponding separation scale is typically enlarged to order σ​log⁡p/n\sigma\sqrt{\log p/n}, with constants depending on the design and error criterion.

There are consequently two different blind regions. A method-induced region, such as pilot-weight lockout, can be narrowed by BSS/BeSS. An information-theoretic indistinguishability region cannot be removed by any selector using the same data. A uniform support claim must either restrict the parameter domain, for example to

Θn​(bn)={β:minj∈S⁡(β)⁡|βj|≥bn},\Theta_{n}(b_{n})=\left\{\beta:\min_{j\in S(\beta)}|\beta_{j}|\geq b_{n}\right\},

with its design margin, model-size rule, and optimization error declared, or report a three-way action: stably nonzero, stably zero, or unresolved.

19.6 Main interface theorem family: observational overlap and deployment conflict

The sparse example raises a general question. If every world has its own low-risk architecture, can the data reliably select the required one at deployment time? Let the finite world set be 𝒲={0,…,m−1}\mathcal{W}=\{0,\ldots,m-1\} and Y∼PwY\sim P_{w}. Put

μ=1m​∑w=0m−1Pw,pw=d​Pwd​μ.\mu=\frac{1}{m}\sum_{w=0}^{m-1}P_{w},\qquad p_{w}=\frac{\,\mathrm{d}P_{w}}{\,\mathrm{d}\mu}.

Let the deployment action space 𝒜\mathcal{A} be compact metric, let each native loss Dw​(a)D_{w}(a) be lower semicontinuous in aa, and define

Fη​(w)={a∈𝒜:Dw​(a)≤η},𝒲⁡(y)={w:pw​(y)>0}.F_{\eta}(w)=\{a\in\mathcal{A}:D_{w}(a)\leq\eta\},\qquad\mathcal{W}(y)=\{w:p_{w}(y)>0\}.
Theorem 19.8 (Deployment conflict under observational overlap).

Under the preceding conditions:

  1. 1.

    A measurable deployment rule δ⁡(Y)\delta(Y) satisfying

    Dw​{δ⁡(Y)}≤ηPw​-a.s. for every ​wD_{w}\{\delta(Y)\}\leq\eta\qquad P_{w}\text{-a.s. for every }w

    exists if and only if

    ⋂w∈𝒲⁡(y)Fη​(w)≠∅for μ-a.e. y with 𝒲⁡(y)≠∅.\bigcap_{w\in\mathcal{W}(y)}F_{\eta}(w)\neq\varnothing\quad\text{for $\mu$-a.e. $y$ with $\mathcal{W}(y)\neq\varnothing$.} (DC-E)
  2. 2.

    For two worlds and two candidate architectures, suppose

    Δ0=D0​(a1)−D0​(a0)>0,Δ1=D1​(a0)−D1​(a1)>0.\Delta_{0}=D_{0}(a_{1})-D_{0}(a_{0})>0,\qquad\Delta_{1}=D_{1}(a_{0})-D_{1}(a_{1})>0.

    Every measurable rule taking values in {a0,a1}\{a_{0},a_{1}\} satisfies

    maxi∈{0,1}⁡𝔼i​[Di​{δ⁡(Y)}−Di​(ai)]≥Δ0​Δ1Δ0+Δ1​{1−TV⁡(P0,P1)}.\max_{i\in\{0,1\}}\mathbb{E}_{i}\!\left[D_{i}\{\delta(Y)\}-D_{i}(a_{i})\right]\geq\frac{\Delta_{0}\Delta_{1}}{\Delta_{0}+\Delta_{1}}\{1-\operatorname{TV}(P_{0},P_{1})\}. (DC-R)

    When Δ0=Δ1=Δ\Delta_{0}=\Delta_{1}=\Delta, the right side is Δ⁡{1−TV⁡(P0,P1)}/2\Delta\{1-\operatorname{TV}(P_{0},P_{1})\}/2. The same number is the exact equal-prior mean-regret Bayes value, attained by a likelihood-ratio rule. The maximum-regret lower bound is not claimed sharp for every asymmetric experiment.

Corollary 19.9 (Repair trichotomy and invariance).

For the problem in Theorem 19.8:

  1. 1.

    changing only the optimizer, while preserving PwP_{w}, DwD_{w}, and 𝒜\mathcal{A}, changes neither (DC-E) nor the bound (DC-R);

  2. 2.

    an information or exposure repair changes the experiment PwP_{w}, and may reduce overlap by increasing total variation;

  3. 3.

    an architecture or class repair changes 𝒜\mathcal{A} and the feasible sets Fη​(w)F_{\eta}(w), and may create a common acceptable action without changing the observations.

An empirical case can therefore claim that this interface changed an architecture choice only if it froze the experiment/information carrier, native loss, action class, and compute contract before confirmation, and the mechanism-matched repair beats equal-information, equal-compute controls on a separately declared endpoint.

19.6.1 Treatment policies under observational overlap and deployment constraints

Let YY denote the observational calibration record used to select a policy, let π\pi map deployment covariates to a treatment in {0,1}\{0,1\}, and let Dw​(π)D_{w}(\pi) be negative policy welfare or regret in causal world ww. Each compatible world may have its own optimal policy. If two calibration-data laws P0,P1P_{0},P_{1} overlap while the preferred policies π0,π1\pi_{0},\pi_{1} reverse and have positive cross-gaps, then Theorem 19.8 lower-bounds the regret of every selector that must choose from {π0,π1}\{\pi_{0},\pi_{1}\} using only YY. The statement concerns the frozen observational experiment and policy class; it is not a causal identification theorem.

Orthogonal nuisance estimation, double/debiased machine learning, heterogeneous-effect learners, and observational policy learning can improve effect or value estimation under their identification and regularity assumptions (Chernozhukov et al., 2018; Athey and Wager, 2021). They do not by themselves create positivity, measure an unobserved confounder, or transport effects to a population unsupported by the data. When opposite treatment preferences remain observationally indistinguishable, replacing the learner while preserving (Pw,Dw,𝒜)(P_{w},D_{w},\mathcal{A}) leaves the deployment-conflict certificate unchanged.

The certificate instead points to typed repairs. Randomization, an additional effect modifier, or a valid proxy changes the information experiment; a referral/abstention option or a richer dynamic policy changes the action class; restricting to an overlap population changes the deployment domain. Any claim that the repair changed policy architecture must freeze these choices and compare the mechanism-matched intervention against equal-information, equal-compute controls on independent units.

The preceding theorem separates information repair from architecture repair abstractly. The next family makes the architecture side computable for one important inverse problem. Under the same information carrier and native loss, the certificate therefore changes the admissible architecture choice from a one-pass thresholded-affine encoder to a recurrent or unrolled repair of sufficient depth.

19.7.1 A no-free-lunch theorem for hidden winding

In the radical architecture, the one-chart obstruction is zero or one according to a divisibility condition on the target degree after normalization. With finitely many sampled angles and no regularity or coverage condition, a winding can be inserted into an unsampled interval. The observed data can then be identical under feasible and impossible population worlds. Integer-wrap and phase-unwrapping formulations provide the classical computational background (Itoh, 1982; Goldstein et al., 1988; Costantini, 1998; Yokoyama, 1997). Information-based complexity results for topological degree of multidimensional Lipschitz maps provide a further neighboring lower-bound tradition (Boult and Sikorski, 1986). That cube problem is not identical to the present one-dimensional circle-winding contract.

Therefore no uniformly valid binary procedure can be informative in general. An honest procedure must sometimes return unresolved.

19.8 Identification, hidden winding, and data-dependent architecture

Degree identification under regularity.

Assume the target phase is LL-Lipschitz and observed with bounded angular error. The set of degrees compatible with the data can be described exactly by a finite mixed-integer program. Divisibility of the entire identification set yields a valid radical certificate.

A local spacing condition can collapse the identification set to one degree. Under uniform random design, upper and lower sample-complexity bounds match at order

L⁡{log⁡L+log⁡(1/α)}L\{\log L+\log(1/\alpha)\}

for the square-root parity problem.

The rate is governed by coverage of locations where an obstruction can hide, not only by pointwise estimation accuracy. The limited novelty claim is the noisy exact mixed-integer identification set together with the random-design logarithmic coverage surcharge. The bare fact that a degree-LL loop requires order-LL spatial resolution is not claimed as new.

Sample splitting and data-dependent architecture.

A practical OALI analysis can use three independent levels:

  1. 1.

    calibration data estimate local oracles, transports, and obstruction certificates;

  2. 2.

    tuning data choose among a finite repair library and fit architectures;

  3. 3.

    held-out biological units evaluate final operational performance.

This design avoids the need for a fully general random-set theorem in the first implementation, though such theory remains valuable for data efficiency.

Exercise 19.14.

Exercise 19.15.

Construct two circle maps that agree on a finite sample but have different winding parity.

Appendix to Chapter 19: complete proofs

Proof of honesty and maximal decisiveness

Dependencies. The confidence world must cover the true population world. The query and its truth map are declared, and the exact truth image q⁡(C)q(C) is available. Compactness is unnecessary for the set-inclusion rule; it is needed only if one replaces the identified image by attained lower and upper endpoints.

Proof.

Fix a realized nonempty confidence world CC. If q⁡(C)={d}q(C)=\{d\}, then every compatible world has truth label dd. On the event that the true world belongs to CC, the resolved output is therefore correct. Thus any false resolved declaration implies failure of confidence-world coverage, whose probability is at most α\alpha.

For maximal decisiveness, suppose q⁡(C)q(C) contains both FF and II. An FF declaration is incorrect in a compatible II-world, while an II declaration is incorrect in a compatible FF-world. Hence no rule required to be correct for every world in CC may make either terminal declaration. The unresolved output is forced. If q⁡(C)q(C) is a singleton, the standard certificate reports its common label. It therefore declares in every and only every case in which a worldwise-correct comparator can declare. When C=∅C=\varnothing, the separate output MM records model conflict and makes no population claim. ∎

Proof of the honest elimination bracket

Dependencies. One simultaneous event must contain both the pointwise defect envelopes and the inner/outer grammar inclusions for every resource budget under consideration. The same declared risk functional is used for all three frontiers and must be monotone; translation equivariance is useful for perturbation bounds but not needed for the bracket itself.

Proof.

Fix a resource budget rr. On the simultaneous event, for every A∈𝔄r⋆A\in\mathfrak{A}_{r}^{\star},

ρ⁡{D¯​(A,⋅)}≤ρ⁡{D⋆​(A,⋅)}≤ρ⁡{D¯​(A,⋅)}\rho\{\underline{D}(A,\cdot)\}\leq\rho\{D^{\star}(A,\cdot)\}\leq\rho\{\overline{D}(A,\cdot)\}

by monotonicity. Moreover,

𝔄¯r⊆𝔄r⋆⊆𝔄¯r.\underline{\mathfrak{A}}_{r}\subseteq\mathfrak{A}_{r}^{\star}\subseteq\overline{\mathfrak{A}}_{r}.

Enlarging a feasible set can only decrease an infimum, while restricting it can only increase an infimum. Hence

infA∈𝔄¯rρ⁡{D¯​(A,⋅)}≤infA∈𝔄r⋆ρ⁡{D⋆​(A,⋅)}≤infA∈𝔄¯rρ⁡{D¯​(A,⋅)}.\inf_{A\in\overline{\mathfrak{A}}_{r}}\rho\{\underline{D}(A,\cdot)\}\leq\inf_{A\in\mathfrak{A}_{r}^{\star}}\rho\{D^{\star}(A,\cdot)\}\leq\inf_{A\in\underline{\mathfrak{A}}_{r}}\rho\{\overline{D}(A,\cdot)\}.

The middle term is O⋆​(r)O^{\star}(r). Because the event is simultaneous in rr, the same deterministic inequalities hold for every declared budget at once. If the event has probability at least 1−α1-\alpha uniformly over population worlds, the complete frontier bracket is uniformly honest at that level. ∎

Dependencies. The defects are continuous only to make the local-section formulation standard; the numerical interleaving itself uses the uniform sup-norm bound.
