Chapter 20 Certificate Statistics and Resolution Complexity

20.1 The certificate record and four nonexchangeable objects

An estimate or posterior alone does not record which population worlds remain compatible with the data, which decision boundary is being audited, or why the answer remains unresolved. Certificate statistics treats the primary finite-information output as a typed record.

A certificate record contains:

  • •

    a declared query contract and operational boundary BB;

  • •

    a confidence world CnC_{n} with an explicit coverage contract;

  • •

    the identified image JCn​(q)J_{C_{n}}(q) and current certificate color;

  • •

    the certificate margin or tolerance profile when the query is ordered;

  • •

    evidence or witnesses supporting the color;

  • •

    a resolution profile indicating what information is still needed.

The record connects four objects without identifying their validity contracts.

Object Evaluated on What it can guarantee
population truth q⁡(w)q(w) one fixed population world ww the task cell that is true at the population level
confidence certificate δCnq\delta_{C_{n}}^{q} a covered confidence world CnC_{n} worldwise error control for every resolved finite-data declaration
posterior color χ⁡(bn)\chi(b_{n}) a prior-relative belief state bnb_{n} a summary of current posterior belief, not uniform validity over worlds
deployment action ana_{n} observer-visible information and the declared deployment grammar operational loss control only when one admissible action or witness works across the required worlds

The four objects can constrain one another, but agreement of their displayed labels does not make them interchangeable. A resolved confidence certificate is not yet a common deployment witness, and high posterior probability is not by itself a worldwise certificate.

Reject-option classification and three-way decision theory are important neighbors (Chow, 1970; Yao, 2010). They optimize or summarize actions under a probabilistic or loss-based contract. Proposition 20.1 isolates a different question: whether one terminal label is correct simultaneously for every world retained by a confidence set. The distinction, not abstention itself, is the point.

Proposition 20.1 (Posterior credibility is not worldwise validity).

For any fixed posterior credibility level below one, there exist a prior and two observationally indistinguishable worlds with opposite certificate colors such that the posterior assigns high probability to one color at every time, while the minority world is reported incorrectly with probability one. Under the available experiment family the corresponding worldwise resolution complexity is infinite.

20.1.1 Truth-map notation for the standard certificate

The preceding proposition warns against reading posterior mass as an honest architecture certificate. Chapter 19 defined the standard confidence certificate for an arbitrary truth map. Here we record the compact notation needed by the resolution theory. For a confidence world CnC_{n}, write

c⁡(Cn)={c⁡(w):w∈Cn}⊆{F,I},c(C_{n})=\{c(w):w\in C_{n}\}\subseteq\{F,I\},

and set

δCnc={M,Cn=∅,d,c⁡(Cn)={d}​ for ​d∈{F,I},U,|c⁡(Cn)|>1.\delta_{C_{n}}^{c}=\begin{cases}M,&C_{n}=\varnothing,\\ d,&c(C_{n})=\{d\}\text{ for }d\in\{F,I\},\\ U,&|c(C_{n})|>1.\end{cases}
Corollary 20.2 (Truth-map form of three-way honesty).

If CnC_{n} covers the true world with probability at least 1−α1-\alpha, every resolved output of δCnc\delta_{C_{n}}^{c} is honest at level 1−α1-\alpha. On a realized nonempty confidence world, no other rule based on the same world can make more declarations while preserving worldwise correctness.

20.2 Resolution complexity

Confidence sequences make the same statement valid under adaptive querying and stopping. Data-dependent hypothesis sets and random-set generalization bounds address a related selection problem (Dupuis et al., 2024); the object here is different because the set represents covered population worlds rather than a learned hypothesis class. A current unresolved state contains compatible worlds of opposite certificate colors. The relevant information is therefore not global parameter information but separation from the nearest world that would reverse the declared conclusion.

Let Θ\Theta be a finite world set, let q:Θ→𝖰q:\Theta\to\mathsf{Q} be the truth partition, and let ℰ\mathcal{E} be a finite experiment set. Experiment ee has law Pθ,eP_{\theta,e} in world θ\theta. Define

de​(θ,λ)\displaystyle d_{e}(\theta,\lambda) =KL(Pθ,e∥Pλ,e),\displaystyle=\operatorname{KL}(P_{\theta,e}\|P_{\lambda,e}), Altq⁡(θ)\displaystyle\operatorname{Alt}_{q}(\theta) ={λ:q⁡(λ)≠q⁡(θ)},\displaystyle=\{\lambda:q(\lambda)\neq q(\theta)\}, (20.1)
ℐXq,∗​(θ)\displaystyle\mathcal{I}_{X}^{q,*}(\theta) =maxw∈Δ⁡(ℰ)⁡min⁡∑e∈ℰλ∈Altq⁡(θ)⁡we​de​(θ,λ),\displaystyle=\max_{w\in\Delta(\mathcal{E})}\min_{\lambda\in\operatorname{Alt}_{q}(\theta)}\sum_{e\in\mathcal{E}}w_{e}d_{e}(\theta,\lambda), TXq,∗​(θ)\displaystyle T_{X}^{q,*}(\theta) ={ℐXq,∗​(θ)}−1.\displaystyle=\{\mathcal{I}_{X}^{q,*}(\theta)\}^{-1}. (20.2)

We use the convention 1/0=+∞1/0=+\infty. The allocation ww is an experimental frequency, whereas the inner minimum is chosen by the least separated opposite-label world.

A sequential rule (τ,q^)(\tau,\widehat{q}) is α\alpha-worldwise valid when

supθ∈Θℙθ​{q^≠q⁡(θ),τ<∞}≤α.\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\mathbb{P}_{\theta}\{\widehat{q}\neq q(\theta),\ \tau<\infty\}\leq\alpha. (20.3)
Theorem 20.3 (Worldwise resolution lower bound).

For 0<α<1/20<\alpha<1/2, every α\alpha-worldwise-valid rule with 𝔼θ​τ<∞\mathbb{E}_{\theta}\tau<\infty satisfies

𝔼θ​τ≥TXq,∗​(θ)​kl⁡(1−α,α).\boxed{\mathbb{E}_{\theta}\tau\geq T_{X}^{q,*}(\theta)\operatorname{kl}(1-\alpha,\alpha).} (20.4)

Consequently,

lim infα↓0𝔼θ​τlog⁡(1/α)≥TXq,∗​(θ).\liminf_{\alpha\downarrow 0}\frac{\mathbb{E}_{\theta}\tau}{\log(1/\alpha)}\geq T_{X}^{q,*}(\theta).

The max–min geometry is the established partition-identification lower-bound mechanism (Kaufmann et al., 2016; Garivier and Kaufmann, 2016; Degenne and Koolen, 2019). Certificate statistics contributes the typed truth partition and connects this rate to evidence and recursive carriers; it does not rename generic pure exploration as a new theorem.

20.2.1 AND/OR phase change

In a Gaussian multichannel threshold problem, feasibility may require verifying that every channel satisfies a constraint, while impossibility can be proved by one violated channel. The optimal information geometry changes accordingly.

  • •

    To certify feasibility, allocation must cover all near-boundary channels: an AND geometry.

  • •

    To certify impossibility, allocation may concentrate on one strongest obstruction: an OR geometry.

For example, sampling channel ii from N⁡(μi,σ2)N(\mu_{i},\sigma^{2}) and declaring feasibility when maxi⁡μi≤ε\max_{i}\mu_{i}\leq\varepsilon gives, away from the boundary,

TXq,∗(μ)={2​σ2​∑i(ε−μi)−2,maxi⁡μi<ε,2​σ2maxi:μi>ε(μi−ε)2,maxi⁡μi>ε.T_{X}^{q,*}(\mu)=\begin{cases}2\sigma^{2}\displaystyle\sum_{i}(\varepsilon-\mu_{i})^{-2},&\max_{i}\mu_{i}<\varepsilon,\\[8.00003pt] \displaystyle\frac{2\sigma^{2}}{\max_{i:\mu_{i}>\varepsilon}(\mu_{i}-\varepsilon)^{2}},&\max_{i}\mu_{i}>\varepsilon.\end{cases} (20.5)

On the feasible side the optimal allocation equalizes the coordinate-wise KL rates. On the impossible side it concentrates on a strongest violation. Thus the asymmetry is intrinsic to the certificate, not to a particular algorithm. We retain this closed form as a worked interpretation; the general exponential-family and partition-identification setting belongs to the pure-exploration literature (Kaufmann et al., 2018; Juneja and Krishnasamy, 2019).

20.3 Evidence carriers and task-relative sufficiency

For each experiment ee, let XeX_{e} denote the raw observation and let a parameter-independent Markov kernel produce retained evidence Ze=Te​(Xe)Z_{e}=T_{e}(X_{e}). Write Qθ,eQ_{\theta,e} for the retained law and define

deX​(θ,λ)\displaystyle d_{e}^{X}(\theta,\lambda) =KL(Pθ,e∥Pλ,e),\displaystyle=\operatorname{KL}(P_{\theta,e}\|P_{\lambda,e}), deZ​(θ,λ)\displaystyle d_{e}^{Z}(\theta,\lambda) =KL(Qθ,e∥Qλ,e),\displaystyle=\operatorname{KL}(Q_{\theta,e}\|Q_{\lambda,e}), (20.6)
ℓe​(θ,λ)\displaystyle\ell_{e}(\theta,\lambda) =𝔼Qθ,eKL{Pθ,e(⋅∣Ze)∥Pλ,e(⋅∣Ze)}.\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}_{Q_{\theta,e}}\operatorname{KL}\{P_{\theta,e}(\cdot\mid Z_{e})\|P_{\lambda,e}(\cdot\mid Z_{e})\}. (20.7)

The conditional KL chain rule gives the exact pairwise KL decomposition

deX​(θ,λ)=deZ​(θ,λ)+ℓe​(θ,λ).d_{e}^{X}(\theta,\lambda)=d_{e}^{Z}(\theta,\lambda)+\ell_{e}(\theta,\lambda). (20.8)

Consequently, if ℐZq,∗\mathcal{I}_{Z}^{q,*} is defined from retained KL rates,

ℐZq,∗​(θ)≤ℐXq,∗​(θ),TZq,∗​(θ)≥TXq,∗​(θ).\mathcal{I}_{Z}^{q,*}(\theta)\leq\mathcal{I}_{X}^{q,*}(\theta),\qquad T_{Z}^{q,*}(\theta)\geq T_{X}^{q,*}(\theta). (20.9)

Pairwise KL loss is not yet the right sufficiency test. Certificate sufficiency need not preserve every likelihood ratio; it need only avoid lowering the max–min floor. At a fixed world θ\theta and allocation ww, put

GX​(w,λ)\displaystyle G_{X}(w,\lambda) =∑ewe​deX​(θ,λ),\displaystyle=\sum_{e}w_{e}d_{e}^{X}(\theta,\lambda), L⁡(w,λ)\displaystyle L(w,\lambda) =∑ewe​ℓe​(θ,λ),\displaystyle=\sum_{e}w_{e}\ell_{e}(\theta,\lambda), (20.10)
sX​(w,λ)\displaystyle s_{X}(w,\lambda) =GX​(w,λ)−ℐXq,∗​(θ).\displaystyle=G_{X}(w,\lambda)-\mathcal{I}_{X}^{q,*}(\theta). (20.11)

At a raw-optimal allocation, sXs_{X} measures how far an alternative lies above the binding certificate floor.

Theorem 20.4 (Exact certificate preservation by slack).

The retained carrier preserves the raw characteristic information at θ\theta,

ℐZq,∗​(θ)=ℐXq,∗​(θ),\mathcal{I}_{Z}^{q,*}(\theta)=\mathcal{I}_{X}^{q,*}(\theta),

if and only if there is an allocation w⋆∈Δ⁡(ℰ)w^{\star}\in\Delta(\mathcal{E}) such that

L⁡(w⋆,λ)≤sX​(w⋆,λ)for every ​λ∈Altq⁡(θ).\boxed{L(w^{\star},\lambda)\leq s_{X}(w^{\star},\lambda)\quad\text{for every }\lambda\in\operatorname{Alt}_{q}(\theta).} (20.12)

Every such w⋆w^{\star} is raw-optimal. In particular, every raw binding alternative at w⋆w^{\star} has zero weighted KL loss.

Locally, the score map projected to the nuisance-quotiented tangent space gives a task-relative information operator. Its minimum modulus determines stability; inverse-square modulus controls sample inflation. This modulus language follows the established analysis of ill-posed and semiparametric inverse problems (Blundell et al., 2007; Chen and Reiss, 2011); certificate statistics uses it only after restricting the tangent directions to those that can reverse the declared truth label.

20.3.1 Average Bayesian loss versus worldwise complexity

Let Q=q⁡(Θ)Q=q(\Theta) be the task label, let XX be the raw record, and let ZZ be retained evidence generated from XX. Write ΠXQ=ℒ⁡(Q∣X)\Pi_{X}^{Q}=\mathcal{L}(Q\mid X) and ΠZQ=ℒ⁡(Q∣Z)\Pi_{Z}^{Q}=\mathcal{L}(Q\mid Z). Under the Markov relation Q→X→ZQ\to X\to Z, the standard conditional-information identity gives the exact prior-predictive identity

𝔼KL(ΠXQ∥ΠZQ)=I(Q;X∣Z).\mathbb{E}\operatorname{KL}(\Pi_{X}^{Q}\|\Pi_{Z}^{Q})=I(Q;X\mid Z). (20.13)

The left side measures how much the retained representation distorts the full-data task posterior on average under the chosen prior. It is therefore a legitimate loss scale for Bayesian representation fidelity and expected experimental utility (Cover and Thomas, 2006; Lindley, 1956).

It is not a worldwise certificate loss scale. For a sharp separation, take two worlds with X|θ0∼Bernoulli⁡(1/4)X\mid\theta_{0}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/4) and X|θ1∼Bernoulli⁡(3/4)X\mid\theta_{1}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(3/4), let ZZ be constant, and assign prior mass rr to θ1\theta_{1}. The posterior loss in (20.13) is at most the binary entropy h2​(r)h_{2}(r) and therefore tends to zero as r↓0r\downarrow 0. Yet the retained laws are identical, so ℐZq,∗=0\mathcal{I}_{Z}^{q,*}=0 and the worldwise characteristic time is infinite, while the raw pair remains distinguishable.

Posterior belief can guide design, worldwise evidence authorizes a certificate, and recursive state preserves what future design will need.

20.4 Recursive certificate posterior quotient

The current posterior probability of certificate colors may be insufficient to choose the next experiment. Two beliefs with the same current color probabilities can imply different optimal future measurements.

Assume now that hypotheses, experiments, observation alphabets, and the reachable belief set ℛ⊆Δ⁡(Θ)\mathcal{R}\subseteq\Delta(\Theta) are finite. The set ℛ\mathcal{R} is closed under every positive-probability Bayes update. Let χ:ℛ→𝖢\chi:\mathcal{R}\to\mathsf{C} be the declared contract color. It may record a present certificate permission, observer gate, or vector of immediate costs; fields omitted from χ\chi are not protected by the quotient.

For experiment ee and observation yy, define

pe​(y∣b)\displaystyle p_{e}(y\mid b) =∑θb⁡(θ)​Pθ,e​(y),\displaystyle=\sum_{\theta}b(\theta)P_{\theta,e}(y), (20.14)
Be,y​b​(θ)\displaystyle B_{e,y}b(\theta) =b⁡(θ)​Pθ,e​(y)pe​(y∣b),\displaystyle=\frac{b(\theta)P_{\theta,e}(y)}{p_{e}(y\mid b)}, (20.15)
Ke​(b,{y}×A)\displaystyle K_{e}\bigl(b;\{y\}\times A\bigr) =pe(y∣b)𝟏{Be,yb∈A}.\displaystyle=p_{e}(y\mid b)\mathbf{1}\{B_{e,y}b\in A\}. (20.16)

The label yy is retained: two states are not equivalent merely because they have the same unlabeled aggregate transition.

Start with b∼0b′b\sim_{0}b^{\prime} when χ⁡(b)=χ⁡(b′)\chi(b)=\chi(b^{\prime}). Given ∼h\sim_{h}, define b∼h+1b′b\sim_{h+1}b^{\prime} when b∼hb′b\sim_{h}b^{\prime} and

Ke​(b,{y}×A)=Ke​(b′,{y}×A)K_{e}(b;\{y\}\times A)=K_{e}(b^{\prime};\{y\}\times A) (20.17)

for every experiment ee, observation yy, and ∼h\sim_{h}-class AA. Put

∼∞=⋂h≥0∼h,Nh=|ℛ/∼h|.\sim_{\infty}=\bigcap_{h\geq 0}\sim_{h},\qquad N_{h}=|\mathcal{R}/\!\sim_{h}|.

A recursive carrier ϕ:ℛ→𝖲\phi:\mathcal{R}\to\mathsf{S} is exact if the color factors through ϕ\phi and, for every experiment, the joint law of the observation label and successor carrier state depends on bb only through ϕ⁡(b)\phi(b).

Theorem 20.5 (Recursive quotient and minimal exact state).

The relations ∼h\sim_{h} are decreasing equivalence relations and

N0≤N1≤⋯≤N∞.N_{0}\leq N_{1}\leq\cdots\leq N_{\infty}.

If b∼hb′b\sim_{h}b^{\prime}, every fixed observation-history policy using at most hh further observations induces the same law of observation labels and contract colors from bb and b′b^{\prime}. The limit ∼∞\sim_{\infty} is the largest color-respecting equivalence relation stable under every labeled kernel KeK_{e}.

The quotient map b↦[b]∞b\mapsto[b]_{\infty} is exact, and every exact recursive carrier refines it:

ϕ(b)=ϕ(b′)⟹b∼∞b′.\phi(b)=\phi(b^{\prime})\quad\Longrightarrow\quad b\sim_{\infty}b^{\prime}. (20.18)

Thus every exact deterministic implementation has at least N∞N_{\infty} reachable states. If each of LL charts distinguishes at most KK states, then

L≥⌈N∞K⌉.L\geq\left\lceil\frac{N_{\infty}}{K}\right\rceil. (20.19)

Signature refinement terminates after at most N∞−N0N_{\infty}-N_{0} strict block increases, and every strict split returns an experiment, observation, and successor block witnessing the missing distinction.

The count N∞N_{\infty} concerns only the recursive belief carrier specified in the theorem. A concrete GLR test, deficit tracker, or D-tracking implementation may keep likelihood sums, visit counts, or time indices in separate and potentially unbounded auxiliary memory. Those counters are not included in N∞N_{\infty} unless the declared carrier grammar explicitly folds them into the protected recursive state.

This construction specializes strong belief bisimulation (Castro et al., 2009; Larsen and Skou, 1991) and realizes the finite quotient by color-respecting partition refinement, connecting model minimization and classical refinement algorithms (Givan et al., 2003; Paige and Tarjan, 1987). Its role here is architectural: the quotient cardinality is a task-relative recurrent capacity, and a split witness tells a repair procedure which state distinction must be installed.

20.4.1 CertTrack and certificate-aware design

A certificate-aware tracker assigns two different jobs to two different loss scales. At current belief bb, the Bayesian task gain from experiment ee is

Geq​(b)=Ib​{q⁡(Θ);Ye}.G_{e}^{q}(b)=I_{b}\{q(\Theta);Y_{e}\}.

This prior-average quantity may decide which informative experiment to run. It cannot by itself decide when every opposite-color world has been excluded. For retained evidence, define the ρ\rho-optimal worldwise face

𝒲ρZ​(θ)={w∈Δ⁡(ℰ):min⁡∑eλ∈Altq⁡(θ)⁡we​deZ​(θ,λ)≥(1−ρ)​ℐZq,∗​(θ)}.\mathcal{W}_{\rho}^{Z}(\theta)=\left\{w\in\Delta(\mathcal{E}):\min_{\lambda\in\operatorname{Alt}_{q}(\theta)}\sum_{e}w_{e}d_{e}^{Z}(\theta,\lambda)\geq(1-\rho)\mathcal{I}_{Z}^{q,*}(\theta)\right\}. (20.20)

A posterior-guided design may maximize ∑ewe​Geq​(b)\sum_{e}w_{e}G_{e}^{q}(b) inside this face. At ρ=0\rho=0 it only breaks ties among certificate-optimal allocations; with ρt↓0\rho_{t}\downarrow 0 it may trade a vanishing fraction of the leading worldwise rate for prior-relevant information.

Stopping remains separate. It occurs only when a simultaneous confidence world has one truth color, or when an anytime-valid likelihood-ratio process crosses its declared boundary. Such validity holds under any nonanticipating design; it does not rely on posterior odds. Forced exploration and deficit tracking can then make empirical allocations follow the selected face (Garivier and Kaufmann, 2016; Kaufmann et al., 2018).

Under finite-model regularity, the resulting tracker attains the optimal almost-sure leading constant. Expected-time equality additionally requires uniform integrability; no posterior-odds optional-stopping argument is being used.

20.4.2 A compressed UCBAdmissions audit

The R UCBAdmissions table records 4526 applicants to six large UC Berkeley departments in 1973, classified by department, sex, and admission outcome (R Core Team, 2026). It is a standard example in which aggregation changes the apparent association (Bickel et al., 1975). Pooling departments gives 1198 admissions among 2691 male applicants and 557 among 1835 female applicants: a male-minus-female admission-rate difference of 0.14160.1416. A two-sided Fisher exact test of that pooled association gives p=4.84×10−22p=4.84\times 10^{-22}.

That calculation does not answer every department-level question. As a worked certificate, declare

dj=pj,M−pj,F,Γ=maxj∈{A,…,F}⁡dj,Γ≤0.10.d_{j}=p_{j,M}-p_{j,F},\qquad\Gamma=\max_{j\in\{A,\ldots,F\}}d_{j},\qquad\Gamma\leq 0.10. (20.21)

The ten-percentage-point tolerance is illustrative, not an ethical or causal criterion. Construct two-sided exact Clopper–Pearson intervals for the 12 department–sex cell probabilities at marginal error 0.05/120.05/12, and project their Bonferroni rectangle onto each difference djd_{j}. This gives a 95% simultaneous confidence world.

Every department point estimate is below ten points, but the simultaneous intervals for B–E cross that boundary, and no lower endpoint exceeds it. The honest certificate for (20.21) is therefore UU. Department B is the resolution bottleneck: its upper excursion is largest, driven by only 25 female applicants.

The same confidence world gives the entire tolerance profile. Because it is rectangular, the identified image of Γ\Gamma has endpoints

LΓ=maxj⁡Lj=−0.0895,UΓ=maxj⁡Uj=0.3109,L_{\Gamma}=\max_{j}L_{j}=-0.0895,\qquad U_{\Gamma}=\max_{j}U_{j}=0.3109,

to the displayed precision. Hence, for the query Γ≤ε\Gamma\leq\varepsilon,

δ⁡(ε)={I,ε<−0.0895,U,−0.0895≤ε<0.3109,F,ε≥0.3109,\delta(\varepsilon)=\begin{cases}I,&\varepsilon<-0.0895,\\ U,&-0.0895\leq\varepsilon<0.3109,\\ F,&\varepsilon\geq 0.3109,\end{cases} (20.22)

up to endpoint rounding. Thus a pooled pp-value near 10−2210^{-22} coexists with unresolved department tolerances across a forty-point range.

readout authorized action
pooled association report the pooled disparity for that declared query; do not transport it into a department-level verdict
department certificate return UU, withhold a binary department verdict, and direct further resolution effort toward the widest binding interval

All displayed quantities are deterministic functions of the public contingency table. No regression model, asymptotic normal approximation, or prior enters this audit. A more structured model may narrow the confidence world, but it would constitute an additional declared assumption rather than a reinterpretation of the same certificate.

Exercises

Exercise 20.6.

Construct a confidence world containing both feasible and impossible parameter values. Show that every honest binary rule must abstain or make an error on some compatible world.

Exercise 20.7.

Compute the max–min information allocation for a two-channel Gaussian OR certificate.

Exercise 20.8.

Construct a raw-optimal allocation with one binding and one nonbinding alternative. Determine how much KL the evidence carrier may discard in each direction without increasing characteristic time.

Exercise 20.9.

Give two posterior distributions with the same current probability of feasibility but different optimal next experiments. Identify the first refinement signature that separates them.

Appendix to Chapter 20: complete proofs

Proof that posterior credibility is not worldwise validity

Dependencies. The positive statement is an application of iterated expectation. The negative statement requires no identifiability: two worlds may have identical observation laws but different truth labels.

Proof.

If

ℙb0​{q⁡(Θ)≠q^∣Hτ}≤ηalmost surely,\mathbb{P}_{b_{0}}\{q(\Theta)\neq\widehat{q}\mid H_{\tau}\}\leq\eta\quad\text{almost surely},

then taking expectation with respect to the prior-predictive law yields

ℙb0{q(Θ)≠q^}=𝔼b0ℙb0{q(Θ)≠q^∣Hτ}≤η.\mathbb{P}_{b_{0}}\{q(\Theta)\neq\widehat{q}\}=\mathbb{E}_{b_{0}}\mathbb{P}_{b_{0}}\{q(\Theta)\neq\widehat{q}\mid H_{\tau}\}\leq\eta.

This is a prior-average statement.

For the separation, take two worlds θF\theta_{F} and θI\theta_{I} with different truth labels and identical laws for every observation under every available experiment. Assign prior masses 1−η1-\eta and η\eta, respectively. Since the likelihood ratio is identically one, the posterior never changes. Reporting the majority label has posterior error η\eta at every time and therefore satisfies the credibility criterion. Conditional on the minority world, however, the report is wrong with probability one. Thus no nontrivial uniform worldwise error guarantee follows from posterior credibility alone. Moreover, every experiment has zero KL divergence between the two opposite-label worlds, so the characteristic information for their truth partition is zero and the corresponding worldwise resolution complexity is infinite. ∎

Proof of the truth-map form of three-way honesty

Dependencies. Theorem 19.3 proves the claim for an arbitrary truth map on a nonempty confidence world. The simultaneous-query clause requires one coverage event for the whole query class; the empty-set output MM is diagnostic and is not a resolved truth claim.

Proof.

Apply Theorem 19.3 to the two cells c−1​(F)c^{-1}(F) and c−1​(I)c^{-1}(I). A singleton image c⁡(Cn)c(C_{n}) is the agreeing case of that theorem, and a two-label image is its unresolved case; honesty and maximal decisiveness follow immediately. If one confidence world covers the complete population object simultaneously over a query class, the same reduction holds for every query on that event and hence for any data-selected query. ∎

Proof of the worldwise resolution lower bound

Dependencies. We use the standard sequential change-of-measure inequality: for a stopped transcript, any event AA measurable at the stopping time, and any pair of worlds θ,λ\theta,\lambda,

∑e𝔼θNe(τ)KL(Pθ,e∥Pλ,e)≥kl{ℙθ(A),ℙλ(A)}.\sum_{e}\mathbb{E}_{\theta}N_{e}(\tau)\operatorname{KL}(P_{\theta,e}\|P_{\lambda,e})\geq\operatorname{kl}\{\mathbb{P}_{\theta}(A),\mathbb{P}_{\lambda}(A)\}.

This follows by applying data processing to the likelihood ratio of the stopped experiment.

Proof.

Fix λ∈Altq⁡(θ)\lambda\in\operatorname{Alt}_{q}(\theta) and take

Aθ={τ<∞,q^=q⁡(θ)}.A_{\theta}=\{\tau<\infty,\ \widehat{q}=q(\theta)\}.

Because 𝔼θ​τ<∞\mathbb{E}_{\theta}\tau<\infty, the rule stops almost surely under θ\theta. Worldwise validity therefore gives

ℙθ​(Aθ)≥1−α.\mathbb{P}_{\theta}(A_{\theta})\geq 1-\alpha.

Since q⁡(λ)≠q⁡(θ)q(\lambda)\neq q(\theta), the same event is an error under λ\lambda, so

ℙλ​(Aθ)≤α.\mathbb{P}_{\lambda}(A_{\theta})\leq\alpha.

For 0<α<1/20<\alpha<1/2, monotonicity of binary relative entropy on these two ranges and sequential change of measure yield

∑e𝔼θ​Ne​(τ)​de​(θ,λ)≥kl⁡(1−α,α).\sum_{e}\mathbb{E}_{\theta}N_{e}(\tau)d_{e}(\theta,\lambda)\geq\operatorname{kl}(1-\alpha,\alpha). (20.23)

Define the normalized expected counts

w¯e=𝔼θ​Ne​(τ)𝔼θ​τ.\bar{w}_{e}=\frac{\mathbb{E}_{\theta}N_{e}(\tau)}{\mathbb{E}_{\theta}\tau}.

They are nonnegative and sum to one. Divide (20.23) by 𝔼θ​τ\mathbb{E}_{\theta}\tau and minimize over λ∈Altq⁡(θ)\lambda\in\operatorname{Alt}_{q}(\theta):

min⁡∑eλ∈Altq⁡(θ)⁡w¯e​de​(θ,λ)≥kl⁡(1−α,α)𝔼θ​τ.\min_{\lambda\in\operatorname{Alt}_{q}(\theta)}\sum_{e}\bar{w}_{e}d_{e}(\theta,\lambda)\geq\frac{\operatorname{kl}(1-\alpha,\alpha)}{\mathbb{E}_{\theta}\tau}.

The left side is no larger than its maximum over all allocations, namely ℐXq,∗​(θ)\mathcal{I}_{X}^{q,*}(\theta). Rearrangement gives

𝔼θ​τ≥kl⁡(1−α,α)ℐXq,∗​(θ)=TXq,∗​(θ)​kl⁡(1−α,α).\mathbb{E}_{\theta}\tau\geq\frac{\operatorname{kl}(1-\alpha,\alpha)}{\mathcal{I}_{X}^{q,*}(\theta)}=T_{X}^{q,*}(\theta)\operatorname{kl}(1-\alpha,\alpha).

If the characteristic information is zero, the preceding inequality forces 𝔼θ​τ=+∞\mathbb{E}_{\theta}\tau=+\infty, contradicting the assumed finite expectation; hence no such finite-time rule exists. Finally, kl⁡(1−α,α)/log⁡(1/α)→1\operatorname{kl}(1-\alpha,\alpha)/\log(1/\alpha)\to 1, which proves the asymptotic statement. ∎

Proof of exact certificate preservation by slack

Dependencies. The evidence kernel is parameter-independent, so the KL chain rule for (Xe,Ze)(X_{e},Z_{e}) has raw KL on the left. The converse uses attainment of the retained max–min problem.

Proof.

For every allocation ww and alternative λ\lambda, summing (20.8) gives

GZ​(w,λ)=GX​(w,λ)−L⁡(w,λ).G_{Z}(w,\lambda)=G_{X}(w,\lambda)-L(w,\lambda). (20.24)

Because L≥0L\geq 0, every retained alternative rate is no larger than its raw counterpart. Taking the alternative minimum and allocation maximum proves ℐZq,∗​(θ)≤ℐXq,∗​(θ)\mathcal{I}_{Z}^{q,*}(\theta)\leq\mathcal{I}_{X}^{q,*}(\theta).

Suppose first that w⋆w^{\star} satisfies (20.12). For every opposite-label λ\lambda,

GZ​(w⋆,λ)\displaystyle G_{Z}(w^{\star},\lambda) =GX​(w⋆,λ)−L⁡(w⋆,λ)\displaystyle=G_{X}(w^{\star},\lambda)-L(w^{\star},\lambda)
≥GX​(w⋆,λ)−sX​(w⋆,λ)\displaystyle\geq G_{X}(w^{\star},\lambda)-s_{X}(w^{\star},\lambda)
=ℐXq,∗​(θ).\displaystyle=\mathcal{I}_{X}^{q,*}(\theta).

Thus ℐZq,∗​(θ)≥ℐXq,∗​(θ)\mathcal{I}_{Z}^{q,*}(\theta)\geq\mathcal{I}_{X}^{q,*}(\theta). Data processing supplies the reverse inequality, so equality holds. Moreover,

minλ⁡GX​(w⋆,λ)≥minλ⁡GZ​(w⋆,λ)≥ℐXq,∗​(θ).\min_{\lambda}G_{X}(w^{\star},\lambda)\geq\min_{\lambda}G_{Z}(w^{\star},\lambda)\geq\mathcal{I}_{X}^{q,*}(\theta).

By definition of the raw maximum, equality must hold and w⋆w^{\star} is raw-optimal.

Conversely, assume ℐZq,∗​(θ)=ℐXq,∗​(θ)\mathcal{I}_{Z}^{q,*}(\theta)=\mathcal{I}_{X}^{q,*}(\theta) and choose a retained-optimal allocation w⋆w^{\star}. Then every opposite-label alternative obeys

GZ​(w⋆,λ)≥ℐZq,∗​(θ)=ℐXq,∗​(θ).G_{Z}(w^{\star},\lambda)\geq\mathcal{I}_{Z}^{q,*}(\theta)=\mathcal{I}_{X}^{q,*}(\theta).

Rearranging (20.24) gives

L⁡(w⋆,λ)≤GX​(w⋆,λ)−ℐXq,∗​(θ)=sX​(w⋆,λ),L(w^{\star},\lambda)\leq G_{X}(w^{\star},\lambda)-\mathcal{I}_{X}^{q,*}(\theta)=s_{X}(w^{\star},\lambda),

which is the required slack domination. The preceding raw-optimality argument applies again. Finally, if λ\lambda is binding in the raw problem at w⋆w^{\star}, then sX​(w⋆,λ)=0s_{X}(w^{\star},\lambda)=0. Since L≥0L\geq 0, slack domination forces L⁡(w⋆,λ)=0L(w^{\star},\lambda)=0. ∎

Proof of the recursive quotient and minimal exact state

Dependencies. All sets are finite. This avoids measurable-quotient issues and makes the decreasing partition sequence stabilize after finitely many strict refinements. Policies are fixed observation-history rules, not rules separately tailored to the two initial beliefs.

Proof.

Equality of χ\chi is an equivalence relation, so ∼0\sim_{0} is an equivalence relation. Suppose ∼h\sim_{h} is one. Within each ∼h\sim_{h}-class, associate to bb the finite signature

sigh(b)=[Ke(b;{y}×A)]e,y,A∈ℛ/∼h.\operatorname{sig}_{h}(b)=\bigl[K_{e}(b;\{y\}\times A)\bigr]_{e,y,A\in\mathcal{R}/\!\sim_{h}}.

The relation ∼h+1\sim_{h+1} is equality of these signatures inside a ∼h\sim_{h}-class. It is therefore an equivalence relation and refines ∼h\sim_{h}. The quotient cardinalities are consequently nondecreasing.

We prove finite-horizon invariance by induction. At horizon zero, related beliefs have the same color. Suppose the claim holds at horizon hh and let b∼h+1b′b\sim_{h+1}b^{\prime}. A fixed observation-history policy selects the same first experiment at the two empty histories. Equation (20.17) gives the same probability to every observation label and successor ∼h\sim_{h}-class. Conditional on such a label and class, the induction hypothesis gives the same law for the remaining hh observations and colors. Summing over the first step proves the claim at horizon h+1h+1.

Call an equivalence relation RR stable when it respects χ\chi and gives equal mass, for every ee and yy, to every RR-class. We show that every such RR is contained in every ∼h\sim_{h}. Color respect gives R⊆∼0R\subseteq\sim_{0}. If R⊆∼hR\subseteq\sim_{h}, each ∼h\sim_{h}-class is a union of RR-classes. Stability on the finer RR-classes can therefore be summed to give equality on every ∼h\sim_{h}-class, so R⊆∼h+1R\subseteq\sim_{h+1}. Induction yields R⊆∼∞R\subseteq\sim_{\infty}.

Because ℛ\mathcal{R} is finite, the decreasing equivalence relations stabilize: for some HH, ∼H=∼H+1=∼∞\sim_{H}=\sim_{H+1}=\sim_{\infty}. The defining equality at the fixed point makes ∼∞\sim_{\infty} itself stable. Hence it is the largest stable color-respecting equivalence relation. Stability also makes the color decoder and every reduced labeled kernel on ℛ/∼∞\mathcal{R}/\!\sim_{\infty} well defined, proving exactness of the quotient map.

Let ϕ\phi be any exact recursive carrier and define b​Rϕ​b′bR_{\phi}b^{\prime} when ϕ⁡(b)=ϕ⁡(b′)\phi(b)=\phi(b^{\prime}). Color factorization makes RϕR_{\phi} color-respecting. Factorization of the joint observation–successor law makes it stable. Maximality therefore implies Rϕ⊆∼∞R_{\phi}\subseteq\sim_{\infty}, which is exactly (20.18). Thus distinct ∼∞\sim_{\infty}-classes require distinct carrier states, giving at least N∞N_{\infty} states. If LL charts expose at most KK states each, they expose at most L​KLK distinct chart–state pairs, and L​K≥N∞LK\geq N_{\infty} proves (20.19).

Starting from N0N_{0} blocks, every strict signature-refinement round increases the block count by at least one and no round can exceed N∞N_{\infty}. Hence there are at most N∞−N0N_{\infty}-N_{0} strict increases. When a block splits, two of its beliefs have unequal signatures; one coordinate of that inequality supplies the promised experiment ee, observation yy, and successor block AA. ∎

Part VI Historical and Conceptual Notes

Confidence world: the name is local, the confidence-set principle is not

A confidence world CnC_{n} is a random confidence set for a complete population world. Its mathematical coverage contract is not a new species of confidence set. In particular, Dufour (1997) observed that a covered joint set can be mapped through any function gg: the image g⁡(Cn)g(C_{n}) remains a valid confidence set because membership of the true joint parameter implies membership of its image. The book’s identified image JCn​(q)J_{C_{n}}(q) is this projection principle applied to a declared structural query.

The closest neighboring objects nevertheless live on different axes.

Lineage Primary object Main question Relation to CnC_{n}
Manski partial identification (Manski, 2003) population identified set ΘI​(P)\Theta_{I}(P) what is determined even with the population law known? a population identification object, not the finite-sample random set itself
Dufour projection (Dufour, 1997) covered joint confidence set and its image g⁡(Cn)g(C_{n}) how is coverage preserved for a transformation or subvector? direct antecedent of the identified-image validity argument
Set inference (Chernozhukov et al., 2007; Andrews and Soares, 2010) estimators and confidence regions in partially identified or moment-inequality models when do set estimators and confidence procedures have consistency, coverage, and useful power? supplies model-specific construction and asymptotic theory that the abstract coverage definition alone does not provide
Vogel random optimization (Vogel, 2008) simultaneous random objective and constraint information how can feasible sets, optimal values, and solution sets be covered together? direct neighbor of the honest inner/outer architecture bracket
Confidence world (this book) complete population object, including nuisance and the sampling/future-experiment structure needed by the declared query which structural conclusions and actions are authorized on one coverage event? an enriched bookkeeping and interface convention built on the preceding confidence-set principles

Coverage alone gives no contraction theorem: the vacuous choice Cn≡𝒲C_{n}\equiv\mathcal{W} satisfies a coverage lower bound. Convergence to an identified set, Hausdorff consistency, nonconservativeness, or power requires additional assumptions and a concrete construction, as in the set- and moment-inequality literatures just cited. Part VI therefore claims transport of a declared coverage event, not automatic consistency of every confidence world.

The three-way rule and the model-conflict state

For a nonempty CnC_{n}, the rule is set unanimity:

q⁡(Cn)={F}⇒F,q⁡(Cn)={I}⇒I,|q⁡(Cn)|>1⇒U.q(C_{n})=\{F\}\Rightarrow F,\hskip 18.49988ptq(C_{n})=\{I\}\Rightarrow I,\hskip 18.49988pt|q(C_{n})|>1\Rightarrow U.

This follows in one line from confidence-set projection and is historically adjacent to equivalence and noninferiority testing, where a confidence set must lie wholly inside or outside a declared margin (Blackwelder, 1982; Berger and Hsu, 1996; Piaggio et al., 2006). The book does not claim that the F/I/UF/I/U threshold logic is new. Its increment is to type the query as a structural architecture claim, preserve the whole identified image and tolerance profile, connect UU to resolution complexity, and keep authorization separate from posterior belief and deployment.

The symbol MM is book terminology for an empty confidence world. Empty-set diagnostics are not without precedent: Dufour (1997) explicitly notes that an empty valid confidence set can be interpreted as rejection of the model or overidentifying restrictions. The book’s contribution is to prevent that diagnostic from being confused with either a feasible or impossible population truth label.

What the theorem-level audit leaves as genuine increments

The worldwise resolution lower bound and recursive quotient import partition-identification and probabilistic-bisimulation machinery. The posterior/worldwise counterexample is standard. The atlas inverse and common- deployment results are program-specific specializations. The exact evidence-slack criterion asks when compression preserves one max–min certificate floor rather than an entire parametric experiment. Its proof is a short KL data-processing and max–min argument, so the book treats it as a useful specialization rather than a new information-theoretic mechanism; see Appendix G.1.

Part VII Obstruction-Aware Learning and Structural Repair
A structural certificate becomes actionable only when it localizes the failed interface, authorizes a compatible intervention, and predicts an improvement that survives independent validation and matched controls.

Chapter 21 Toward a Certified Structural Learning Theory

A structural learning theorem should not hide distinct mechanisms inside one undifferentiated excess-risk bound. It should report lower or upper certificates for the risk components that the data and structural analysis can actually identify.

Let 𝔄^\widehat{\mathfrak{A}} be a possibly data-dependent architecture selected on calibration data, and let A^\widehat{A} be trained on an independent training split. On a held-out test split, the desired statement has the form

Δmodel¯+Δarch¯≤R⁡(A^)−R⋆≤Δmodel¯+Δarch¯+Δgen¯+Δopt¯.\underline{\Delta^{\mathrm{model}}}+\underline{\Delta^{\mathrm{arch}}}\leq R(\widehat{A})-R^{\star}\leq\overline{\Delta^{\mathrm{model}}}+\overline{\Delta^{\mathrm{arch}}}+\overline{\Delta^{\mathrm{gen}}}+\overline{\Delta^{\mathrm{opt}}}.

Every term should have a declared source.

21.1 Three nonexchangeable carrier contracts

Chapter 20 has already fixed the evidence-carrier contract in Section 20.3 and the recursive carrier contract in Section 20.4. We reuse those definitions unchanged. The additional interface here is the deployment carrier HdepH_{\rm dep}: in the carrier–decoder factorization of Chapter 16, it maps operating inputs to the state used by an action decoder. When HdepH_{\rm dep} is induced by a nonnative lift, it enters this chapter only after passing the quotient-faithful extraction gate of Section 10.4.

Placed side by side, the three exactness obligations have different domains and loss scales:

deployment: a⋆=ddep∘Hdep,\displaystyle a^{\star}=d_{\rm dep}\circ H_{\rm dep},
evidence: TZq,∗​(θ)=TXq,∗​(θ),\displaystyle T_{Z}^{q,*}(\theta)=T_{X}^{q,*}(\theta),
recursion: the declared color and every observation-labeled update factor through ​ϕrec.\displaystyle\text{the declared color and every observation-labeled update}\text{ factor through }\phi_{\rm rec}.

The first is charged in native loss, the second in expected observations, and the third in reachable states or charts. They form a typed audit vector, not three terms of one excess-risk sum. Figure 21.1 makes the three chains and their common terminal gate visible before the no-compensation theorem is stated.

The surrounding foundations are classical: statistical decision functions, sufficiency and comparison of experiments, treatment rules, and MDP state abstraction all precede this synthesis (Wald, 1950; Bahadur, 1954; Blackwell, 1951; Blackwell, 1953; Manski, 2004; Li et al., 2006). The claimed contribution is the typed interface and its explicit common-witness gate, not those component theories.

Theorem 21.1 (Typed no-compensation).

Each of the following failures survives unlimited resources in the other two carrier branches.

  1. 1.

    Evidence blindness. If opposite-label worlds θ\theta and λ\lambda satisfy Qθ,e=Qλ,eQ_{\theta,e}=Q_{\lambda,e} for every experiment ee, no retained-evidence rule can stop almost surely and have worldwise error at most α\alpha at both worlds, even with exact recursive and deployment carriers.

  2. 2.

    Recursive collision. If ϕrec​(b)=ϕrec​(b′)\phi_{\rm rec}(b)=\phi_{\rm rec}(b^{\prime}) for beliefs in different classes of the minimal recursive quotient from Theorem 20.5, a finite labeled future context distinguishes them. No decoder on that fixed recurrent state can realize the exact reduced process, even with raw evidence and an unrestricted deployment decoder.

  3. 3.

    Deployment collision. If Hdep​(x)=Hdep​(x′)H_{\rm dep}(x)=H_{\rm dep}(x^{\prime}) while ax⋆≠ax′⋆a_{x}^{\star}\neq a_{x^{\prime}}^{\star}, no decoder on that fixed carrier realizes both oracle actions. Under the compact-separation assumptions above, when both inputs have positive mass the best such decoder has strictly positive native defect even with raw evidence and identity recursive state.

Consequently, none of the three exactness predicates by itself implies either of the other two. This refutes bare implications and automatic compensation; it does not rule out cross-branch reasoning from a conjunction of hypotheses, a proved factorization theorem, or an optimization problem with an explicitly declared exchange rate.

The evidence-blind branch is the zero-information endpoint of the classical two-world change-of-measure method (Kaufmann et al., 2016); the theorem keeps that statistical obstruction typed separately from deployment and recursive-state failures.

A minimal memory-split stress test makes the boundary especially sharp. Let a fair history bit HH be erased by a constant baseline memory before a binary action is chosen. In one world the binary target is an independent fair coin; in another it is HH passed through a binary symmetric channel. Every baseline-executable policy then has the same retained action–reward law in both worlds, although retaining HH improves value only in the second world. If a temporary memory split is forbidden, the architecture query has zero characteristic information. If the split is allowed diagnostically, choosing the action A=HA=H reduces the query to testing Bern⁡(1/2)\operatorname{Bern}(1/2) against Bern⁡(1−η)\operatorname{Bern}(1-\eta). Charging for the diagnostic changes information per unit cost, not the statistical object. Thus operational exposure is an experiment-menu gate: under a resettable finite contract it is absorbed by active sequential experiment design (Chernoff, 1959; Naghshvar and Javidi, 2013), while the history quotient remains within state-abstraction theory (Li et al., 2006). The companion go/no-go audit records the exact finite calculation; it is not an additional principal result.

21.1.1 Routed experts and external memory under bounded observability

In a sparsely routed expert system, let Hdep​(x)H_{\rm dep}(x) be exactly the state visible to the router and let the action be an expert index, or a legal top-kk expert set. A per-input oracle can choose the best expert for every token or query, yet this pointwise family need not factor through one measurable gate on HdepH_{\rm dep}. If two positive-mass query classes collide in the router-visible state and reverse their preferred experts, the deployment-collision branch of Theorem 21.1 gives a positive native defect. More router optimization with the same carrier and action grammar cannot remove that collision. Sparse expert routing is the representative mechanism, not the name of the problem class (Shazeer et al., 2017; Fedus et al., 2022).

The possible repairs act on different contracts. Giving the router an additional feature or retrieved evidence changes its information carrier; top-kk routing, a shared residual expert, or an abstention/fallback path changes the action class; adding experts without making the distinguishing information visible may change neither. A larger context window changes a charged resource budget and must be analyzed as such. Retrieval-augmented generation is particularly revealing: retrieval changes the experiment and external-memory carrier available to the generator, rather than merely optimizing the same closed-book decoder (Lewis et al., 2020).

A credible architecture-choice claim therefore freezes the router-visible information, retrieval corpus and index, expert/action library, native task loss, and compute/latency budget before confirmation. It then tests the certificate-directed carrier or class repair against equal-information and equal-compute controls on an independent endpoint. Without those controls, an improved routed or retrieval system does not identify which typed repair caused the gain.

21.2 Typed architecture realization

The no-compensation theorem is the negative half of the interface. The positive half explains how the deterministic deployment chain, statistical authorization, and recursive continuation meet without identifying their loss scales.

Let qarch:Θ→𝖰archq_{\rm arch}:\Theta\to\mathsf{Q}_{\rm arch} be an architecture-action color. It may record feasibility, a witness class, or a repair permission, but it must distinguish worlds requiring different terminal deployments. Let CtC_{t} be an anytime confidence world for the same population model. Apply the raw and retained characteristic-information definitions of Chapter 20 to this color, and denote the resulting characteristic times by

TXarch,∗​(θ)andTZarch,∗​(θ).T_{X}^{\rm arch,*}(\theta)\quad\text{and}\quad T_{Z}^{\rm arch,*}(\theta).

For recursive control, color each reachable retained-evidence state uu by

ζ⁡(u)=(cdep​(u),ccert​(u),cctx​(u)),\zeta(u)=\bigl(c_{\rm dep}(u),c_{\rm cert}(u),c_{\rm ctx}(u)\bigr), (21.1)

where the entries record the deployment output, certificate permission, and sound contextual equivalence class. Applying the labeled-kernel refinement of Section 20.4 to ζ\zeta gives a stable joint quotient; write NjointN_{\rm joint} for its number of classes.

Theorem 21.2 (Typed architecture realization interface).

Under the preceding conditions, the evidence and recursive branches impose the following necessary bounds. The confidence-world conclusion is a separate conditional interface.

  1. 1.

    Every α\alpha-worldwise-valid system that resolves qarchq_{\rm arch} from retained evidence has expected stopping time satisfying

    𝔼θ​τ≥TZarch,∗​(θ)​kl⁡(1−α,α).\mathbb{E}_{\theta}\tau\geq T_{Z}^{\rm arch,*}(\theta)\operatorname{kl}(1-\alpha,\alpha). (21.2)

    Evidence processing gives TZarch,∗≥TXarch,∗T_{Z}^{\rm arch,*}\geq T_{X}^{\rm arch,*}, with equality exactly under the certificate-slack criterion for the binding opposite-action worlds.

  2. 2.

    Every exact shared recursive carrier preserving ζ\zeta and every observation-labeled update has at least NjointN_{\rm joint} reachable states. If each of LL charts distinguishes at most KK states, then

    L≥⌈NjointK⌉.L\geq\left\lceil\frac{N_{\rm joint}}{K}\right\rceil. (21.3)
  3. 3.

    For an adapted, measurable terminal selector AτA_{\tau}, the declared confidence-world authorization gate is the common-witness condition

    Aτ∈⋂λ∈Cτ𝔉Rη​(λ).A_{\tau}\in\bigcap_{\lambda\in C_{\tau}}\mathfrak{F}_{R}^{\eta}(\lambda). (21.4)

    If this gate is verified, then on the simultaneous coverage event the witness satisfies the declared tolerance in the true world. Items 1 and 2 do not imply the gate.

  4. 4.

    Conditional on the same common-witness gate, resource capacity and native loss remain governed by the carrier–decoder decomposition of Chapter 16; a claimed operational consequence follows only through the transmission and exposure gates of Chapter 17.

For the positive composition direction, an anytime-valid retained-evidence certificate, an exact joint recursive carrier, an adapted witnessed common deployment, and the declared native and contextual gates compose into an anytime-valid common certified action.

21.2.1 Radical instance: a genuine common witness

The radical loop makes the common-witness quantifier concrete. Let CtC_{t} be any confidence world of continuous target loops zλ:S1→ℂz_{\lambda}:S^{1}\to\mathbb{C} satisfying

infλ∈Ctinfθ∈S1|zλ​(θ)|≥ρ>0.\inf_{\lambda\in C_{t}}\inf_{\theta\in S^{1}}|z_{\lambda}(\theta)|\geq\rho>0.

Freeze the repaired operating contract before the terminal decision: the deployed input contains u=zλ​(θ)u=z_{\lambda}(\theta), or a carrier from which uu is exactly recoverable, and the native defect of a point output is

Du​(a)=|ak−u|2.D_{u}(a)=|a^{k}-u|^{2}.

For a symmetric task, the full-root rule

Wk​(u)={a∈ℂ:ak=u}W_{k}(u)=\{a\in\mathbb{C}:a^{k}=u\}

is one world-independent set-valued architecture. If its loss is the largest native defect of a returned element, write 𝔉set0​(λ)\mathfrak{F}_{\mathrm{set}}^{0}(\lambda) for the zero-tolerance feasible set under this repaired grammar. Then

Wk∈⋂λ∈Ct𝔉set0​(λ).W_{k}\in\bigcap_{\lambda\in C_{t}}\mathfrak{F}_{\mathrm{set}}^{0}(\lambda).

If a local point representative is required, cover ℂ∖{0}\mathbb{C}\setminus\{0\} by the two slit domains

U0=ℂ∖(−∞,0],U1=ℂ∖[0,∞).U_{0}=\mathbb{C}\setminus(-\infty,0],\qquad U_{1}=\mathbb{C}\setminus[0,\infty).

Each domain has a continuous logarithm and hence a local root ψj​(u)=exp⁡{Logj⁡(u)/k}\psi_{j}(u)=\exp\{\operatorname{Log}_{j}(u)/k\}. A fixed measurable router chooses an available domain and retains its chart label. The resulting two-chart rule Aatl​(u)=(j⁡(u),ψj⁡(u)​(u))A_{\mathrm{atl}}(u)=\bigl(j(u),\psi_{j(u)}(u)\bigr) is again independent of λ\lambda. Writing 𝔉atl0​(λ)\mathfrak{F}_{\mathrm{atl}}^{0}(\lambda) for the corresponding zero-tolerance feasible set,

Aatl∈⋂λ∈Ct𝔉atl0​(λ).A_{\mathrm{atl}}\in\bigcap_{\lambda\in C_{t}}\mathfrak{F}_{\mathrm{atl}}^{0}(\lambda).

Thus the confidence world need not collapse to a singleton before either repaired grammar has an actual common witness. Degree identification still decides whether the original θ\theta-indexed one-chart baseline is ruled out. It does not, by itself, exhibit a common one-chart root: even if every compatible loop has degree divisible by kk, their worldwise root fields may be different.

This construction does not silently solve the original contract of Theorem 14.1. If the deployed input is only θ\theta and does not expose zλ​(θ)z_{\lambda}(\theta), neither rule above is admissible. If the task requires one globally labeled root, the set-valued rule changes the output semantics and the atlas rule changes the routing grammar. In that case one must instead shrink CtC_{t} and exhibit a single admissible θ↦a⁡(θ)\theta\mapsto a(\theta) in the intersection. The distinction is exactly the difference between a mechanism-matched repair and a world-specific oracle family disguised as one deployment.

This interface closes the statistical upgrade of the architecture theory. Chapter 22 turns the first failed gate into a typed return path for data acquisition, evidence repair, state refinement, deployment expansion, or contextual revision.

21.3 Finite-library comparison and data-dependent selection

A finite-library version.

Suppose calibration data choose a finite candidate library

ℒ={𝔄(1),…,𝔄(K)},\mathcal{L}=\{\mathfrak{A}^{(1)},\ldots,\mathfrak{A}^{(K)}\},

from which one trained architecture A^\widehat{A} is selected without using the test sample. Fix MM predeclared baselines A1,…,AMA_{1},\ldots,A_{M}, also without inspecting the test sample. Let the test-unit loss lie in [0,B][0,B]. For b=1,…,Mb=1,\ldots,M define

Δ^b=1nte​∑i=1nte{ℓ⁡(Ab,Zi)−ℓ⁡(A^,Zi)}.\widehat{\Delta}_{b}=\frac{1}{n_{\rm te}}\sum_{i=1}^{n_{\rm te}}\{\ell(A_{b};Z_{i})-\ell(\widehat{A};Z_{i})\}.

Hoeffding’s inequality and a union bound give, with probability at least 1−δ1-\delta, simultaneously for all b=1,…,Mb=1,\ldots,M,

Δb≥Δ^b−B​2​log⁡(M/δ)nte\Delta_{b}\geq\widehat{\Delta}_{b}-B\sqrt{\frac{2\log(M/\delta)}{n_{\rm te}}}

for the stated range convention.

Theorem 21.3 (Finite-library held-out improvement).

With probability at least 1−δ1-\delta, simultaneously for every b=1,…,Mb=1,\ldots,M,

Δb≥Δ^b−B​2​log⁡(M/δ)nte.\Delta_{b}\geq\widehat{\Delta}_{b}-B\sqrt{\frac{2\log(M/\delta)}{n_{\rm te}}}.

Consequently, on that event, if

minb⁡Δ^b>B​2​log⁡(M/δ)nte,\min_{b}\widehat{\Delta}_{b}>B\sqrt{\frac{2\log(M/\delta)}{n_{\rm te}}},

then Δb>0\Delta_{b}>0 for every baseline, so the selected architecture has smaller population loss than every predeclared baseline.

The independent unit is the biological sample, task, or trajectory, not the individual cell or time point when those observations are dependent within units.

Architecture certificate plus held-out gain.

A convincing OALI conclusion combines two statements.

Structural statement.

Calibration data yield

𝔒¯​(𝔄0)>0\underline{\mathfrak{O}}(\mathfrak{A}_{0})>0

for the baseline architecture and a small upper witness for the repair.

Predictive statement.

Independent test data show lower operational loss for the repair.

Either statement alone is weaker. A held-out gain without a certificate may be generic architecture search. A certificate without held-out gain may be operationally irrelevant.

Data-dependent classes.

If the same data define the atlas and fit the experts, uniform fixed-class theory is insufficient. Three routes are available.

  1. 1.

    Sample splitting. Simple, transparent, but less data efficient.

  2. 2.

    Finite-library conditioning. Condition on calibration output and validate a predeclared finite set.

  3. 3.

    Random-set complexity. Bound generalization of the data-dependent set of architectures or optimizer trajectories.

PAC–Bayesian bounds for random hypothesis sets provide one general route to the third option (Dupuis et al., 2024). The current OALI program uses the first two routes. A theorem specialized to learned atlases and their structural certificates remains open.

Certification-aware architecture selection.

Ordinary model selection minimizes estimated predictive risk. Certification-aware selection uses a two-dimensional criterion:

(held-out risk,unresolved obstruction interval).\bigl(\text{held-out risk},\text{unresolved obstruction interval}\bigr).

An architecture with slightly lower empirical loss but an unresolved or unstable certificate may be less scientifically auditable than a robustly certified alternative.

21.4 Confidence, stopping, and the learning-theory frontier

Structural and operational confidence.

A population obstruction can be positive but hidden from the chosen task. Conversely, a small native defect can be amplified by a sensitive downstream decision. A complete confidence statement may therefore bracket both native and observable frontiers.

The deterministic nonexpansiveness of task envelopes allows one confidence event to propagate to the operational audit when kernel errors are controlled.

Stopping rules for architecture research.

Certificate statistics suggests a principled stopping rule. Continue data collection while the confidence world contains both:

  • •

    a world where the baseline is saturated; and

  • •

    a world where the baseline has a practically meaningful obstruction.

Stop when the certificate becomes decisive or when the cost of resolution exceeds the value of the architecture decision.

What would constitute a new learning theory.

A mature structural learning theory would provide:

  1. 1.

    objective-native architecture lower bounds;

  2. 2.

    resource-indexed upper witnesses;

  3. 3.

    honest finite-data transport;

  4. 4.

    data-dependent generalization;

  5. 5.

    optimization residual certificates;

  6. 6.

    task-relative operational interpretation;

  7. 7.

    automated, mechanism-specific repair.

The current program closes several of these interfaces in finite, convex, graph, and singular normal forms. It does not yet supply one universal theorem for arbitrary deep networks.

Appendix to Chapter 21: complete proofs

Proof of typed no-compensation

Dependencies. The evidence branch is a finite adaptive experiment with a parameter-independent retained channel. The recursive branch uses the finite labeled-kernel refinement of Chapter 20. The deployment branch has positive mass on the colliding inputs, a common compact action space, and finite lower-semicontinuous native defects whose zero sets are their distinct oracle actions.

Proof.

For evidence blindness, fix opposite-label worlds θ\theta and λ\lambda with Qθ,e=Qλ,eQ_{\theta,e}=Q_{\lambda,e} for every experiment. Induction on time shows that every retained transcript has the same law in the two worlds: conditional on a common transcript, a nonanticipating rule chooses the same distribution over experiments, and the next retained observation has the same conditional law. The conclusion remains true at a stopping time. If AA is the event that the rule reports q⁡(θ)q(\theta), almost-sure stopping and worldwise correctness would require

ℙθ​(A)≥1−α,ℙλ​(A)≤α.\mathbb{P}_{\theta}(A)\geq 1-\alpha,\qquad\mathbb{P}_{\lambda}(A)\leq\alpha.

Equality of transcript laws makes the two probabilities equal, contradicting α<1/2\alpha<1/2.

For a recursive collision, let bb and b′b^{\prime} be merged by ϕrec\phi_{\rm rec} but separated by the stable relation ∼∞\sim_{\infty} of Theorem 20.5. Because the reachable set is finite, the refinement stabilizes after finitely many steps, so there is a least hh with b≁hb′b\not\sim_{h}b^{\prime}. If h=0h=0, their declared colors differ. Otherwise they agree through depth h−1h-1, but some experiment, observation label, and ∼h−1\sim_{h-1} successor block has different probability from the two beliefs. This is a finite future context with different reduced laws. A decoder receiving the same recurrent state cannot reproduce both laws.

For a deployment collision, every decoder dd satisfies

d⁡{Hdep​(x)}=d⁡{Hdep​(x′)}.d\{H_{\rm dep}(x)\}=d\{H_{\rm dep}(x^{\prime})\}.

Write px,px′>0p_{x},p_{x^{\prime}}>0 for the two input masses and define, on the common action space,

δx,x′=mina⁡{px​𝖣x​(a)+px′​𝖣x′​(a)}.\delta_{x,x^{\prime}}=\min_{a}\{p_{x}\mathsf{D}_{x}(a)+p_{x^{\prime}}\mathsf{D}_{x^{\prime}}(a)\}.

The minimum is attained by compactness and lower semicontinuity. If it were zero, nonnegativity would force one action to have zero defect at both inputs, hence to equal both distinct oracle actions. Therefore δx,x′>0\delta_{x,x^{\prime}}>0, and every decoder on the collided carrier has expected native defect at least this margin. This conclusion is unchanged if the evidence carrier is the identity and the recursive state retains the full belief.

In each construction, choose identity carriers on the other two branches. Conversely, finite product components can place any one collision beside exact versions of the other interfaces. Thus exactness of either remaining branch cannot compensate for the failed one, and the three predicates are pairwise logically independent. ∎

Proof of the typed architecture realization interface

Dependencies. The architecture action color is a specialization of the truth map in Chapter 20; the joint color uses the same finite labeled-kernel refinement. The terminal deployment statement uses the single time-uniform confidence event of Chapter 19; the stopping time is adapted and the terminal architecture is an ℱτ\mathcal{F}_{\tau}-measurable selector in the declared resource class. Membership in the displayed common-witness intersection is a separate authorization hypothesis, not a consequence of worldwise color resolution or recursive-state preservation. The native and contextual conclusions retain their original contracts. No joint resource-budget conclusion or color-to-action factorization is inferred. If statistical components are constructed separately, their error budgets are combined by a union bound before this common event is invoked.

Proof.

Use q=qarchq=q_{\rm arch} in Theorem 20.3. Because the terminal rule is worldwise valid under the retained laws, that theorem gives (21.2) with TZarch,∗T_{Z}^{\rm arch,*}. Applying data processing and Theorem 20.4 to the same opposite-action partition gives TZarch,∗≥TXarch,∗T_{Z}^{\rm arch,*}\geq T_{X}^{\rm arch,*} and its equality criterion.

Now use ζ\zeta as the contract color in Theorem 20.5. Its stable quotient is the joint quotient by definition, so the universal refinement property gives at least NjointN_{\rm joint} states; counting chart–state pairs gives (21.3).

For the conditional deployment branch, assume the terminal selector passes the authorization gate (21.4). On the time-uniform coverage event, the true world belongs to CtC_{t} for every tt, hence to CτC_{\tau} at the adapted stopping time. Measurability of the selector makes AτA_{\tau} a legitimate terminal action, and membership in (21.4) places AτA_{\tau} in the true world’s feasible set. This is exactly the common- deployment implication of Theorem 19.6. The carrier–decoder decomposition then evaluates the witness in the declared native loss scale, and the transmission and exposure gates determine which part is visible under the declared contextual contract. Thus simultaneous passage of the evidence, recursive, common-witness, native, and contextual gates produces the claimed common certified action on the coverage event, whose complement has probability at most α\alpha. ∎

Proof of finite-library held-out improvement

Dependencies. The candidate architectures and baselines must be fixed before the independent test sample is inspected. The independent units, not lower-level observations nested inside them, are the concentration units. The loss difference must be bounded in an interval of length 2​B2B.

Proof.

For baseline bb, let

Xi(b)=ℓ⁡{Ab;Zi}−ℓ⁡{A^;Zi},−B≤Xi(b)≤B,X_{i}^{(b)}=\ell\{A_{b};Z_{i}\}-\ell\{\widehat{A};Z_{i}\},\qquad-B\leq X_{i}^{(b)}\leq B,

and write

Δ^b=1nte​∑i=1nteXi(b),Δb=𝔼​Xi(b).\widehat{\Delta}_{b}=\frac{1}{n_{\rm te}}\sum_{i=1}^{n_{\rm te}}X_{i}^{(b)},\qquad\Delta_{b}=\mathbb{E}X_{i}^{(b)}.

Hoeffding’s inequality for a variable with range length 2​B2B gives

ℙ{Δb<Δ^b−t}≤exp(−nte​t22​B2).\mathbb{P}\{\Delta_{b}<\widehat{\Delta}_{b}-t\}\leq\exp\left(-\frac{n_{\rm te}t^{2}}{2B^{2}}\right).

Set

t=B​2​log⁡(M/δ)nte.t=B\sqrt{\frac{2\log(M/\delta)}{n_{\rm te}}}.

The right-hand side becomes δ/M\delta/M. A union bound over the MM predeclared baselines yields, with probability at least 1−δ1-\delta,

Δb≥Δ^b−B​2​log⁡(M/δ)ntefor every ​b.\Delta_{b}\geq\widehat{\Delta}_{b}-B\sqrt{\frac{2\log(M/\delta)}{n_{\rm te}}}\qquad\text{for every }b.

If the smallest empirical improvement exceeds the common tolerance, every population improvement is positive. ∎

Chapter 22 Obstruction-Aware Learning and Inference

The preceding chapters separate population structure from finite-sample evidence. Obstruction-Aware Learning and Inference (OALI) is proposed as a falsifiable experimental and audit protocol, not as an established general architecture-selection theory. Its premise is deliberately restrictive: a structural repair should be attempted only after a baseline deployment contract has been declared, a mechanism-specific obstruction has been diagnosed, and the available data support a certificate strong enough to justify changing that contract.

22.1 From diagnosis to controlled intervention

The basic workflow is

local oracle estimation→structural audit→certificate→mechanism-matched repair→training→independent validation\boxed{\begin{gathered}\text{local oracle estimation}\to\text{structural audit}\to\text{certificate}\\ \to\text{mechanism-matched repair}\to\text{training}\to\text{independent validation}\end{gathered}}

Before fitting the repaired system, one declares:

  • •

    the local objective and native defect;

  • •

    the baseline deployment class and output semantics;

  • •

    the population aggregation and statistical unit;

  • •

    the resource and regularity constraints;

  • •

    the downstream endpoint and independent validation protocol.

The local oracle stage estimates the relevant fiber, branch multiplicity, and uncertainty. Related work on amortized inference separates per-instance optimization from the limitations of a shared inference mechanism (Cremer et al., 2018; Margossian and Blei, 2024; Marino et al., 2018). OALI uses a more restrictive intervention rule: it changes the deployment contract only after the failure has been typed and certified. Some gaps therefore call for better local optimization rather than structural repair.

The structural audit then determines how local oracle objects correspond across inputs: through point distances, permutations, partial bijections, quotient relations, or set-valued correspondences. Only after this representation has been stabilized does the procedure compute a structural certificate such as a transport lower bound, a coordination obstruction, a cycle holonomy, a resource lower bound, or a three-way feasible/impossible/unresolved certificate.

The distinction between OALI and OAI is operational. OALI is the general workflow above. OAI is a concrete instance designed for multibranch oracle families, using partial transport, cycle consistency, and atlas construction.

22.2 The repair must match the diagnosed mechanism

A positive certificate does not by itself say “use a larger model.” The diagnosed mechanism determines which part of the deployment contract should change.

The design principle is minimal intervention. Change only the interface named by the certificate whenever possible, while keeping parameter count, computation, training protocol, and data usage comparable to the original baseline. This makes it possible to distinguish a structural repair from a generic increase in flexibility.

A repaired class can still be implemented badly. Atlas experts can collapse onto the same branch; a quotient decoder can reintroduce an arbitrary canonicalization; a gate can use information unavailable at deployment. Training diagnostics should therefore retain the structural audit and report, as applicable, chart occupancy, within-chart native defect, transport consistency, gate stability, resource use, and numerical residuals.

22.3 A falsifiable saturation–repair–validation chain

Training saturation is not an architecture theorem and is not implied by a positive certificate. Misspecification, optimization failure, data scarcity, regularization, or an insensitive metric can all produce plateaus. A stronger structural interpretation requires the following sequence.

  1. 1.

    A calibration-stage certificate predicts a positive obstruction under a fixed deployment contract.

  2. 2.

    Increasing capacity, sample size, or optimization effort without changing that contract does not remove the diagnosed native gap once those ordinary errors have been controlled.

  3. 3.

    A minimal mechanism-matched change reduces the obstruction or native defect in the direction predicted by the theory.

  4. 4.

    On independent statistical units, the repaired system improves the predeclared endpoint relative to parameter- and compute-matched baselines.

  5. 5.

    Random partitions, generic mixtures, or other negative controls do not stably reproduce the improvement; in no-obstruction controls the structural procedure does not trigger unnecessary complexity.

This sequence is intentionally falsifiable. Failure of any step prevents the full architecture-choice conclusion, although earlier steps may retain their narrower meaning. No experiment in the present edition completes all five steps; the sequence is a proposed validation standard for future work.

Laboratory 24.2.1 illustrates only the certificate and repair-comparison stages for amortized variational inference. Its data, width, and training-effort curves continue to improve at their tested endpoints and therefore do not establish saturation. Its Monte Carlo reference and evaluation draws are reused, and it lacks compute-matched and negative-control repairs. It consequently does not validate the complete chain or justify a general architecture choice. Its endpoint is the sampled native variational objective, not a downstream classification benefit.

22.4 When a certificate implies population improvement

The final comparison requires a common loss scale. Suppose the baseline class has a certified lower bound O^\widehat{O} relative to the local oracle, the repaired system has oracle and implementation error at most ϵrep\epsilon_{\rm rep}, and the required finite-sample tolerances sum to Δ\Delta.

Theorem 22.1 (Population improvement template).

Under the stated certificate event, the population improvement of the repaired system over the baseline architecture class is at least

O^−ϵrep−Δ.\widehat{O}-\epsilon_{\rm rep}-\Delta.

In particular, the improvement is strictly positive whenever the right-hand side is positive.

The theorem also fixes the role of independent validation. OALI is not identified by the use of experts, charts, or routing; those devices are common architectural choices. Its distinguishing claim is conditional: a declared baseline contract is first shown to have a typed structural failure, and the repair is selected because it targets that failure. Capacity-matched random partitions, wider single models, additional test-time computation, and alternative repairs are therefore required controls rather than optional ablations.

Let Rbase⋆=infA∈𝔄baseR⁡(A)R_{\rm base}^{\star}=\inf_{A\in\mathfrak{A}_{\rm base}}R(A) and let RoracleR_{\rm oracle} be the local-oracle risk. The certified baseline event states

Rbase⋆−Roracle≥O^.R_{\rm base}^{\star}-R_{\rm oracle}\geq\widehat{O}.
